The existence of small defining polynomials for number fields

We prove that every number field of degree $n$ and absolute discriminant $D$ has a defining integral polynomial of degree $n$ whose coefficients are all $O_n(\sqrt D)$ in size, thus resolving a 1998 conjecture of Ruppert.
 Our proof compares ideal lattices with their trace duals, via which we handle all number fields with the exception of CM fields whose maximal totally real subfields have small discriminant. We then treat the remaining fields by averaging completed Epstein zeta functions over all possible ideal classes and archimedean scalings, for which we make critical use of Hecke's formula and the subconvexity theorem of Michel and~Venkatesh.
 Our proof does not use the Quasi-Riemann Hypothesis.
The $\mathrm{U}$-Derivative Associated with Linear Recurrence Sequences

We associate a canonical operator to every linear recurrence sequence admitting a distinct-root Binet representation \(\mathrm{U}_n=\sum_{j=1}^{k}A_jλ_j^n.\) The construction is based on the spectral Binet operator \(\mathcal{B}_\mathrm{U}=\sum_{j=1}^{k}A_jT_{λ_j}, \) where \(T_{λ_j}f(x)=f(λ_jx)\) is the dilation operator associated with the characteristic root \(λ_j\). The corresponding recurrence derivative is defined by \(\mathrm{D}_\mathrm{U}=x^{-1}\mathcal{B}_\mathrm{U}.\) Its fundamental property is the monomial identity \(\mathrm{D}_\mathrm{U}(x^n)=\mathrm{U}_nx^{n-1},\) which establishes a direct correspondence between recurrence sequences and degree-lowering operators. We develop the operator theory of \(\mathrm{D}_\mathrm{U}\), including iteration, a spectral product rule, the associated Leibniz defect, and a quotient rule. The construction reveals a natural bifurcation determined by the value \(\mathrm{U}_0\), producing the Ward and non-Ward regimes as intrinsic operatorial phenomena. The product structure is shown to be governed by \(k-2\) residual spectral channels, leading to notions of spectral cancellation and spectral balance. As an application, we obtain a complete qualitative classification of second-order recurrence calculi. Using Horadam sequences as a universal second-order model, we prove that every such calculus is determined by the invariant triple \((\mathrm{W}_0,Δ, Z_\mathrm{W}),\) where \(\mathrm{W}_0\) identifies the Ward/non-Ward type, \(Δ\) determines the spectral geometry, and \(Z_\mathrm{W}\) determines regularity or singularity.
Supercritical sharpness for Ising double random currents
Trishen S. Gunaratnam; Christoforos Panagiotis; Romain Panis; Franco Severo

We show that the percolation model induced by the double random current representation of the Ising model on $\mathbb Z^d$, with $d\geq 3$, satisfies local uniqueness of the macroscopic cluster with high probability for every $β>β_c$, uniformly in boundary conditions (i.e. sources). Such a result is sometimes called supercritical sharpness in percolation theory and yields a detailed description of the model via standard renormalisation techniques. As applications, we show the exponential decay of truncated correlations for the Ising model and exponential mixing for the FK-Ising measure, results previously obtained by Duminil-Copin, Goswami and Raoufi. However, our proof is considerably simpler, as it replaces the use of a highly technical multi-valued map principle with a simple sprinkling argument.
We show that any Serrin domain in $\mathbb{R}^2$ with two boundary components is a member of the canonical unduloidal family
Francesco Di Braccio; Simon Griffiths; Pedram Noohi; Leo Versteegen

Given a sequence $\mathbf{a}=(a_i)_{i\geq 1}$ of positive real numbers, we say that a colouring $c:E(K_n)\to \mathbb{N}$ is $\mathbf{a}$-bounded if the proportion of edges coloured $i$ is at most $a_i$, for all $i$. We write
 \[
 \mathbf{a}\, \to\, K_k
 \]
 if, for all sufficiently large $n$, all $\mathbf{a}$-bounded colourings $c:E(K_n)\to \mathbb{N}$ contain a monochromatic $K_k$. We say that the sequence $\mathbf{a}$ is \emph{Decay-Ramsey} if $\mathbf{a}\to K_k$ for all $k\ge 2$. In this short paper we introduce the question of determining which sequences are Decay-Ramsey and present some initial results.
Arithmetic Siegel--Weil formula on the product of modular curves

We prove the full generating series arithmetic Siegel--Weil formula on the product of two modular curves, with arbitrarily singular coefficients. This is the case $\operatorname{GSpin}(2,2)$ in Kudla's program.
Every Gromov elliptic domain is meromorphically pseudoconvex

We prove that every Gromov elliptic domain $Ω$ in a complex manifold has the following property, which we call meromorphic pseudoconvexity: each boundary point has a neighborhood $V$ such that $Ω\cap V$ becomes Stein after removing a set which is, locally in $Ω\cap V$, the union of the polar sets of finitely many meromorphic functions on $Ω\cap V$. Since meromorphic functions on Hartogs figures extend to their hulls, it follows that, for a domain $Ω=\operatorname{int}\overlineΩ$ in a Stein manifold, Gromov ellipticity is equivalent to being Oka and Stein, and also to being Oka and admitting a complete Kähler metric. This complements a theorem of Matsumura and the author that every weakly pseudoconvex Oka manifold admitting a positive line bundle is elliptic. As applications, we show that the Oka manifolds $\mathbb C^n\setminus\overline{\mathbb B^n}$ and $\mathbb C^n\setminus\mathbb R^n$, $n\geq2$, are not elliptic, and that no proper domain with Lipschitz boundary in $\mathbb P^n$, $n\geq2$, is elliptic.
Droplets obstruct Onsager-type solutions of the Ising model in a magnetic field

Onsager solved the two-dimensional Ising model in zero field, but no solution is known in a magnetic field. We prove that in any dimension $d\ge2$, at every fixed dimensionless field outside a countable set, the free energy obeys no algebraic differential equation in the coupling, even locally. The obstruction arises from droplet geometry: the maximal droplet volume grows as the $d/(d-1)$ power of its boundary size, while an integer band in the pressure coefficients protects the extremal contributions against cancellation. Our result excludes Onsager-type solutions and closed forms in elliptic, hypergeometric, or Painlevé functions of the coupling at these fields.
Complex generalized spin-c Killing spinors in low dimensions
José Luis Carmona Jiménez; Alejandro Gil-García; C. S. Shahbazi

We classify all complex generalized spin-c Killing spinors with complex Killing function $iμ-α$ on complete Riemannian surfaces, presenting an explicit list of all possible cases. We show that, contrary to previous statements in the literature, there exist complex generalized spin-c Killing spinors on Riemannian surfaces for which $αμ\not\equiv0$. We illustrate the classification by providing several explicit local, compact, and complete examples, including a complete example for which $αμ>0$ everywhere. We then move to three dimensions, proving that a spin-c Riemannian three-manifold admits a complex generalized spin-c Killing spinor with complex Killing function $iμ-α$ if and only if it is a $μ$-exact trans-Sasakian manifold of type $(α,μ)$. In addition, we construct a geodesically incomplete Riemannian three-manifold equipped with a complex generalized spin-c Killing spinor for which neither $μ$ nor $α$ vanishes identically, and then prove that this is not possible if the characteristic vector field of the associated trans-Sasakian structure is complete. These results settle a conjecture by Große and Nakad (Results in Mathematics, 2015) stating that on two- and three-dimensional Riemannian manifolds the complex Killing function of any complex generalized spin-c Killing spinor must be either globally real or globally imaginary.
We prove that completely parabolic translation surfaces are Veech, answering a question of Smillie-Weiss.

We introduce invariants we call $k$-divisibility and $d$-dominance, which are combinatorial constraints on the minimal generators of monomial ideals. We then prove that $k$ (respectively, $d$) is an upper bound (respectively, lower bound) for the projective dimension of a $k$-divisible (respectively, $d$-dominant) monomial ideal. This leads us to an explicit minimal resolution of $k$-divisible, $d$-dominant ideals when $d=k-1$ via a Lyubeznik resolution. This framework allows us to prove a conjecture made by Alesandroni. Using these invariants, we also provide a characterization of monomial ideals whose minimal free resolution is attainable from the Taylor resolution by performing exactly one consecutive cancellation. We also prove that for all $q,k,d$ in the range $1\leq d<k \leq q-1$, there exist monomial ideals that are $k$-divisible and $d$-dominant with $q$ minimal generators.
Hypergraphs with the smallest Hall ratio are still hard to colour
Veronica Bitonti; Freddie Illingworth; Pedram Noohi; Jane Tan

For $H$ a hypergraph, the Hall ratio $ρ(H)=\text{max}_{X\subseteq V(H)}\frac{\lvert{X}\rvert}{α(H[X])}$ is a natural lower bound for its chromatic number, and among non-empty $k$-uniform hypergraphs the smallest possible Hall ratio is $k/(k-1)$. For graphs ($k = 2$), having minimum Hall ratio $2$ forces chromatic number $2$. Nešetřil, Rödl, and Sales asked whether a similar phenomenon holds at higher uniformities. We answer this question negatively in a strong form, showing that for every $k \geqslant 3$ there are $k$-uniform hypergraphs with Hall ratio exactly $k/(k-1)$ and arbitrarily large fractional chromatic number.
Proof of the Penrose Conjecture for Maximally Parameterized Initial Data Sets
Hubert Bray; Tuan Dolmen; Marcus Khuri; David Schmidt

We prove the spacetime Penrose inequality for asymptotically flat initial data sets $(M^n,g,k)$ in all dimensions $n\geq 3$, under the dominant energy condition, for data admitting the 'maximally parameterized form' defined in equation (4.7). In this case, the second fundamental form $k$ is locally parameterized by $n(n+1)/2$ functions, giving the same formal local functional degrees of freedom as an arbitrary symmetric $2$-tensor.
 The proof is based on a new 1-parameter family of generalized Schoen-Yau identities and their gauge-invariant specialization, inspired by the generalized Jang framework of Bray-Khuri [8, 9]. For maximally parameterized data, these identities produce a Riemannian comparison metric \[
 \bar g=g+β\otimesβ\] with nonnegative scalar curvature $R_{\bar{g}} \geq 0$. Under a natural nondegeneracy condition (5.7) at the apparent horizon, the comparison metric admits a smooth minimal completion up to $\partial M^n$. Together with suitable asymptotic control, this reduces the Penrose inequality to its Riemannian counterpart. The all-dimensional conclusion uses the Riemannian Penrose theorem of Bi-Zhu [6], together with a minimizing enclosure argument that allows singular boundaries.
 More generally, in the spirit of [8, 9], we note that the Penrose conjecture follows whenever a certain system of PDEs (3.18) involving $k$ can be solved, in which case our new identity (3.15) immediately implies $R_{\bar{g}} \geq 0$. A natural problem is thus to regularize our degenerate system to prove a general existence theory, thereby proving the Penrose conjecture. Essentially, we believe this is what the OpenAI paper [27] posted last week on October 6, 2026 claims to have done.
Minimal $\mathfrak{sl}_N$ Complexes of Rational Tangles via the Fukaya Category

We compute minimal $\mathfrak{sl}_N$ complexes for oriented rational tangles, denoted $[\![τ_{u/v}^{O}]\!]_N$, in terms of the topological Fukaya category of the $3$-punctured disk. This demonstrates that the complexes stabilize, allowing us to define a HOMFLY-PT homology for rational tangles.
The large sieve inequality and additive decompositions of sums of squares

Building on the large sieve, we prove a new sieve estimate for sets which are missing various residue classes modulo prime squares. For certain interesting residue class configurations, our bound is a significant improvement over the corresponding Johnsen-Selberg sieve inequality.
 Our application of this sieve estimate is motivated by Ostmann's problem. We study additive decompositions of sums of squares and show that any non-trivial sumset decomposition must consist of two sets of roughly equal size: If $A_1, A_2 \subseteq \mathbb{Z}$ with $A_1 + A_2 = \{x^2 + y^2 : x, y \in \mathbb{Z}\}$ and $|A_1|, |A_2| \geq 2$, then $\sqrt{x}/(\log x)^{9/2} \ll |A_i \cap [1, x]| \ll \sqrt{x}(\log x)^4$ for $i \in \{1, 2\}$.
The $k$-color poset Ramsey number of the diamond is $2k$
Tom Bohman; Will Cong; Quentin Dubroff; Teresa Huang; Zheyuan Li; BangTam Ngo

The $k$-color Ramsey number of a poset $P$ is the smallest dimension $d$ such that any $k$-coloring of the $d$-dimensional Boolean lattice contains a monochromatic induced copy of $P$. For $ j\ge 2$ the $j$-diamond is the poset that consists of a maximum element, a minimum element and an antichain of size $j$. We prove that the $k$-color Ramsey number of the $j$-diamond is at most $jk$. Colorings of the Boolean lattice that assign sets of the same size the same color provide matching lower bounds for $j \in \{2,3,4\}$.

Rockafellar showed that every cyclically monotone operator is contained in the subdifferential of a convex function, and characterized the maximal ones. We establish the quasi-convex analogue of this theorem, with no assumption on the operator: in any separable Banach space, a setting we show to be sharp, every cyclically quasi-monotone operator is contained in the normal cone operator of a quasi-convex function. In finite dimension, we characterize maximal cyclically quasi-monotone operators and show that they are maximal quasi-monotone. Unlike in the convex case, the potential is not unique, and we build it from a preference relation obtained through successive preorders. As applications, we extend Afriat's theorem on revealed preferences in economics to infinite data sets, and obtain Kantorovich-type potentials for a supremal optimal transport problem.
Fast separation of Euler and Navier--Stokes flows in two dimensions
Siming He; Yupei Huang; Jincheng Yang

We study the long-time validity of the inviscid limit problem by measuring when the two-dimensional ideal fluid ceases to accurately approximate a slightly viscous fluid with the same initial datum. We construct a stationary solution of the Euler equation from which the Navier--Stokes solution separates at a time scale proportional to the logarithm of the inverse viscosity, achieving the fastest separation from Euler steady states.
A Decomposition-Based Data-Driven Branch-and-Bound Approach for Black-Box Global Optimization

Many scientific and engineering applications require the global optimization of expensive black-box functions. In high-dimensional settings, however, achieving computational scalability is a major challenge. To address this challenge, we propose a distributed spatial branch-and-bound framework that exploits partially separable structure for the global optimization of box-constrained black-box problems. The proposed framework adopts a two-layer structure in which branching is performed only on a lower-dimensional set of coupling variables in an outer layer. Within each outer node, the remaining non-overlapping (private) variables, which appear independently across blocks, have their domains partitioned and explored in parallel within an inner layer, resulting in a naturally parallelizable framework that is well suited for implementation on multi-core CPU architectures. At each node, valid upper bounds are obtained via sampling, with optional refinement using a local solver, while lower bounds are computed using data-driven convex underestimators constructed over partitions of the private variables. A residual-based correction and finite-sample validity analysis provide conditions under which the partitionwise underestimators are valid lower bounds, while the proposed branching and refinement mechanism establishes convergence to an $ε$-global optimum. Numerical studies on benchmark and ODE-constrained parameter-estimation problems demonstrate improvements in both sampling efficiency and computational performance relative to monolithic approaches.

Let theta be an ordinary character or a Brauer character of a finite group N. We show that theta extends to every overgroup $G=G_θ\trianglerighteq N$ if and only if Z(N) <= Ker(theta) and the deflated character of Inn(N) extends to Aut(N)_theta. This equivalence is compatible with fields of values. A similar investigation for extensions from subnormal subgroups leads to a new characteristic subgroup of N.
Effective equidistribution of polynomial trajectories in $\operatorname{SL}_3(\mathbb R)/\operatorname{SL}_3(\mathbb Z)$

For a fixed matrix-polynomial trajectory in $\operatorname{SL}_3(\mathbb R)/\operatorname{SL}_3(\mathbb Z)$, we give a necessary and sufficient intrinsic Diophantine condition for its time averages to equidistribute at a power rate on its homogeneous orbit closure. The condition uses a lattice in the space of polynomial functions on the normalized orbit-closure group, each admitting a representative of total degree at most two in the matrix entries. These polynomial tests have a common degree bound of two, independent of the curve degree and optimal in general. The proof begins with a classification of the possible orbit-closure groups and derives lower bounds for polynomial coefficient vectors from the intrinsic condition. It combines quantitative nilmanifold equidistribution, unipotent tangent approximation, and effective flow estimates, with arithmetic separation and quantitative nondivergence controlling cusp excursions and periodic-orbit obstructions.
Claw-Free and Line Graph Edge Deletion on Block Graphs

Edge deletion problems ask for the fewest edges whose deletion gives a graph with a specified property. We study two such problems on block graphs. First making the graph claw-free, and second making it a line graph. Since every line graph is claw-free, the second problem is at least as difficult as the first. We show that on block graphs the two optimum values are always equal, and both are attained by the line graph of a forest. The main step is a completion argument, in which starting from any claw-free solution, we put back edges to get some nice structure inside each block still maintaining the claw-free property. This reduces both edge-deletion problems to the same problem of selecting vertices within the blocks of the input graph. We solve it by dynamic programming in $O(n+m)$ time, which also produces an optimal deletion set and a forest whose line graph is what remains after the completion argument. We also extend the method to $K_{1,r+1}$-free edge deletion for every fixed $r$.
On Meeks' conjecture on disjoint minimal graphs

We study disjoint solution pairs $(u,D)$ to the minimal surface equation in $\mathbb{R}^n$, with $u=0$ on $\partial D.$ A conjecture of W. Meeks states that at most two such pairs can exist in $\mathbb{R}^n.$ We confirm the conjecture in two complementary cases. For $n\in\{2,3,4,5,6\},$ we prove it under a superlinearity assumption. In dimension $n=2,$ we establish the result under a suitable sublinearity assumption. We also derive estimates on the asymptotic angle of domains supporting nontrivial solutions for $n\geq 3.$
Separation of variables for coupled radiative perturbations of Kerr-Newman-de Sitter black holes

We extend Hintz's separation of variables for radiative gravitational and electromagnetic perturbations from Kerr-Newman to Kerr-Newman-de Sitter black holes. On subextremal backgrounds with nonzero rotation and charge, an explicit algebraic matrix transformation yields coupled two-component radial and angular ordinary differential systems linked by a common separation constant. The transformation is independent of the frequency and azimuthal number and applies to both signs of spin weight. For real frequencies, we establish a complete angular mode decomposition. We also translate regularity at the future black hole outer and cosmological horizons into ingoing and outgoing boundary conditions, respectively, for the separated radial systems. These results show that exact separation of the coupled radiative equations extends beyond asymptotically flat Kerr-Newman spacetime.

We prove that every mod $k$ integral cycle $T$ of sufficiently high codimension in an oriented Riemannian manifold $\mathcal{M}$ can be approximated in flat norm by a cycle which is a $\mathbb{Z}_k$-smooth submanifold $Σ$ of nearly the same area, up to a singular set of codimension 5. If in addition $T$ belongs to a mod $k$ homology class admitting an embedded $\mathbb{Z}_k$-smooth manifold representative, then $Σ$ can be taken fully regular, up to the codimension one stratum of classical singularities. This extends the smooth approximation theory to cycles with coefficients in $\mathbb{Z}/k\mathbb{Z}$ in stable regimes. Moreover, we provide examples showing the impossibility of locally approximating minimizing cycles by smooth or $\mathbb{Z}_k$-smooth submanifolds, even in homology classes with smooth or $\mathbb{Z}_k$-smooth representatives.
Smoothness criterion for Fano orbifolds and bases of Lagrangian fibrations

We establish a smoothness criterion for Fano varieties with quotient singularities. As an application, we show that if $X\to B$ is a Lagrangian fibration from a compact hyper-Kähler manifold and $B$ has quotient singularities, then $B$ is a projective space.
Uniform $L^2$-bounds for the $n$-th Calderón commutator on Lipschitz graphs
Joan Hernández; Joan Mateu; Laura Prat

We prove that, for every real Lipschitz function $A$ and every integer $n\ge1$, $\|T_{A,n}\|_{L^2(\mathbb{R})\to L^2(\mathbb{R})}\le C\,\|A'\|_\infty^n$, where $T_{A,n}$ is the $n$-th Calderón commutator and $C$ is an absolute constant. The essential tool is the Coifman--McIntosh--Meyer theorem, applied to a holomorphic family of complex curves, together with the Cauchy integral formula on a contour surrounding the interval of secant slopes. We also include a simpler version of the argument that gives $O(\log n)$ and explains why the contour has the shape it has.
Cheng's Theorem in the Spectral Setting

We prove a maximal diameter rigidity theorem for closed 3-dimensional Riemannian manifolds under a spectral lower bound for the Ricci curvature. We show that if $0<γ<2$, $K>0$ and $λ_1(-γΔ+\operatorname{Ric})\geq 2K$, then the optimal bound $\operatorname{diam}(M,g)\leq\fracπ{\sqrt{K}}$ is attained if and only if (M,g) is isometric to the round 3-sphere of constant sectional curvature $K$.
Transference principles for divergence sets of dispersive equations and their applications

In this article, we study the fractal refinement of the Carleson's problem: (1) We introduce an equivalence relation on linear dispersive PDEs on $\mathbb{R}^{n}$ based on the high-frequency oscillation of their Fourier multipliers, proving that equations in the same class share the same Hausdorff dimension of divergence sets. As applications, we estimate these dimensions for abstract dispersive families. Consequently, we recover known $1$-dimensional results for linearized Boussinesq and Beam propagations, while establishing new results for both in higher dimensions and for Klein-Gordon propagations in all dimensions. (2) Next, we study the effect of radial symmetry by obtaining dimension estimates for fractional Schrödinger equations with concave phase and radial initial data. Applying a transference principle, dimension estimates are extended to families of abstract dispersive equations. As special cases, we recover the known result for the Beam propagation and also obtain new results for the linearized Boussinesq and the Klein-Gordon propagations in the radial setting. (3) We study analogues of (2) for the $3$-dimensional real hyperbolic space by obtaining dimension estimates for a wide class of dispersive propagations: the Schrödinger, fractional Schrödinger (with convex and concave phases), Beam, linearized Boussinesq, Wave and Klein-Gordon equations. This is the first result of its kind, outside the setting of flat Euclidean geometry. Our arguments are based on an inter-spatial transference principle of geometric-analytic flavour. In the process, we also obtain a quantitative result on the singular sets of Sobolev functions, in the spirit of Žubrinić, which may be of independent interest.
Crystallographic quotients of Artin braid groups and torus bundles over flat $3$-manifolds

For $n\geq3$, let $\overline B_n=B_n/[P_n,P_n]$ be the crystallographic quotient of the Artin braid group, with translation subgroup $\overline P_n=P_n/[P_n,P_n]\cong\mathbb Z^N$, where $N=\binom n2$. We prove that every compact connected flat $3$-manifold $M$, considered up to affine equivalence, is the base of a geometric torus bundle whose total space is a compact flat manifold with fundamental group a Bieberbach subgroup of some $\overline B_n$. More precisely, for every $n\geq n_M$, where $n_M\in\{3,4,5\}$ is an explicit optimal threshold depending on $M$, we construct a Bieberbach subgroup $Γ_n(M)\leq\overline B_n$ of dimension $N$ and a complete normal subgroup $K_n(M)\cong\mathbb Z^{N-3}$ consisting of translations such that $$ Γ_n(M)/K_n(M)\congπ_1(M). $$ We also determine which of the associated torus-bundle group extensions split: for the realizations constructed here, splitting occurs for exactly four of the ten affine-equivalence classes of compact flat $3$-manifolds.
An extension principle for Einstein-Maxwell-charged scalar field system with finite Doppler exponent
Xinliang An; Haoyang Chen; Taoran He

We prove a new extension principle for the spherically symmetric Einstein--Maxwell--charged scalar field system. Rather than imposing conditions for mass ratio $2m/r$ as in Christodoulou's small-mass-ratio criterion or as in An--Chen--Singh's proof [1] with $2m/r<3/8$, here we work through a proposal by An-Tan [2] with finite Doppler exponent (blueshift). By conducting two successive blow-up analyses, followed by a stationary comparison and a rigidity argument, we establish the uniform boundness of $α'$ with $α'=\partial_vα/\partial_vr$ and $α=\partial_v(rφ)/\partial_vr$. This provides the desired extension principle in An-Tan [2] and completes the picture of weak cosmic censorship developed therein.
 As we were about to release our preprint, Cicortas communicated to us that together with his collaborators, they concomitantly used a different approach to obtain the corresponding extension principle with finite blueshift (Doppler exponent) for the uncharged Einstein-scalar field system. Hence, we decided to put the current paper as an appendix to An-Tan [2], thereby completing the proof of the weak cosmic censorship for the Einstein-Maxwell-charged scalar field system. At the same time, we are working with Cicortas and his collaborators to write a new preprint containing both approaches for the Einstein-scalar field system.
A Scale-Critical $μ<\frac38$ Extension Principle for Spherically Symmetric Einstein-Scalar Field System
Xinliang An; Haoyang Chen; Jaydeep Singh

We present a new quantitative, scale-critical $C^1$ extension principle for the spherically symmetric Einstein--scalar field system. We derive estimates for solutions in the causal past of a possibly singular endpoint $\mathcal{O}$ of the center. Assume that there is no trapped surface in this region and assume that the Doppler exponent (blue shift) along each incoming null cone is uniformly bounded. We then prove that the solution can extend regularly across $\mathcal{O}$ provided the mass ratio $μ=2m/r$ satisfies $\supμ<\frac38$. This improves the small-mass-ratio condition in Christodoulou's extension principle by an explicit threshold of order one. Our proof has three new ingredients. First, we derive several new uniform scale-critical pointwise estimates for the scalar field and its derivatives. Second, we obtain refined estimates in an exterior self-similar domain within the triangular causal past region. Third, we establish a family of higher-order Morawetz-type identities and identify the ranges of $μ$, with which there are coercive spacetime estimates. The unweighted identity yields the threshold $μ\leq\frac14$, while employing extra self-similar weight raises the threshold to $μ<\frac38$ and provides a weighted control, which implies that the solution's BV norm along an outgoing null cone is small, so that Christodoulou's theory of bounded variation solutions gives the extension.

We study the category of constructible $p$-Kummer-étale sheaves on the log adic generic fiber $(\mathrm{X},\mathcal{M}_{\mathrm{D}})_η$ for the stratification induced by a horizontal normal crossings divisor $\mathrm{D}$, showing that it is antiequivalent to a category of finitely generated unit Laurent crystals on the log prismatic site. We give a local description of finitely generated unit crystals on a framed log affine in terms of $(\varphi,Γ)$-modules, and show pushforward compatibility for strict log smooth proper morphisms.
Topological recursion for spin enumeration of hypermaps
Alexander Alexandrov; Boris Bychkov; Petr Dunin-Barkowski; Maxim Kazarian; Sergey Shadrin

We establish topological recursion for the spin enumeration of hypermaps, or, in the dual language, spin dessins d'enfants. This problem has remarkable features distinguishing it from other applications of topological recursion to enumerative combinatorics. First, the spectral curve is elliptic rather than rational, as in most cases studied before. Second, it contains degenerate ramification points, and one has to apply a version of degenerate topological recursion. Finally, the meromorphic correlator differentials have "moving" poles on the antidiagonals between pairs of distinct arguments, and one has to adjust the loop equations to this kind of degeneracy as well.
 The computations involve concepts of different kinds, such as BKP integrability, Gaussian integrals, the x-y swap, and symplectic duality.
Allen--Cahn and mean curvature flows from Clifford hypersurfaces to equators

In this short note, using OpenAI's resolution of the Solomon--Yau conjecture, we extend our joint work with Pedro Gaspar to all dimensions $n\geq2$. We construct eternal Allen--Cahn flows on $S^{n+1}$ connecting approximations of any prescribed least-area Clifford hypersurface and equatorial sphere. We also construct infinitely many eternal integral Brakke flows from least-area Clifford hypersurfaces to equatorial spheres.
Universal norms of partially de Rham $B$-pairs and perfectness in Lubin--Tate Iwasawa theory

We study the behaviour of partially de Rham Selmer groups of $B$-pairs along abelian $p$-adic Lie extensions. In the cyclotomic case we compare them with the universal norms studied by Berger. For analytic Lubin--Tate $(\varphi,Γ)$-modules we prove that the $Ψ=1$ eigenspace is coadmissible of the expected rank over the algebra of analytic distributions and establish a comparison result between its Lie-algebra coinvariants and the projective limit of the partially de Rham Selmer groups of the attached $B$-pair.
Intersecting families of loose spanning hypertrees

A loose hypertree is a hypergraph whose incidence graph is a tree. Let $b\ge3$, $n\equiv1\pmod{b-1}$, and $s:=(n-1)/(b-1)$. We determine the largest $t$-intersecting families of loose spanning $b$-uniform hypertrees on $[n]$, simultaneously for every $1\le t\le s$, provided $n$ exceeds an explicit constant depending only on $b$. The extremal families consist of all such hypertrees containing a fixed $t$-edge loose forest whose component sizes are as equal as the divisibility condition permits. In particular, when $bt\le n$, the extremal forests are matchings. We also prove a Hilton--Milner-type bound: if $n\ge C_b(t+1)$, where $C_b$ depends only on $b$, every nontrivial $t$-intersecting family has at most $(s+1)r_{t+1}(n)$ members. Here $r_j(n)$ is the maximum possible number of loose spanning $b$-uniform hypertrees containing a fixed $j$-edge loose forest. For fixed constants $b,t$, this bound is asymptotically sharp and is $O_{b,t}(n^{2-b})r_t(n)$. The proofs combine exact forest enumeration with the intersection theorems of Kupavskii for spread families.
K-area bounds for smooth sphere bundles

Let $E\to B$ be a smooth $S^n$ bundle with oriented Riemannian total space $(E,g)$, where $n\ge2$. We prove K-area$(E,g)\le4πn(n-1)/σ$ whenever every fibre has intrinsic scalar curvature at least $σ>0$, independently of the dimension of $B$. In particular, unit round fibres give K-area$(E,g)\le4π$. For arbitrary metrics on two-sphere fibres, K-area is bounded by the supremum of their areas. We also obtain stronger bounds from fibrewise scalar spectra.
Entire solutions of higher order Briot-Bouquet equations
Alexandre Eremenko; Tuen Wai Ng; Teng Zhang

For a meromorphic function $f$ in the complex plane, we determine when $f$ and $f^{(k)}$ are algebraically dependent. This happens precisely when $f$ belongs to the class $W$ of elliptic functions and their degenerates, or satisfies a linear differential equation $f^{(k)} + af + b = 0$ with constant coefficients. The case of functions having a pole was settled previously. We complete the proof by treating entire solutions.

We investigate the notion of holomorphic $p$-contact structure, that we introduced recently in the scalar case with H. Kasuya and L. Ugarte and in the line-bundle case with K. Broder, in the context of a holomorphic family of compact complex manifolds equipped with a holomorphic family of holomorphic line bundles. Firstly, we show that the existence of a holomorphic $p$-contact structure is {\bf deformation-open} when a non-jumping assumption is made on the $\bar\partial$-cohomology of bidegree $(p,\,0)$. This ought to become a source of further examples of holomorphic $p$-contact manifolds. Secondly, we obtain a Berndtsson-type {\bf (semi-)positivity} result for the holomorphic vector bundle over the base induced, as a direct image, by the line bundle on the total space that supports the p-contact structures. Thirdly, we introduce a moduli space of relative holomorphic p-contact structures and we show that it is {\bf Hausdorff} and {\bf open} in a certain quotient topological space.
The classical homotopy category is cartesian closed

The category of all topological spaces and homotopy classes of maps is cartesian closed. In fact, the $(\infty, 1)$-category of all topological spaces and continuous maps, localised at homotopy equivalences, is cartesian closed. We model the exponential object using a topological space whose points are continuous maps equipped with putative neighbourhood filters. In general, this topological space will not even be $T_1$-separated, but the evaluation map induces a natural weak homotopy equivalence witnessing the universal property.
On the Complexity of Linear Programs with Parametric Constraint Matrices
Laurie Boveroux; Margarida Carvalho; Andrea Lodi; Quentin Louveaux

While sensitivity analysis for linear programs with parametric right- hand side vectors is well established, cases involving parametric constraint matrices remain less explored. To address this gap, we investigate linear programs where the constraint matrix depends linearly on a scalar parameter. Our goal is to compute the minimum and maximum optimal values of these parametric linear programs within a fixed parameter range. This corresponds to solving two bilevel programs. We show that both decision versions of these optimization problems are NP-complete by proving both NP-hardness and membership in NP. We additionally identify three sufficient conditions on the parametric matrix under which the bilevel programs are no longer NP-hard. We introduce a reformulation for both problems, together with a Farkas-based certificate for the lower-level feasibility condition, and compare the execution time for solving them on standard benchmark instances. The experiments highlight a practical dichotomy. Although both bilevel optimizations are NP-hard, computing the parameter value corresponding to the minimum of the linear program is fast, whereas computing the value corresponding to the maximum is not. We relate this asymmetry to the parametric equality constraints, whose free dual variables leave the relaxation of the maximum reformulation unbounded.
Intermittency for the parabolic Anderson model on spaces with sub-Gaussian heat kernel estimates
Fabrice Baudoin; Hongyi Chen; Li Chen; Søren Kjærsgaard

We study the parabolic Anderson model $\partial_t u=Δu+βu\,\dot W_α$ on an unbounded Ahlfors $d_h$-regular Dirichlet metric measure space whose heat kernel satisfies two-sided sub-Gaussian estimates with walk dimension $d_w$. The noise is white in time and, in space, either white ($α=0$) or colored through the Riesz kernel of $(-Δ)^{-2α}$, where $0\le 2α<d_h/d_w<1+2α$. No recurrence is assumed. We prove existence, uniqueness and Hölder regularity of the mild Skorohod solution for bounded initial conditions. For nonzero nonnegative bounded initial conditions, the solution is positive and its moment Lyapunov exponents exist for every real $p\ge1$, independently of the spatial point and the initial condition. For $p\ge2$, these exponents have order $p\,(β^2(p-1))^{d_w/((1+2α)d_w-d_h)}$, with upper and lower bounds matching up to constants.
Dual-Inertial Bregman Methods with Energy-Based Safeguarding

We develop a dual-inertial framework for convex optimization that introduces inertia in dual coordinates while retaining the Bregman proximal-type oracles. For unrestarted iterations, uniformly bounded positive directional variation gives a last-iterate $\cO((1+\log k)/k^2)$ rate, improving to $\cO(k^{-2})$ under additional weighted summability. A computable safeguarded algorithm gives a global $\cO(N^{-1})$ objective-gap bound for the best accepted point, where $N$ counts all proximal oracle calls. Under local strong-convexity and kernel regularity conditions, all three safeguarded methods restart finitely and attain a final-epoch last-iterate $\cO(N^{-2})$ rate. Numerical experiments compare objective accuracy and computational cost on entropy regression and nonnegative least squares. Comparative numerical experiments illustrate the performance advantages of the proposed methods.
Tracking a Small Set of Experts in Online Convex Optimization
Angelos Assos; Anand Brahmbhatt; Elad Hazan

For the fundamental problem of prediction from expert advice, Freund asked whether one could compete with a comparator that switches $k$ times among only $m$ experts. For a discrete set of experts, this problem was resolved by Bousquet and Warmuth (2020), who gave an efficient algorithm with optimal regret matching the information-theoretic limit.

An inefficient algorithm can be derived by discretizing the action space and applying the Bousquet--Warmuth algorithm, giving regret of $\widetilde{O}(md+k)$, while the best known efficient algorithm for this problem has regret $\widetilde{O}(dk)$. We show that this computational inefficiency is inherent, establishing a separation between the information-theoretic and polynomial-time regret achievable for this problem. Specifically, under the hypergraphic planted-clique conjecture, we show that for every polynomial-time algorithm there exist instances for which it incurs at least $(k\sqrt d)^{1-o(1)}$ regret.

Let $G$ be the terminal graph of the random triangle-removal process started from $K_n$. We prove that $e(G)/n^{3/2}\to1/(2\sqrt2)$ in $L^2$. More generally, we obtain the analogous result for any fixed strictly $k$-balanced $k$-graph. Our main tool is a more general theorem on random greedy matchings in nearly regular uniform hypergraphs with few short cycles under a stability assumption on the survival equations.
When Does Momentum Help in Reinforcement Learning with Verifiable Rewards?
Kaifei Wang; Zikang Shan; Liwei Wang; Yinyu Ye; Han Zhong

Momentum is a classical tool for accelerating convex optimization and a standard component of modern large language model training. Yet recent empirical work has questioned the usefulness of first-moment momentum in reinforcement learning with verifiable rewards (RLVR). We study this question through a bandit formulation of RLVR with bias-corrected exponential moving average (EMA) momentum, where the EMA coefficient $β$ controls how quickly the weights on past gradients decay. When policy gradients are evaluated exactly, we prove that increasing $β$ within a range that prevents overshoot strictly accelerates optimization. When gradients are estimated from sampled responses, a positive expected gain can be obscured by sampling fluctuations. We show that as the learning rate $η$ decreases, the expected gain with fixed $β$ vanishes faster than these fluctuations, whereas increasing $β$ to keep $η/(1-β)$ within the safe regime preserves a nonvanishing gain that eventually dominates them. Bandit simulations quantitatively validate these predictions. On Qwen2.5-32B with AdamW, simply increasing $β_1$ improves mean validation accuracy by nearly $2$ percentage points over the conventional choice, demonstrating the principle's effectiveness at a larger model scale.

The resetting of stochastic processes has become a key mechanism appearing in many research fields, such as searching for a target, the transmission control protocol, biology, chemistry, finance, insurance, etc., with the main interest concerning the first passage time (FPT) by the process under resetting. In this paper, we focus on the exit time $\mathcal{T}_L$ from the interval $(-L, L)$ of Lévy flights (LF) under resetting, but we also consider spectrally negative Lévy processes (SNLP). As the main result, we find the asymptotics of the mean first passage time (MFPT) as $L$ tends to $+ \infty$. For LF with $α\in (0, 2)$, the scaling behaves as $L^α$ regardless of the reset rate and the asymmetry of the initial condition, a behaviour completely different from that for the known case of Brownian Motion ($α=2$). For the symmetric $α$-stable case with $α\in (0, 2)$, we also found that taking $r \to \infty$ with fixed $L$ yields a finite MFPT, which therefore may be used as a valid approximation. For completely asymmetric stable processes, we show that the scaling is very different from that for LF, and point out a method to obtain the exact distribution of FPT under resetting. The analytical calculations are verified by numerical simulations of the processes under resetting.

A perfect 1-factorization of the complete graph $K_{2t}$ is a partition of its edges into perfect matchings such that the union of any two of them is a Hamilton cycle. Kotzig conjectured in 1963 that $K_{2t}$ has a perfect 1-factorization for every $t \ge 2$, but apart from some infinite families and a list of sporadic orders the conjecture is open, and $92$ was one of the nine orders up to $100$ for which no perfect 1-factorization was known. In this paper we construct two non-isomorphic perfect 1-factorizations of $K_{92}$.
Treewidth and the Product of Tree-Independence and Tree-Chromatic Numbers

For a graph $G$, let $\mathrm{tw}(G)$, $\mathrm{tree}\text{-}α(G)$, and $\mathrm{tree}\text{-}χ(G)$ denote its treewidth, tree-independence number, and tree-chromatic number, respectively. We prove that every nonempty graph $G$ satisfies $\mathrm{tw}(G)+1\leq\mathrm{tree}\text{-}α(G)\mathrm{tree}\text{-}χ(G)(1+\lfloor\log_2(\mathrm{tree}\text{-}α(G))\rfloor)$. This improves the quadratic bound of Koutsoutis, Krause, Liu, Redzic, and Ueckerdt. For every pair of integers $n,k\geq2$, we construct a graph $G$ with $\mathrm{tree}\text{-}α(G)=n$, $\mathrm{tree}\text{-}χ(G)=k$, and $\mathrm{tw}(G)=Ω(nk\log_2 n)$. Thus the upper bound is best possible up to a constant factor.
CMC foliations on Euclidean spaces are minimal foliations
José Edson Sampaio; Euripedes Carvalho da Silva

In this article, we provide a complete answer to one of the most classical conjectures in differential geometry (of foliations). More precisely, we present a complete positive answer to the classical conjecture, due to Meeks III, Pérez, and Ros (2008), that states that every foliation on $\mathbb{R}^{n+1}$ by (possibly varying) CMC hypersurfaces is a foliation by minimal hypersurfaces. Moreover, if $n\leq 6$, such a CMC foliation must consist of parallel hyperplanes.
On the Structure of Radical Towers and their Parametrizations

Radical parametrizations describe algebraic varieties by means of nested radicals of polynomials, and their theory relies on three varieties associated with a parametrization, namely, the incidence, tower and radical varieties. In this paper we revisit this framework from a computational point of view and show that it is governed by the radical tower rather than by the particular parametrization. We prove that the tower variety depends only on the tower and that the incidence variety is always irreducible, so that no prime decomposition is needed. Moreover, we show how to replace a tower by an isomorphic one whose tower variety is defined by the equations of the tower, so that it can be computed without elimination. We introduce universal radical parametrizations and we use them to settle, under a natural hypothesis on the coefficients, an open case in the transformation of differential equations with radical coefficients into equations with rational coefficients. We show that radical subtowers form a lattice, which yields minimal radical parametrizations, and we give algorithms to compute them. We also prove that dominance between towers induces a unique dominant rational map between their tower varieties, through which unirationality is transferred. Finally, we study towers over subfields of $\mathbb{C}$ and, in the real case, relate the real points of the tower variety to the real domains of the associated parametrizations.
Generalization of Strang-Fix remark for discrete maximum principles on tetrahedral meshes
Safdar Ali; Maksat Ashyraliyev; Sergey Korotov; Sergei Silvestrov

Most of qualitative properties of finite element (FE) approximations for various PDE models, in particular the validity of the discrete maximum principles (DMPs), are usually guaranteed by certain geometric properties (e.g. acuteness/nonobtuseness) of FE meshes used. In this work, we revisit the linear FE discretization of the Poisson equation and discuss, in the context of DMPs, the representation of the stiffness matrix entries in terms of the edge lengths and cotangents of the dihedral angles of the tetrahedral meshes, thus avoiding the common use of face areas and element volumes. Using this type of entry representation, certain structural properties of meshes, and simple trigonometric relations, as proposed in the two-dimensional case by Strang and Fix, we show that DMPs still hold (as the stiffness matrices remain $M$-matrices) for many tetrahedral configurations with obtuse dihedral angles. Such a relaxation of the standard acuteness/nonobtuseness conditions can be vital in practical calculations, as these angle properties are difficult to preserve in global and local mesh refinements. Several representative examples are presented.
Relative entropy in quantum field theory: the case of squeezed fermions

We review the role of relative entropy in quantum field theories, where the local von Neumann algebras are generically of type III. Consequently, only few exact results are known, and even bounds are difficult to obtain. As a new result, we prove that the relative entropy between a locally squeezed state and the Minkowski vacuum is finite for free fermions.
Marcin Briański; Meike Hatzel; Karolina Okrasa; Michał Pilipczuk

The first major step in the theory of graph minors of Robertson and Seymour was the grid theorem, a fundamental duality result describing that any graph of sufficiently high treewidth must contain a large grid as a minor. Since this pioneering work, multiple grid theorems have been established in structural graph theory, linking various width parameters of combinatorial objects with the non-existence of grid-like obstructions. In particular, Kawarabayashi and Kreutzer [STOC'15] proved a variant of the grid theorem for directed graphs that links directed treewidth with the non-existence of topological minors of large cylindrical walls. On the other hand, to study immersions of undirected graphs $-$ another containment relation that focuses on edge-disjointness, rather than vertex-disjointness $-$ Wollan [JCTB'15] introduced a parameter, tree-cutwidth, and proved that it is dual to immersions of large walls.
 In this work, we present a version of Wollan's parameter for directed graphs, the directed tree-cutwidth. The main result is a grid theorem for directed tree-cutwidth, establishing that it is dual to directed immersions of large cylindrical walls.
Exact Joint MAP Decoding for Unknown Load and Message Counts in Orthogonal Unsourced Random Access

We study joint recovery of the load (the number of active users) and message-count vector in type-based unsourced random access with very short messages. Each user's $k$-bit message activates one of $M=2^k$ orthogonal resources; coherent collisions therefore produce a noisy, unnormalized histogram of the transmitted messages. For arbitrary load and message priors, we propose an exact joint maximum-a-posteriori (MAP) decoder. Known-load allocation is separable and convex; our contribution is to show that the solutions for all candidate loads are nested prefixes of one greedy chain. Scoring these prefixes with the Bayesian posterior terms jointly estimates the load and message-count vector in $O(M+K_{\max}\log M)$ time. We compare the proposed joint MAP decoder with marginal MAP, three scalar-count two-stage receivers, oracle-load MAP, a sum-only receiver, and a soft-pilot receiver. For $K\sim\operatorname{Unif}\{0{:}60\}$ at 2 dB, the proposed decoder cuts the no-activity false-alarm probability from $25.9\%$ to $3.5\%$ relative to the Bayesian-count two-stage receiver and, conditioned on $K\ge1$, reduces normalized count error by $21.4\%$. The advantage concentrates under idle or sparse uncertain activity, whereas support-count processing approaches joint MAP when the possible loads are well separated. We also prove that the sum-only statistic is insufficient and quantify prior and amplitude mismatch. The model targets synchronized, power-controlled, very-short payloads rather than general URA.
The Kaplansky-Walker Lemma for additive categories

We establish a Kaplansky-Walker type lemma for idempotent complete additive categories with direct sums. It will be used in compactly generated triangulated categories to provide a version of Kaplansky's theorem on projective modules and an isomorphism-refinement result for direct sums of countable objects.

Given $0\le m<n$ and a positive Radon measure $μ$ on $\mathbb R^n$ with at most polynomial growth, assume that it has finite $m$-dimensional \emph{Gaussian discrepancy}, defined as $$\mathcal D(μ):=\limsup_{R\to\infty}\Bigl[R^2\sup_{x\in\mathrm{spt}μ}|G_R^μ(x)-1|\Bigr],$$ where $G_R^μ(x):=(4πR^2)^{-m/2}\int_{\mathbb R^n} e^{-|z-x|^2/(4R^2)}\,dμ(z)$. Provided that $μ$ admits a flat blow-down $\mathcal H^m\llcorner V$ (an assumption that cannot be dropped entirely), we prove that there exists a finite (smallest) $0\leδ<\infty$, called the \emph{width} of $μ$, such that $$\mathrm{spt}μ\subseteq \bar B_δ(V+x_0),\quad δ^2\le C(m,n)\mathcal{D}(μ),$$ where $\bar B_δ(V+x_0)$ denotes the closed $δ$-neighborhood of a suitable translate of $V$. Note that the exponent is optimal because of scale invariance.
 In particular, when $\mathcal D(μ)=0$, the support of $μ$ is included in an $m$-dimensional affine plane. We use this fact to give a simpler proof of Preiss's rectifiability theorem: while still based on Gaussian averages of $μ$, this new proof avoids showing uniqueness (and hence conicality) of blow-downs of $m$-uniform measures, as well as studying Gaussian-weighted moments beyond second order.

GCD and ABC inequalities for abelian varieties over function fields

We prove two height inequalities for rational points on abelian varieties over function fields of characteristic 0. The first is the GCD inequality, which shows that the height with respect to a closed subscheme of an abelian variety of codimension at least 2 is much smaller than the usual height function. This can be viewed as a compact and geometric analogue of a theorem of Levin. The second is a special case of the (geometric) abc conjecture proposed by Vojta, which compares the truncated counting function and the usual counting function. This is a compact analogue of a theorem of Guo, Nguyen, Sun and Wang, and also resolves a conjecture of Buium, which was only known for traceless abelian varieties or constant abelian varieties previously.

Building on the canonical Xie-Yuan heights, we control discrete counting functions by continuous integrals of Betti forms. The main new tools are uniform Nevanlinna-type estimates for families of linear entire curves on abelian varieties; combined with covering arguments based on Besicovitch theory and averaging, these handle overlaps and gaps precisely.
Discrete Morse Theory for Computing Filtered Cosheaf Homology

This paper addresses the computation of persistent homology for filtrations of cellular cosheaves over a fixed cell complex, where the algebraic data vary along the filtration while the underlying topological structure remains unchanged. We extend methods from discrete Morse theory to this setting, establishing conditions under which chain complexes can be reduced while preserving the associated persistence module. Building on these results, we introduce "FilteredScythe", an algorithm that identifies Morse matchings compatible with all stages of the filtration and performs reductions using Schur complements, based on the exist "Scythe" algorithm. We prove the correctness of these reductions and establish bounds on the algorithm's time and space complexity.

We prove an \(L\log L\)-endpoint Cwikel estimate on quantum tori $\mathbb T_θ^d$, i.e., for every \(d\geq 1\) and \(x\in L\log L(\mathbb T_θ^d)\), \begin{equation*}
 (1-Δ)^{-\frac{d}{4}}λ(x)(1-Δ)^{-\frac{d}{4}}\in\mathcal{L}_{1,\infty} \end{equation*} with a bound depending only on the dimension, where $λ(x)$ is the left multiplication by $x$. The main ingredient is an abstract weak Hilbert--Schmidt estimate for multiplication operators in finite von Neumann algebras whose \(L_2\)-spaces admit orthonormal bases of unitaries. When $θ=0$, our argument also gives a simpler proof of the $L\log L$ Cwikel estimate on classical tori. For $d\geq2$, we use the $C^*$-algebraic principal symbol map to prove Weyl's laws for finite sums \[
 \sum_{\ell=1}^N
 S_\ell(1-Δ)^{-d/4}λ(x_\ell)
 (1-Δ)^{-d/4}T_\ell, \] where $x_\ell\in L\log L(\mathbb T_θ^d)$ and $S_\ell,T_\ell\inΠ$, the $C^*$-algebra generated by $λ(C(\mathbb T_θ^d))$ and Fourier multipliers with continuous symbols homogeneous of degree zero. We also prove a semiclassical Weyl's law for critical Schrödinger operators with $L\log L$ potentials.
Degeneracy graph determinants and higher-dimensional Young diagrams

Kemp and Ramgoolam proposed a basis of monomials for a commutative semisimple algebra with generators \(C_1,\ldots, C_L\), constructed from a degeneracy graph which records how the eigenspaces of \( C_1\) are successively split by \( C_2,\ldots, C_L\). They showed that the basis property is equivalent to the non-vanishing of the determinant of the matrix of values of these monomials on the projector basis, and conjectured a factorised formula for this determinant, as a product of powers of eigenvalue differences. We prove this formula for any number of generators. The proof uses graph analogues of Newton polynomials. Their evaluation matrix is not triangular in general, but expanding the rows of the children of each node of the penultimate layer in a Newton basis of their eigenvalues makes it block triangular, with diagonal blocks given by smaller degeneracy graphs in which the final layer is removed. The formula then follows by induction on the number of layers. We show that the exponents in the determinant are overlap volumes of higher-dimensional Young diagrams attached to the nodes of the graph: intervals, ordinary Young diagrams, plane partitions and their higher analogues. Finally, the block triangular structure gives an explicit recursive inversion of the evaluation matrix, expressing the projectors in the monomial basis.
A Unified Linear Programming Approach for Maximizing Vertex-Degree-Based Indices of Trees

The problem of maximizing vertex-degree-based topological indices over trees with a prescribed order and maximum degree $Δ$ has traditionally relied on ad-hoc combinatorial arguments. In this paper, we establish a unified linear programming approach that systematically resolves these extremal problems. By formulating the optimization over degree-pair multiplicities, the search for an extremal tree reduces to minimizing a discrete dual penalty. Treating vertex degrees as continuous variables yields an analytical single-variable test condition that guarantees global optimality. We apply this framework across a diverse collection of invariants. We prove that the standard basic feasible solution is optimal for the Tangent Sombor, $SO_1$, $SO_2$, Albertson, and $σ$-irregularity indices for all $Δ\ge 3$. However, the dual optimality conditions establish exact analytical thresholds at which the standard basis loses optimality, necessitating a transition to alternative basic feasible solutions. For the Arithmetic-Geometric ($AG$) index, the standard basis is optimal strictly for $Δ\ge 9$; for smaller maximum degrees ($3 \le Δ\le 8$), optimization shifts to an alternative edge basis, allowing us to explicitly construct and characterize all extremal trees across congruence classes, including chemical trees ($Δ\in \{3, 4\}$). Conversely, for the Triangle Volume index ($SO_{11}$), the standard basis is optimal exclusively for $Δ\le 8$, while for $Δ\ge 9$ we analytically derive a novel, degree-dependent optimal basis to explicitly construct its extremal configurations.
On local minimality of Hausdorff dimension for round limit sets
Sami Douba; Andrés Sambarino; Franco Vargas Pallete

We address a question of Canary--Taylor and Canary--Minsky--Taylor for sufficiently symmetric compact hyperbolic $3$-orbifolds with totally geodesic boundary. We give sufficient conditions on the symmetries of such an orbifold to show that, among the complete convex cocompact structures on the interior, the structure with Fuchsian ends is a critical point (respectively, a strict local minimum) for the critical exponent. We also provide an infinite family of non-rigid examples fulfilling these conditions.

We establish finite-dimensional von Neumann type inequalities for commuting matrix tuples in noncommutative operator balls. Let $Ω=\mathbb{D}_Q$ be the NC operator ball of a linear pencil $Q$ with linearly independent coefficients. If $Ω(1)$ admits a transitive subgroup of automorphisms with NC lifts and $Ω(1)$ has the bounded $H^\infty$-Gleason property at the origin, then $\|f(T)\|\leq C_{Ω,n}\|f\|_{H^\infty(Ω(1))}$ for every commuting tuple $T\inΩ(n)$, with $C_{Ω,n}=(2ρ_ΩK_Ω)^{n-1}$; here $K_Ω$ is the Gleason constant and $ρ_Ω$ is the sum of the suprema of the coordinate functions on $Ω(1)$. The scalar coordinate bounds persist at every matrix level. The hypotheses hold for products of row and column balls, where $ρ_Ω=d$, yielding an unconditional estimate $(2dK_Ω)^{n-1}$. For a general type I Cartan domain $R_{p,q}$, we obtain only a conditional result: the same bound holds provided the scalar domain has the bounded $H^\infty$-Gleason property at the origin, which we do not establish when $\min(p,q)\geq 2$.

For the quadratic unconstrained binary optimization (QUBO) problem, such assignments can be computed efficiently via autarkies of quadratic posiforms. However, the largest autarky domain and thus the number of fixed variables can depend on the specific posiform representation. We show that every quadratic posiform with the greatest possible constant term (the roof-dual bound) yields the largest autarky domain obtainable from any quadratic posiform. By computing such a roof-dual-optimal quadratic posiform and a corresponding autarky with largest domain in polynomial time, one can therefore attain the maximum partial optimality obtainable by quadratic posiform autarkies in polynomial time. This justifies the computation of roof-dual-optimal quadratic posiforms and corresponding autarkies in popular polynomial-time algorithms and establishes that finding additional partial optimality in QUBO requires going beyond autarkies of quadratic posiforms.

We study nonconvex-strongly-concave minimax problem $\min_{\mathbf{x}\in\mathbb{R}^{d_x}}\max_{\mathbf{y}\in\mathbb{R}^{d_y}}f(\mathbf{x},\mathbf{y})$ in which the objective has $ρ$-Lipschitz Hessian and condition number $κ$. Let $S_m$ be the Schur multiplier with symbol $m$. We characterize the boundedness of $S_m:\mathcal S^1\to\mathcal S^{1,\infty}$ by approximation of weighted columns in a common finite-dimensional subspace. If $W(m)$ is the weak $(1,1)$ bound and $\fD(m)$ is the column approximation constant, then $\tfrac12W(m)\le\fD(m)\le2W(m)$. These estimates hold uniformly under amplification. The proof uses two adjacent dyadic grids and block decompositions indexed by finite binary trees. We apply Cuculescu's projections to the associated block-diagonal filtration. Let $G=C_2\times C_2$ and $A=\{0,1\}$. We characterize the submonoid of $\text{CA}(G;A)$ generated by lazy and invertible cellular automata. A cellular automaton belongs to this submonoid if and only if, whenever it maps the two free $G$-orbits onto the same free orbit, it maps both constant configurations and some two-point orbit to the same constant. The proof gives a factorization using elementary orbit collapses and three two-cell lazy maps. An external receiver requests a linear combination of these data, and the sources use information cached before the request is known to reduce the communication needed to recover the requested result. In our model, each of the $N$ sources stores its own independent file over a finite field and has an additional cache of normalized size $M$. The receiver must recover any requested linear combination with zero error from the messages sent by the sources over separate noiseless links. We establish a lower bound on the worst-case communication rate over any finite field by analyzing several requests under the same cache placement. This bound determines the optimal rate when no additional cache is available. For binary files, we propose parity-aided placement (PAP), a coded-placement scheme that combines cached parities with uncoded symbols. For every $N\geq3$, we characterize its communication rate for each request and optimize its placement parameters to obtain a closed-form worst-case rate. The resulting achievable rate meets the lower bound for $0\leq M\leq1/(2N-1)$ and $M\geq(N-1)/N$, establishing the optimal memory--rate tradeoff in these two ranges.
Antoine Abram; Florent Hivert; James D. Mitchell; Jean-Christophe Novelli; Maria Tsalakou

In this paper we describe the quotients of several plactic-like monoids by the least congruences containing the relations $a^{σ(a)} = a$ for $σ(a) \geq 2$ for every generator $a$. The starting point of this paper is the recent paper of Reutenauer and the first author about the stylic monoid. This monoid is the quotient of the plactic monoid by the relations $a^2 = a$ for every generator $a$. The plactic-like monoids considered here are the plactic monoid itself, the Chinese monoid, the hypoplactic monoid, the sylvester monoid, the metasylvester and hyposylvester monoids. Given a set of employees and a set of customers with pre-scheduled visits, we want to build doubly-open routes to guarantee visits to all customers, ensuring that each customer is visited by an employee with the appropriate skills to carry out the required activity. The travel times between customers and the service time in each customer are known. The problem includes time windows for visiting customers, each employee has a maximum working time, and the daily working period is between 9 AM and 6:30 PM. The routes respect the lunch break period if they extend from morning to afternoon, which means that lunch break can be avoided if the route is fully completed in the morning or in the afternoon. The aim is to minimize the distance covered by all routes with a penalty for including lunch breaks. The distances and times between customers are collected via an API to Microsoft Azure; and the solutions are then displayed on Bing Maps. The results obtained show the operational advantages of an efficient and effective vehicle routing planning in a specific condominium management company. The model can be extended to other service provider companies.
Undirected Network Coding and Faster External-Memory Integer Sorting
Baochun Li; Zongpeng Li; Sirui Liu

Network coding allows intermediate nodes to combine messages, whereas routing only forwards them. The Li-Li conjecture asserts that network coding and fractional routing have the same capacity region in undirected multiple-unicast networks. We give a counterexample to this conjecture and apply it to external-memory integer sorting. Since Aggarwal and Vitter posed the question in 1988, whether integer sorting can beat the external-memory comparison bound has remained a central and extensively studied open problem. We give a deterministic sorting algorithm: for $N$ integers of $Θ(\log N)$ bits, a memory holding $M$ integers, and block transfers of $B$ integers, where $2B\le M\le N$, the number of block transfers is $O\left(\frac{N}{B}\left[1+\frac{\log N}{(\log(M/B))^{1-\varepsilon}(\log M)^\varepsilon}\right]\right)$, where $\varepsilon>0$ is an absolute constant. In a range of parameter regimes, this bound is asymptotically smaller than the classical comparison-sorting bound. We also use Lean 4 to verify the sorting algorithm's correctness and complexity bounds, and the strict advantage of coding over routing.
On the maximum relational complexity of affine groups
Coen del Valle; Nick Gill; Pablo Spiga

Let $G$ be a group of permutations of a set $Ω$. The relational complexity $\mathrm{RC}(G)$ is the least integer $r\geq 2$ such that the $G$-orbit of every finite tuple is determined by the $G$-orbits of its $r$-subtuples; there is currently only a small collection of groups $G$ for which $\mathrm{RC}(G)$ is known precisely. In this paper we study the relational complexity of finite affine groups acting naturally on a $d$-dimensional vector space over $\mathbb{F}_q$. We prove that every such group has relational complexity at most $d+2$ when $q>2$ and at most $d+1$ when $q=2$; we produce a complete classification of the primitive such groups for which these bounds are attained.
Finitistic dimensions of formal power series rings

We consider the big finitistic projective and flat dimensions of a commutative ring and of its formal power series ring. When the ring is Noetherian, both invariants increase by one. Coherence of the power series ring does not force either equality to hold. For every \(n\ge0\) and every \(d\) with \(n+1\le d\le\infty\), the flat pair \((n,d)\) can be realized. The finite projective pairs are realized when \(n\ge1\), and also for \((0,1)\). For every \(n\ge0\), one family realizes \((n,\infty)\) for both invariants at the same time. The seed is a zero-dimensional perfect local ring. Its power series ring has countably presented modules whose flat dimension is \(r\) and whose projective dimension lies between \(r\) and \(r+1\), for every \(r\ge1\). The remaining finite projective case is controlled by a dichotomy for perfect coefficient rings. If the Jacobson radical is nilpotent, the power series value is one; if it is not nilpotent, there is a module of projective dimension exactly three. In particular, the pair \((0,2)\) is impossible. For one fixed countable perfect ring, the power series ring has finitistic flat dimension one. Its finitistic projective dimension is \(m+2\) when \(2^{\aleph_0}=\aleph_m\) with \(1\le m<\infty\), and is infinite when \(2^{\aleph_0}>\aleph_ω\).

OpenAI (using a non-public "internal frontier model'') has recently (6 October 2026) made a number of remarkable claims, including some claims regarding the quasi-Riemann hypothesis (QRH). While there are good reasons to be cautious regarding these claims, one can nevertheless ask what (if true) their implications would be. While there is widespread agreement that any version of the QRH will provide various improved bounds on the location of the prime numbers, I feel that there is some value in making these improvements explicit. Specifically, if we assume validity of the claimed 7/8 version of the QRH then I shall demonstrate (for all $n\in \mathbb{Z^+}$): 1) the existence of primes between eighth powers, in the interval $(n^8,(n+1)^8)$; 2) the existence of primes in the shorter interval $(n^8,n^8+8n^7)$; 3) the existence of primes in the even shorter interval $(n^8,n^8+n^7).$ Similarly for reals greater than unity $x>1$ one can demonstrate: 4) the existence of primes in the Hoheisel-style interval $(x,x+x^{7/8})$. All of this is contingent on the validity of the claimed 7/8 version of the QRH.
A semi-discrete scheme for horizontal mean curvature flow in the Heisenberg group
A. Cesaroni; M. Novaga; P. Pozzi

The horizontal mean curvature flow is a geometric evolution associated with the horizontal perimeter in sub-Riemannian spaces. In this paper, we introduce a minimizing movement scheme for this flow in the first Heisenberg group $\mathbb{H}$, and prove the existence of a flat flow which is locally $1/2$-Hölder continuous in time, with respect to the $L^1$-distance. The construction applies to arbitrary bounded sets of finite horizontal perimeter and does not require smoothness or symmetry of the initial datum.
Scaling Limits of Density Fluctuation Fields of the Symmetric Partial Exclusion Processes Approaching the Zero Range Process

We study equilibrium fluctuations for the symmetric partial exclusion process (SPEP) on the one-dimensional integer lattice $\mathbb{Z}$, an interacting particle system in which each site is occupied by at most $α$ particles. We assume that the jump rate is decomposable and that the instantaneous current admits a gradient form. Our aim is to study the scaling limit of the density fluctuation field of the SPEP starting from an invariant measure and to derive the corresponding stochastic partial differential equation (SPDE).
 A distinctive feature of our setting is that the maximum number of particles per site depends on the scaling parameter $n$ as $α=α_n \propto n^a$ for some $a>0$, so that the model interpolates between the partial exclusion process ($α<\infty$) and the symmetric zero range process (SZRP, $α= \infty$). Under the diffusive rescaling in which the lattice spacing is $1/n$ and time is accelerated by a factor $n^2$, we prove that the density fluctuation field converges to the solution of the stochastic heat equation.
 The limiting SPDE coincides with the one obtained for the SZRP. A key ingredient in the proof is the convergence, under a suitable rescaling, of the partition function of the reversible measure of the SPEP to that of the SZRP. This convergence implies that expectations of a wide class of local functions under the reversible measure of the SPEP converge to the corresponding expectations under the reversible measure of the SZRP, and provides a rigorous sense in which the SPEP approximates the SZRP as $n\to\infty$.
Michael Hull; Thomas Payne; Thomas Weighill

We show that every vineyard can be decomposed into vines, that is, every path in the space of persistence diagrams $\mathcal{D}$ can be decomposed into a sequence of paths in $\mathbb R^2$. Moreover, we characterize which spaces $X$ have the property that every continuous map $X\to \mathcal{D}$ has such a decomposition. Our results hold not just for $\mathcal{D}$, but also for many other spaces of unordered tuples.
Markman--Markushevich principle and Lagrangian fibrations on O'Grady six-manifolds

To any compact holomorphically symplectic manifold and a nef BBF-isotropic class we associate a quasi-projective variety called the Markman--Markushevich space which parametrises the Lagrangian fibrations with this isotropic class modulo Tate--Shafarevich twists. We give a systematic interpretation of known results about Tate--Shafarevich twists of Lagrangian fibrations using this space, employ it to obtain a conjectural result for the last deformation type for which such a result is not yet proposed, and make some first steps towards its proof. As a byproduct, we generalise the results of Kumar on existence Shioda--Inose partners for abelian surfaces to a slightly more general class of K3 surfaces, and associate a canonical K3 surface with transcendental lattice isometric to $U^2\oplus\langle-2\rangle^2$ to a smooth cubic surface with a choice of a Schläfli double-six. We also review some other approaches towards the construction of complete families of O'Grady six-manifolds with Lagrangian fibrations, and show how they may still be useful even though they do not quite work.
Algebraic and Symmetrized Affine star-Ricci Solitons for the Bott Connection on Three-Dimensional Lorentzian Lie Groups

We fix a spacelike two-dimensional left-invariant distribution and its associated almost contact structure on a three-dimensional Lorentzian Lie group, and investigate the star-Ricci contraction of the curvature of the Bott connection. We compute the complete tensor for seven standard bracket families and determine all real parameter solutions of the general algebraic equation and its self-adjoint subclass. Using the symmetric part of the tensor, we also define a Bott affine star-Ricci soliton equation and classify all left-invariant vector field solutions. Every affine solution is steady, while two non-unimodular families admit branches with a nonzero symmetrized tensor. The proofs provide complete component equations, treat all degenerate parameter branches, and establish sufficiency by explicit substitution. We also distinguish almost contact structures from contact metric structures.
Maximal subsets of $n\times n$ board without cycles

abla(n)=L_n$ in case $n\equiv 1\pmod 6$ and $n\equiv 4\pmod 6$, while for the remaining $4$ residue classes $
abla(n)=L_n$ or $
abla(n)=L_n+1$. In this paper, we provide optimal constructions in the odd residue classes $n\equiv3,5\pmod6$, (proving $
abla(n)=L_n$) and a geometric obstruction showing that equality in lower bound is impossible when $n\equiv0,2\pmod6$ (yielding $
