The Fomin-Kirillov algebras $\mathcal{FK}_n$ are shown to be infinite-dimensional for $n\geq 6$. By computer calculations, we find an explicit nonzero primitive element of degree 14 in the identity component of $\mathcal{FK}_6$. For every $n\geq 6$, the existence of such an element implies that $\mathcal{FK}_n$ contains a polynomial subalgebra and is therefore infinite-dimensional, and that the canonical homomorphism from $\mathcal{FK}_n$ onto its associated Nichols algebra is not an isomorphism.
A particle swarm optimization with a reduced-subspace trust-region safeguard for contact-rich controller tuning
Morteza Kimiaei; Roya Khalili-Amirabadi; Mohsen Jalaeian-Farimani

Contact-rich robotic insertion is challenging because uncertainty in alignment, friction, and contact conditions can lead to unsuccessful assembly, excessive contact forces, and jamming. Designing a reliable controller therefore requires balancing insertion performance, robustness, and recovery from unexpected contact. In this paper, we propose PSO+TR, a derivative-free optimization (DFO) method that combines the exploratory search of particle swarm optimization (PSO) with a trust-region (TR) procedure for local refinement to improve the search process when progress stagnates. We apply the method to derivative-free policy optimization of an interpretable robotic insertion controller, jointly tuning its motion, feedback, and recovery parameters while preserving its predefined control structure. The proposed approach is evaluated on 93 eligible benchmark problems from the bound-constrained programs (BCP) collection and a synthetic contact-rich planar insertion task under uncertain operating conditions. Three random seeds per benchmark problem yield 279 matched problem--seed instances per method. PSO+TR reaches the prescribed target on 228 of these instances (81.72\%), the highest observed target-attainment rate among the five compared methods, which also include PSO, randomized black-box optimization (VRBBO), matrix adaptation evolution strategy (MAES), and differential evolution (DE). Across eight robotic optimizer seeds, the deployed controller-selection pipeline achieves 97.78\% completion under development conditions and 58.00\% under withheld stress conditions, compared with 91.22\% and 31.12\%, respectively, for the fixed staged controller. The stress violation rate is reduced from 20.69\% to 2.19\%. These findings support combining global and local search for DFO and structured contact-rich controller tuning. The synthetic planar results require validation on physical robots.
Stabilities of Background Perturbations for Compressible Adiabatic Flows through Porous Media in 3-D

In this paper, we study the background stability problem for three-dimensional compressible adiabatic flows through porous media. For two given equilibrium states $(\bar{P}^k,\vec{0},\bar{S}^k)$ ($k=0,1$), under the assumption of small initial perturbations around each equilibrium state, pointwise estimates of solutions for individual perturbation problems are obtained. Based on these pointwise structures, a comparison between two individual solutions could be applied and it is proved that the difference between two solutions depends continuously on the equilibrium distance $|\bar{P}^0-\bar{P}^1|+|\bar{S}^0-\bar{S}^1|$ as well as the initial perturbation difference, with additional decay rates, thereby establishing a nonlinear comparison principle for this system. Compared with previous works on background stability problems, it is the first time to obtain stabilities in the pointwise sense. Our main tools are Green's functions, a priori energy estimates, and refined decay estimates for higher-order derivatives.
Sequence Factory: Families of Integer Sequences Generated by Gödel Implication

A finite Gödel chain generates not one integer sequence but a large family of them. The combinatorial mechanism is developed in a companion paper; here the sequences themselves are the primary objects. For $V_m=\{v_0<\cdots<v_{m-1}\}$, let $g_{j,n}^{(m)}$ count outputs equal to $v_j$, aggregated over all full bracketings on $n$ variables and all $m^n$ valuations. The root-pair refinement produces $N_{i,j}^{(m)}(n)=\sum_{r=1}^{n-1}g_{i,r}^{(m)}g_{j,n-r}^{(m)}$, with generating functions $N_{i,j}^{(m)}(x)=G_i^{(m)}(x)G_j^{(m)}(x)$.
 We prove that the initial coefficients of these products uniquely identify the unordered root-value pair. Consequently, for each fixed $m$, there are exactly $\binom{m+1}{2}$ distinct root-pair generating functions. We catalogue the factories for $m=4,5,\ldots,10$, giving the first ten terms of every base sequence and every symmetric root-pair sequence. This range contains 49 base sequences and 210 symmetric pair classes, yielding 259 indexed sequence families before additional aggregates. The catalogue provides reproducible data for integer-sequence analysis and comparison with the On-Line Encyclopedia of Integer Sequences (OEIS).
On the Topology of Fibers of Rational Functions

In 1988 Broughton proved that if a complex polynomial function on ${\mathbb C}^n$ is tame at infinity its fibers are homotopy equivalent to bouquets of some spheres. Since then several basic properties of polynomial functions were studied by many mathematicians in various situations. In this paper, we show some evidence for the possibility of extending Broughton's result to rational functions satisfying some tameness condition at infinity and the one at their points of indeterminacy. Specifically, assuming some conditions on a rational function on ${\mathbb C}^n$ we prove that the cohomology groups of a generic fiber of it are isomorphic to those of a bouquet of $S^1$ and some spheres. In the course of the proof, the theory of the nearby and vanishing cycle sheaves for meromorphic functions will play an essential role.
Maximal subgroups of topological full groups of shifts of finite type

We study maximal subgroups of topological full groups of irreducible one-sided shifts of finite type whose associated groupoids have Cantor unit space. For each wide open subgroupoid of such a groupoid, we construct a subgroupoid graph and identify the subgroupoid with a full compact open reduction of the corresponding countable graph groupoid. Every minimal wide open subgroupoid is either AF or purely infinite. A proper wide open subgroupoid is prime if it admits no proper intermediate wide open subgroupoid. We prove a trichotomy for prime subgroupoids: they are minimal, arise from a clopen bipartition, or have a unique nonempty proper closed invariant set, which is nowhere dense. For a prime subgroupoid, the normalizer of its topological full group is maximal in the ambient topological full group precisely when it maps onto the ambient abelianization. An analogous criterion holds in every subgroup containing the ambient commutator subgroup. For a minimal prime subgroupoid, its topological full group is maximal precisely when it equals its normalizer and the inclusion induces a surjection on first groupoid homology. We also describe all fully amplified maximal subgroups, namely those closed under local agreement. For Thompson's group $V$, the stabilizer of every simple type system is maximal, extending results of Belk, Bleak, Quick and Skipper for finite type systems and certain classes of infinite ones. Finally, every subgroup containing the ambient commutator subgroup has continuum many pairwise nonisomorphic maximal subgroups acting minimally on the unit space.
Strong Negative Type of Star-shaped Manifolds

Metric spaces of negative type (NT) and strong negative type (SNT) are fundamental in wide applications across computer science and statistics. It is well-known that spheres equipped with geodesic distance are of NT, and subsets of a sphere that contain at most one pair of antipodal points (e.g. an open hemisphere) are of SNT. In this paper, we extend these results to a class of star-shaped manifolds. By constructing a metric $d$ based on layer-wise radial projections, we prove that every star-shaped manifold, equipped with $d$, is of NT. Moreover, we prove that a subset of a star-shaped manifold is of SNT under certain injectivity and directional asymmetry conditions. In particular, for a subset of a single layer, it is of SNT if it contains exactly one point from each preimage of an open hemisphere (a fully directional asymmetry); moreover, it is of SNT if and only if it contains at most one opposite-directional pair.
Ergodic and Metastable Behavior of Stochastic Popularity Dynamics in Social Networks
Chiara Ravazzi; Paolo Frasca; Gaya Cocca

This paper studies popularity dynamics in social networks, where users' engagement with competing channels is driven by intrinsic content quality, social influence, and popularity feedback. We introduce a stochastic model in which users interact through a directed influence network and channel exposure depends jointly on these three mechanisms. We first characterize the resulting dynamics in the absence of intrinsic quality, showing that popularity concentrates asymptotically on a single channel, leading to a winner-takes-all regime. When all channels have positive intrinsic quality, we establish ergodicity of the popularity process and characterize its long-run behavior. We further show that, when intrinsic quality is small, the system exhibits metastable behavior: it can remain for long periods near configurations dominated by a single channel before transitioning to another. These results highlight how weak quality differences can coexist with strong path dependence induced by popularity feedback. We then investigate platform-level interventions and propose controls that compensate for network-induced exposure biases and mitigate excessive concentration. Analytical results are illustrated through numerical simulations and an empirical analysis of YouTube data, whose observed popularity dynamics are consistent with the proposed stochastic framework. The results provide a mathematical framework for understanding the interplay between quality, social influence, and reinforcement in online popularity dynamics.

It is folklore that passing "convergence" diagnostics does not guarantee that a Markov chain has converged. We prove this as an impossibility for any finite checklist of diagnostics. Running more chains, longer chains, and smarter diagnostics does not avoid this impossibility in certifying convergence. Under regularity assumptions, we determine how the worst-case undetected non-convergence decays as more diagnostics are added, and how to choose diagnostics optimally. Folklore suggests that the sampler's slowest mixing modes are the "dangerous" ones that must be monitored; we prove that the slow modes yield nearly optimal diagnostics as sampling proceeds. Given a source class, we also give an anytime-valid bound on the remaining discrepancy and show how undetected bias caps the effective sample size that a finite checklist can certify.
Refined blow-up behavior for semilinear heat equations with arbitrarily fast growing nonlinearities

We study radially nonincreasing, positive blow-up solutions of a class of superlinear heat equations in the non-scale-invariant setting. This class contains nonlinearities with arbitrarily fast, super-exponential growth.
 Under suitable structural assumptions on the nonlinearity, we derive the sharp global blow-up profile in the original space-time variables.
 More precisely, for positive nonlinearities $f$ satisfying $$
 \lim_{X\to \infty}f'(X)G(X)= q\ge1\quad \quad
 \hbox{ where }\quad\quad G(X)=\int_{X}^{\infty}\frac{ ds}{f(s)}<\infty\quad\forall\ X>0, $$ and assuming either the time monotonicity $u_t\ge0$ holds or $q>\frac{p_S}{p_S-1}$, we have
 $$
 u(x,t)=(1+o(1))\,G^{-1}\bigg(T-t+\frac{|x|^2}{4q|\log |x|^2|}\bigg),
 \quad \hbox{as $(x,t)\to (0,T)$.} $$ This estimate in particular provides the sharp final space profile and the corresponding refined space-time profile. Moreover, our result recovers the universal structure of the global blow-up profile, given by the resolvent $G^{-1}$ of the associated ODE evaluated at a time-space building block, which only depends on the limit $q$.
On deformations of foliated complex analytic structures III: Unfoldings

We study unfoldings of foliated complex analytic structures defined by locally free subsheaves of cotangent sheaves. We prove theorem of existence for unfoldings of foliated complex analytic structures defined by locally free subsheaves of cotangent sheaves for one-parameter families. We prove theorem of completeness for unfoldings of foliated complex analytic structures defined by locally free subsheaves of cotangent sheaves. We also present unfoldings of foliated nonsingular varieties defined by locally free subsheaves of cotangent sheaves in the language of functors of Artin rings which is the algebraic version of unfoldings of foliated complex analytic structures. We identify first-order unfoldings and obstructions.
Divisibility Estimates for Gaussian Norms and Almost-Prime Orders of a CM Elliptic Curve

Let $E:y^2=x^3-x$. We prove that $\#E(\mathbf{F}_p)/8$ is squarefree and has at most two prime factors for $\gg X/(\log X)^2$ primes $p\le X$. The proof follows the Gaussian CM sieve framework of Iwaniec and Jiménez Urroz and incorporates the intersection terms identified by Xie. For a squarefree Gaussian ideal $\mathfrak{a}$, we separate its largest rational ideal factor and use the resulting divisibility of both integral coordinates to control the large-factor tail. This transfers an ideal Bombieri--Vinogradov estimate to rational norm divisibility at level $1/2$, with any fixed power of the divisor function as a weight. We prove the corresponding distribution estimate for the switched product sequence and apply the transfer to both sequences in Chen's weighted sieve. The primes counted may be restricted to $p\equiv5\pmod8$; their normalized orders are odd, squarefree, and supported on primes congruent to $1\pmod4$.
Avoiding a partial Latin square with an isotope of a given Latin square

For all sufficiently large $n$, we prove that every Latin square of order $n$ can be made to avoid any prescribed partial Latin square of order $n$ by permuting only its rows and columns. The proof combines Hall's theorem with elementary estimates for a random permutation.
Minimax estimation of the pseudo-spectral gap of continuous Markov chains, with applications to empirical concentration bounds
Vahe Karagulyan; Mikołaj Kasprzak; Pierre Alquier

We study the minimax estimation of the pseudo-spectral gap $γ_{ps}$ of a Markov chain from the observation of a single trajectory. Extending earlier works on finite-state space chains by Wolfer and Kontorovich (2024), we provide an estimator in the case of a compact, continuous state-space. Our estimator appears to be minimax-optimal on the class of chains with a transition operator with Lipschitz density, up to logarithmic terms. Our estimator, combined with Paulin's version of Bernstein inequality, allows to derive empirical concentration inequalities for Markov chains. This unlocks many applications, from confidence intervals, to active learning and generalization bounds. In particular, for rested bandits with Markov rewards, we provide a version of UCB with a regret bound similar to the one in the iid case, without assuming any knowledge on the pseudo-spectral gap of the chains.
Multi-Instantons and Exact-WKB Stokes Jumps in Multi-Well Quantum Mechanics

We study the relation between the exact-WKB Delabaere--Dillinger--Pham Stokes jumps and the multi-instanton expansion of a one-dimensional potential with $N$ equal-depth minima. For a single barrier this relation is the Bogomolny--Zinn-Justin cancellation between the instanton--anti-instanton ambiguity and the Borel ambiguity of perturbation theory, and we extend it to every consecutive barrier interval and to the integration contours themselves. In the dilute large-$T$ regime at fixed nonperturbative grade, we derive the quasi-zero mode integral over the instanton separations from the Euclidean path integral and reduce it to Gamma and Hankel periods. With the local Weber level function of each well and one normalization per well fixed by the local Weber connection matrix, these periods reproduce the two lateral connected exact-WKB coefficients. The two lateral contours of each instanton--anti-instanton separation differ by exactly one Hankel cycle, and this linear Picard--Lefschetz relation reproduces the Stokes jump of the connected coefficient. A numerical solution of the Schrödinger equation for a symmetric triple well confirms the resulting two-barrier level splitting. At higher fixed grade, the map from ordered event sequences to normalized scalar coefficient products is not one-to-one. At leading dilute order the scalar weight of a closed event sequence depends only on the numbers of barrier crossings, $\mathcal I\bar{\mathcal I}$ pairs, and $\mathcal I\mathcal I$/$\bar{\mathcal I}\bar{\mathcal I}$ pairs. We construct two inequivalent grade-six triple-well event sequences with the same product of local Weber amplitudes, which embed in every potential with $N\ge3$ wells. Our results hold within the regular dilute, one-loop, local Weber approximation.
Sharp Sobolev inequalities under first moment constraints
Rupert L. Frank; Tianling Jin; Hua-Yang Wang; Jingang Xiong

Let $n\geq2$ and $1<p<n$. We study sharp Sobolev inequalities on the round sphere $\mathbb{S}^n$ for functions $u\in W^{1,p}(\mathbb{S}^n)$ satisfying $\int_{\mathbb{S}^n}x|u|^{np/(n-p)}\,dσ=0$. We prove that \[
 \|u\|_{L^{np/(n-p)}(\mathbb{S}^n)}^p \leq 2^{-p/n}S_{n,p}^p\|\nabla u\|_{L^p(\mathbb{S}^n)}^p+B\|u\|_{L^p(\mathbb{S}^n)}^p \] holds for all such functions with some $B=B(n,p)<\infty$ if and only if $1<p\leq2$ or $2<p<n<3p-2$, where $S_{n,p}$ is the optimal Euclidean Sobolev constant. This determines the exact range in which Aubin's inequality holds with the sharp gradient coefficient. For every $2\leq p<n$, we also establish the corresponding inequality with squared norms and gradient coefficient $2^{-2/n}S_{n,p}^2$. The gradient coefficient in each inequality is optimal. The proof combines stereographic averaging with quantitative stability of the Euclidean Sobolev inequality to obtain local second moment estimates that allow absorption of the localization errors.
Interior smoothness and zero-variance geometry for finite-maturity Heston American puts
Junkee Jeon; Takwon Kim; Jehan Oh

We study finite-maturity American puts in the Heston model without the Feller condition. At positive variance, the exercise boundary is smooth and strictly decreasing in remaining maturity and variance. At zero variance, the endpoint is locally Lipschitz in remaining maturity, the boundary moves with bounded speed in maturity uniformly down to zero variance, and it extends continuously to the axis. Each boundary slice at positive maturity has a regular $C^1$ closure tangent to the zero-variance axis, its stock threshold has variance derivative tending to minus infinity, and both partial derivatives of the inverse boundary graph vanish along the slice. The continuation premium at the axis contact stock is of order variance, and as a consequence smooth fit fails in the variance direction at the axis. At expiry the whole boundary, including its axis edge, converges to the strike. We give quantitative boundary gap bounds, an exact limiting weighted boundary Hessian, and vertical identities retaining the maturity term. Exact boundary gap equivalents remain open.
An elementary proof of Brémont's theorem on the convergence of equilibrium measures at temperature zero

We give an elementary proof that if $f$ is a locally constant function on a topologically mixing subshift of finite type, then the equilibrium measures for $tf$ converge as $t\to\infty$, a result due to Brémont. The proof shows that the limit measure assigns an algebraic number to every cylinder.
New spherical codes by tuning an annealing solver

The spherical code problem asks how to place $N$ points on a unit sphere in $D$ dimensions to maximize the smallest distance between two points. It is a non-smooth and non-convex max-min problem, where few problem sizes have known optimal solutions, some have constructions, but most still only have numerically obtained solutions. We use a simple solver, with seven parameters, that anneals a LogSumExp surrogate, minimizes with L-BFGS, applies a random perturbation between anneals, and repeats with no acceptance test until a fixed limit is reached. We search the solver parameters for every instance with $N \le 1024$, $3 \le D \le 32$, and $N > 2D$, a total of 29,670 instances, using 32 parameter trials. We then run the solver for 60 seconds with the best parameters for each instance, without utilizing any symmetries or existing solutions. After enforcing monotonicity of the results and numerically polishing the solutions, we improve the best known code in 4,577 instances. When a single set of solver parameters is used for all instances, with one 60-second episode, the number of improvements is still 3,649. From our records, we find 24 codes with an exact algebraic cosine. Among our ablations, we find that 1) the repeated anneal contributes most to improvements, 2) at our $32 \times 60$-second budget only fitting one parameter per-instance is better than fitting all seven, and 3) good parameters can be predicted from the instance size. We provide the solver code, the fitted parameters, and the codes.
A Parametrization of Solutions to the Yamabe Equation with Isolated Singularity
Qing Han; Jui-Yun Hung; Nan Wu

Inspired by a pioneering work by Caffarelli, Gidas, and Spruck, we study positive solutions to the Yamabe equation with nonremovable isolated singularities. It is known that there is a formal one-to-one correspondence between the collection of the solutions to the Yamabe equation with nonremovable isolated singularities and the collection of harmonic functions through formal infinite series determined by the harmonic functions. In this paper, we prove that these formal infinite series yield actual solutions to the Yamabe equation with a nonremovable isolated singularity. These solutions to the Yamabe equation have designated asymptotic behaviors determined by the harmonic functions. In a broader context, we provide a general method of constructing all solutions near their isolated singular points and all solutions near infinity.
Elliptic theory and dimension drop for operators with divergence-free form-bounded drifts in one-sided chord-arc domains

We develop a boundary value and potential theory for elliptic operators \[ L=-\Div(A
abla)+\B\cdot
abla \] with form-bounded drift in one-sided chord-arc domains. Assuming that the positive part of $\Div\B$ has sufficiently small form bound, we establish local regularity estimates and solvability of the Dirichlet problem, and construct the associated harmonic measure. Under the additional assumption $\Div\B\le0$, we construct a Green's function and prove pointwise and gradient estimates. For the characteristic distributional identity with a Dirac mass at the pole to hold, we will additionally assume either $\Div\B=0$ or $\B\in L^{n,1}_{	extup{loc}}(Ω)$. Moreover, in the divergence-free case, we obtain a local lower bound for the Green's function, CFMS estimates, doubling of harmonic measure, a comparison principle for nonnegative solutions with zero trace, and a change of pole formula. Finally, using AI, we construct, in the upper half-space, an operator of the form $-Δ+\B\cdot
abla$ with $\B$ form-bounded and divergence-free, whose harmonic measure exhibits dimension drop.

Robert Eymard; Thierry Gallou{ë}t; Rapha{è}le Herbin

This chapter focuses on finite volume methods. The finite volume method is a discretization method that is well suited for the numerical simulation of various types (for instance, elliptic, parabolic, or hyperbolic) of conservation laws; it has been extensively used in several engineering fields, such as fluid mechanics, heat and mass transfer, or petroleum engineering. Some of the important features of the finite volume method are similar to those of the finite element method: it may be used on arbitrary geometries, using structured or unstructured meshes, and it leads to robust schemes. The finite volume method is locally conservative because it is based on a ``balance'' approach: a local balance is written on each discretization cell that is often called ``control volume;'' by the divergence formula, an integral formulation of the fluxes over the boundary of the control volume is then obtained. The fluxes on the boundary are discretized with respect to the discrete unknowns.

In a few exceptional cases we provide necessary and sufficient conditions for such embeddings to hold, in many others only sufficient conditions and in that situation we clearly indicate why these are not necessary by means of additional criteria and specific examples. Rotation gives the inner disk bound, and conormal duality gives the outer bound. Both constants are optimal for the class of properly convex domains normalized at a Pick zero. The argument requires neither boundary smoothness nor any restriction on the multiplicity of the Pick zero.
C1 Virtual Element Methods for the Optimal Control of Oseen Equations with Stream-Function Formulation
Arbaz Khan; David Mora; Alberth Silgado; Harpal Singh

This work analyzes a $C^1$-conforming virtual element method for the optimal control of generalized Oseen equations, formulated using the stream-function on simply connected polygonal domains. The method is based on a conforming discretization in $H^2$ of arbitrary order $k \ge 2$. The discrete scheme considers an approximation of the state and co-state equations which involves a specifically designed operator for the convective term and a \textit{variational discretization} of the control variable. We derive quasi-optimal a priori error estimates in the $H^1$ and $H^2$-norms for the stream-function, and in the $L^2$-norm for the control, under standard assumptions on the family of polygonal meshes. The proposed method recovers the fluid velocity, vorticity, and pressure using suitable projections. Finally, we report several numerical experiments to support the theoretical findings using different polygonal meshes including the cavity problem. We highlight that this analysis also covers OCPs governed by Brinkman and Stokes equation.

We prove that a convex body with $C^\infty$ boundary in an odd dimension $n\ge3$ is algebraically integrable if and only if it is an ellipsoid. This answers Arnold's problem for smooth convex bodies. Together with Vassiliev's even-dimensional nonexistence theorem, it gives the classification in every dimension $n\ge2$. More generally, in odd dimensions, a convex body with $C^\infty$ semialgebraic boundary is an ellipsoid whenever its section volume function satisfies a joint algebraic relation.
Weighted composition--differentiation operators on mixed-norm, derivative Hardy and F(p,q,s) spaces

We study weighted composition--differentiation operators on mixed-norm, derivative Hardy and F(p,q,s) spaces. Explicit dyadic criteria yield boundedness, compactness and two-sided norm and essential-norm estimates, including endpoint and quasi-Banach cases. We also obtain multiplier and approximation results, Schatten criteria on weighted Dirichlet spaces, and exact singular values for monomial weights and linear symbols.
Time-Inconsistent Singular Dividend Control with Regime Switching and Bankruptcy
Xiaochen Chen; Guohui Guan; Zongxia Liang; Xiaodong Luo

This paper studies infinite-horizon equilibrium dividend distribution for a firm whose surplus follows a diffusion under observable Markov regime switching and is absorbed at bankruptcy. Dividend payments are modeled as singular controls, and non-exponential discounting leads to time inconsistency. We formulate equilibrium control laws and establish a verification theorem for a general finite-state model with surplus-dependent coefficients. For a two-state model with constant positive drifts and volatilities and bi-exponential discounting, we prove the existence of a regime-dependent equilibrium barrier policy for arbitrary positive switching intensities. The policy retains surplus below the prevailing regime's threshold and distributes any excess immediately. Numerical experiments examine how shareholder patience and economic conditions affect dividend decisions. Over the parameter ranges considered, greater discount-rate dispersion at a fixed initial average rate raises both barriers, while switching speed can generate nonmonotone responses and reverse their ordering.
Calabi metric on the space of k-Hessian potentials

Let $(X,ω)$ be a compact Kähler manifold of complex dimension $n$, and let $1\leq k\leq n$. We consider the space of smooth $k$-admissible potentials introduced in the study of the Hessian-cscK equation by Guo--Smith--Tong. The complex $k$-Hessian equation identifies this space, modulo constants, with the space of smooth positive densities of fixed total mass. We compute the differential of the Hessian density map and use it to pull back the Fisher--Rao metric. The resulting Riemannian metric is \[
 G^{\HC,k}_{\varphi}(u,v)
 =\int_X
 \bigl(Δ_{\varphi}^{(k)}u\bigr)
 \bigl(Δ_{\varphi}^{(k)}v\bigr)
 \,ω_{\varphi}^{k}\wedgeω^{n-k}. \] We then show that the square-root Hessian density map \[
 \varphi\longmapsto
 2\sqrt{\frac{ω_{\varphi}^{k}\wedgeω^{n-k}}{ω^n}} \] is a global Riemannian isometry onto the positive part of the $L^2(X,ω^n)$-sphere of radius $2\sqrt{V}$, where $V=\int_Xω^n$. For $k=n$, this recovers the spherical description of the classical Calabi metric. We also derive the curvature, geodesic and diameter formulas, and prove a quantitative local comparison between adjacent Hessian--Fisher distances.
Sharp radial--angular mixed norm Fourier extension and global stability on spheres

We study the sharp Fourier extension inequality from $L^2(\mathbb S^{d-1})$ to the radial--angular mixed space $L^q_{\mathrm{rad}}L^2_{\mathrm{ang}}$. Our work is motivated by and builds upon the foundational analysis of Carneiro, Oliveira e Silva and Sousa \cite{COS}, who initiated the sharp mixed-norm spherical restriction problem from the viewpoint of spherical-harmonic decomposition. Their reduction revealed that the extremal problem is governed by a competition among the individual harmonic modes, and their results established degree-zero extremizers in several important ranges of exponents, including even integer exponents and the endpoint case. The present paper addresses this question by establishing a complete modal ordering result. Building on their spherical-harmonic reduction, the sharp-constant problem is reduced to the weighted Bessel moments \[ I_{ν,k}(q) := \int_0^\infty |J_{ν+k}(r)|^q r^{2ν+1-νq}\,dr, \qquad ν:=\frac d2-1. \] For every integer $d\ge2$ and every finite admissible exponent $q>2d/(d-1)$, we prove \[ I_{ν,k}(q)<I_{ν,0}(q), \qquad k\ge1, \] and hence constants are the unique nonzero extremizers of the sharp mixed-norm extension inequality. In dimensions $d\ge3$ we prove the stronger strict ordering \[ I_{ν,0}(q)>I_{ν,1}(q)>I_{ν,2}(q)>\cdots. \] We resolve this difficulty by combining exact Hankel asymptotics with a finite remainder comparison.
 The modal ordering also yields the optimal quadratic global stability inequality. For every finite admissible $q$, \[ C_{d,q}^2\|f\|_2^2 -\|\widehat{fσ}\|_{L^q_{\mathrm{rad}}L^2_{\mathrm{ang}}}^2 \ge Γ_{d,q}\|f-P_0f\|_2^2, \] with the best possible coefficient. When $d\ge3$, this coefficient is explicitly \[ Γ_{d,q} =(2π)^d \left[ I_{ν,0}(q)^{2/q}-I_{ν,1}(q)^{2/q} \right]. \]
The Big Match under translation-invariant charges

We study two-player zero-sum stochastic games in which a stream of stage payoffs is evaluated by a translation-invariant charge on the set of stages. Every patient valuation, that is, every diffuse charge that obeys the time value of money principle, is translation-invariant, and by Mertens and Neyman each player has, for every $\varepsilon>0$, a strategy that is $\varepsilon$-optimal for all patient valuations simultaneously. We show that this robustness breaks down for translation-invariant charges. In the Big Match with $0$--$1$ payoffs, whose uniform value is $1/2$, every strategy of Player 1 is worthless: for every strategy of Player 1 and every $δ>0$, Player 2 has a pure reply, and there is a translation-invariant charge under which Player 1's payoff is less than $δ$. Consequently, the Big Match has no value with respect to all translation-invariant charges. This contrasts with finite Markov decision processes, where every stationary Blackwell optimal strategy is optimal for every translation-invariant charge. We pose questions on robust guarantees in general stochastic games and on optimality with respect to a fixed translation-invariant charge.
Model-Induced Hazard Geometry and Functional Representations in Survival Analysis

Individualized survival predictions are often summarized by scalar risk scores or event probabilities at selected time horizons, although clinically relevant risk may also differ in its temporal organization. We consider finite-dimensional representations of individual hazard trajectories through interpretable hazard functionals, such as peak timing, cumulative hazard over prespecified intervals, and persistence of elevated risk.
 A central issue is that the richness of such representations is constrained by the hazard geometry supported by the underlying survival model. We formalize this through model-induced tangent spaces and functional ranks, derive an exact decomposition of model-supported variation into directions retained and lost by a chosen representation, and introduce a model-relative notion of local completeness. We further distinguish intrinsic model capacity from the variation actually activated by covariates.
 These results motivate a structured extension of AFT time scaling through a positive-affine deformation on the log-time scale, yielding a power-warp mechanism with an additional temporal deformation direction. Combined with a log-logistic reference hazard, this gives a parsimonious likelihood-based working specification for which peak timing and peak height provide complete coordinates over the unimodal regime. We also establish plug-in recovery and asymptotic inference for hazard functionals. Simulations and a lung-cancer application illustrate how model-induced restrictions propagate to hazard-functional representations.
What Inverse Problems Can Be Solved Using Neural Networks?
A. S. Leonov; D. V. Lukyanenko

The relationship between classical methods for solving inverse problems and neural network methods is examined. An answer is provided to the question of what inverse problems can be solved using neural networks. The answer is that neural network algorithms can solve only conditionally well-posed problems (well-posed according to Tikhonov). The reason is that the design of standard neural network algorithms violates the well-known Bakushinsky veto from the theory of ill-posed problems. It requires that any method theoretically guaranteeing a stable solution to an ill-posed problem must depend explicitly on the error level of data. The article highlights the distinction between the concept of regularization (RA) in the theory of ill-posed problems and regularization as understood in neural network training, where Bakushinsky's veto is violated. Due to this violation, any changes to the neural network architecture, regularization during training, or training dataset augmentation cannot alter the answer specified above. It is theoretically demonstrated that an ill-posed inverse problem can be solved only by using a parametric set of neural networks that explicitly depend on the known error levels (as parameters) of data. Accordingly, as an alternative to standard neural network algorithms, \neural network based regularization algorithms (NNBRAs) are proposed to solve ill-posed inverse problems. One approach to their construction involves using a regularized dataset. Such a dataset can be generated from perturbed inverse-problem data using a specific base RA explicitly depended on the error level of the data. Test solving the simplest finite-dimensional ill-posed inverse problem demonstrate that the accuracy of the NNBRA approximate solutions is comparable to that of the base RA. At the same time, errors of conventional neural network methods may be unacceptable.
Bei Kang; Lu-Yao Wang; Ke Wu; Wei-Zhong Zhao

By means of $W$-representation, we investigate the Wishart-Laguerre $β$-ensemble and present a compact expression for Catalan polynomials. For a special Nekrasov partition function associated with the Wishart-Laguerre $β$-ensemble, we show that it can be expressed as a exponential form of the special Catalan polynomials. Furthermore, we make a rule to calculate the Catalan polynomials by means of Feynman diagrams and present another expression for Catalan polynomials. We also establish the connection between certain Catalan polynomials and knot theory.
Sharp $L^q$ estimate of adjoint problem and Pucci conjecture

Let $L$ be a linear second-order elliptic operator satisfying a nondegeneracy condition. We establish sharp $L^q$ estimates for solutions of the adjoint problem associated with $L$ and, by duality, derive sharp $L^p$ estimates for solutions of $Lu = f$. In particular, this confirms a conjecture of Carlo Pucci.
Isometries of Unit Spheres of SFS-Spaces and a Geometric Approach to Tingley's Problem
Karimbergen Kudaybergenov; Mukhtar Ibragimov; Allabay Arziev

We investigate surjective isometries between the unit spheres of facially symmetric spaces and their interaction with the underlying facial structure. It is shown that such isometries preserve the essential geometric relations associated with symmetric faces, orthogonality, and geometric tripotents. In particular, a surjective sphere isometry induces a natural correspondence between the geometric tripotents of the underlying spaces and preserves the principal structural features determined by the Peirce decomposition. These results provide a geometric framework for studying linear extension problems for sphere isometries.
 As an application, we establish a positive solution of Tingley's problem for finite-dimensional real neutral strongly facially symmetric spaces satisfying the joint Peirce property. We also obtain an extension result for a wider class of real neutral strongly facially symmetric spaces admitting an appropriate approximation by finite-dimensional Peirce subspaces. In these settings, every surjective isometry between unit spheres extends uniquely to a surjective real-linear isometry of the ambient spaces. The results demonstrate that the facial and tripotent structures play a decisive role in the rigidity of spherical isometries.
Percolative MDLA: phase transition and critical behaviour
Eviatar B. Procaccia; Haoyu Wang; Yuan Zhang

In this paper we introduce the model of Percolative MDLA (PMDLA) on $\mathbb{Z}^2$ which engulfs the entire occupied percolation component of each particle that reaches the aggregate. We prove a phase transition of finite time explosion, as a function of the particle density $λ$, where the critical value equals $λ_c=-\log(1-p_c^{\rm site}(\mathbb{Z}^2))$. Below $λ_c$, the process is nonexplosive and has a linear upper bound on its radius. For $2/3<λ<λ_c$, it also has a linear lower bound on the growth rate. Above $λ_c$, an infinite component is swallowed in finite time a.s. At $λ_c$, every update is finite, but the updates accumulate in finite time, causing a blowup. Excluding criticality, the results are generalized to all higher dimensions.
Sharp Constants, Threshold, and Failure of Uncertainty Principles on Non-trivial Flat Finsler Manifolds

By uncertainty principles we mean the generalized Caffarelli--Kohn--Nirenberg (CKN) inequality and the Heisenberg--Pauli--Weyl (HPW) uncertainty principle, with the latter being an endpoint case and the Hardy inequality a further limiting case. We study these \(L^p\)-type inequalities \((1<p<n)\) on \(n\)-dimensional non-trivial flat Finsler manifolds, which arise from Hilbert's fourth problem. These manifolds are forward complete but not backward complete, projectively flat, with zero flag curvature, and have infinite reversibility, making them highly asymmetric. They are the simplest non-Riemannian, non-Minkowskian solutions to Hilbert's fourth problem, providing a natural framework in which classical inequalities exhibit new behavior.
 For the full class, we establish a sharp threshold at the parameter value \(s=2\): the generalized CKN inequality and the HPW uncertainty principle hold for \(s>2\) but fail completely for \(s\le2\). When the generating Minkowski norm is reversible (while the Finsler metric itself remains irreversible with infinite reversibility), we determine the sharp constants for \(s>2\), which were previously unknown. These constants are approached in the limit by compactly supported radial functions. As a corollary, our results cover Berwald's metric space and resolve the open questions on its sharp constants. These findings reveal that the threshold phenomenon is structural for the entire class and is a genuinely non-Riemannian feature with no analogue in the Riemannian flat case.
The $RO(C_2)$-graded Hurewicz image of Atiyah's Real K-theory
Sihao Ma; Xiaolin Danny Shi; Zhouli Xu; Albert Jinghui Yang; Shangjie Zhang

We determine the $RO(C_2)$-graded $k\mathbb R$-Hurewicz image, where $k \mathbb R$ denotes the connective Atiyah's Real $K$-theory spectrum. As a consequence, we obtain four infinite families in the $RO(C_2)$-graded equivariant stable stems that are $C_2$-equivariant refinements of the classical $μ$-families. Using a $C_2$-equivariant $v_{1,0}$-self map, we explicitly construct an equivariant Adams periodicity operator $P_{C_2}$ that captures these $v_1$-periodicity phenomena in the $C_2$-stable stems.
On the Erdős--Odlyzko--Sárközy conjecture for prime-power moduli

Erdős, Odlyzko and Sárközy conjectured that every reduced residue class modulo $q$ contains a product of two primes not exceeding $q$. O. Klurman, A. P. Mangerel and J. Teräväinen (2023) have shown that three primes suffice when $q$ is sufficiently smooth. We study the moduli $q=p^γ$ that are powers of a fixed prime $p$ and we show that the third prime can be taken subpolynomially small. For any $q_\bullet\le q$ for which $q_\bullet\ge\exp\bigl(C(\log q)^{2/3}(\log\log q)^{4/3}\bigr)$, we give an asymptotic formula for the weighted number of representations of each reduced class as a product of two primes not exceeding $q$ and a third not exceeding~$q_\bullet$. We also show that the conjecture holds for all but a proportion $\exp\bigl(-c(\log q)^{1/3}(\log\log q)^{-1/3}\bigr)$ of the reduced classes. Here $C$ and $c$ are positive constants that depend only on $p$. Both results are unconditional and they rely on a wide zero-free region with no exceptional zeros for the Dirichlet $L$-functions attached to characters modulo $p^γ$.We also present conditional versions of these results for arbitrary $q$ under a quasi-Riemann hypothesis.
On the Isomorphism of Semicircular Algebras

Building on OpenAI's proof of isomorphism of free group factors, we give a self-contained proof of a corresponding result for $C^{*}$-algebras generated by free semicircular systems: the isomorphism class of a $C^{*}$-algebra generated by a semicircular $n$-tuple does not depend on $n\in\{2,3,\dots,+\infty\}$. Similarly, reduced free products of $n$ copies of the Jiang--Su algebra are isomorphic for different $n$ in this range. While reduced free group $C^{*}$-algebras of different ranks are not isomorphic (by a result of Pimsner--Voiculescu), we show that they have strong free absorption properties. At the heart of the proof is an automorphism approximation property for inclusions of $C^{*}$- and $W^{*}$-algebras; a relative version of that property was previously used to derive free complementation results.
A short open space curve of unit width
Tinko Sebastian Bartels; Dennis Kevin Choy; Ruixiang Wu; Tongxin Li

In this work, we propose a curve to be a minimum of length among rectifiable, continuous curves of unit width in three-dimensional Euclidean space. We show that a previously conjectured minimizer of that problem is not of unit width, give the numerical derivation of a candidate family of unit width curves, prove that it admits a strict local minimum within that candidate family and that this minimum is of unit width and length $3.905124162243593\ldots$. The curve consists of eight straight segments, two cone geodesics, and three circular helices. Its parameters are specified by a uniquely isolated solution of the joining and stationarity equations. To establish unit width in every direction, we combine analytic estimates with interval arithmetic on a finite covering of the remaining directions. We conjecture that the curve is globally minimizing. We supplement this work with the programs used to identify the candidates, replicate the computer-assisted parts of our proof, as well as a formalization of our proof in Lean.
Maximizing Reaction via Spatial Localization: A PDE-Constrained Variational Approach
Mohammad Yasir Feroz Khan; Bo Li

We study a PDE-constrained variational problem for the optimal spatial distribution of a catalytic material reacting with a substrate in a biological or materials system. With a given catalyst concentration, the substrate concentration is determined by a reaction-diffusion equation. The reaction functional for the catalyst concentrations is defined to be the total reaction output, which is the product of catalyst and substrate concentrations. Both the linear and Michaelis-Menten reaction kinetics are considered. We construct reaction-maximizing sequences through the localization of catalysts using barrier functions and show the non-existence of a global maximizer. We also derive the first and second variations of the reaction functional. By constructing a competing catalyst concentration, we show the non-existence of a local maximizer. Based on our analysis, we propose a regularized variational model and prove the existence of its global maximizer.
The Density and Quantitative Upper Bound of Integers Not Expressible as the Sum of a Prime and a Zumkeller Number

A Zumkeller number is a positive integer whose set of positive divisors can be partitioned into two disjoint subsets of equal sums. In this paper, we investigate the additive properties of these numbers in conjunction with prime numbers. Specifically, we study the natural density of the exceptional set \(\mathcal{E}\) consisting of all positive integers not expressible as the sum of a prime and a Zumkeller number. Let $α(x) = \#\{n \le x : n \in \mathcal{E}\}$ denote its counting function. We establish a quantitative upper bound for $α(x)$, demonstrating that $α(x) \ll x(\log \log x)^{-A}$, where $A = \log_2\left(\frac{2π^2}{2π^2-3}\right) \approx 0.2378$, thereby proving that the natural density of this exceptional set is $0$.
On Inherent Privacy of Posterior Sampling: A Unified Rényi-Divergence Framework

Differential Privacy (DP) provides a rigorous framework for quantifying privacy guarantees. While most methods achieve DP by injecting calibrated random noise, the intrinsic randomness of certain procedures such as sampling can yield DP guarantees ``for free''. In this work, we develop a unified Rényi divergence framework to characterize the inherent DP guarantees of sampling from a Bayesian posterior distribution. We show that the privacy loss incurred by One-Posterior-Sampling (OPS) is governed by posterior exponential moments of the single-record log-likelihood ratio, and establish explicit DP guarantees under uniformly bounded, sub-Gaussian, or sub-exponential tail regimes. We apply the framework to representative Bayesian models, including categorical likelihoods with arbitrary priors, Gaussian-Gaussian conjugate pair, generalized linear models from the exponential family and linear regression with Gaussian likelihood, both with Gaussian priors on the regression coefficients. Our results elucidate sample size, model structure, neighboring relations in DP (bounded or unbounded), and how prior if applicable, jointly determine the inherent DP guarantees of OPS. Furthermore, our results recover the existing DP guarantees for OPS as special cases -- often with tighter privacy loss bounds -- and substantially broaden the class of Bayesian models for which the inherent DP guarantees of OPS can be rigorously characterized.
The Two-Level Poset Game is PSPACE-Complete

Poset games form a fundamental class of combinatorial games that includes classical games such as Nim and Chomp. Determining the outcome of a poset game is known to be PSPACE-complete even for posets of height at most three. However, the exact computational complexity of Two-Level Poset Game, played on posets of height at most two, has remained an open problem for over a decade. We resolve this problem by proving that Two-Level Poset Game is PSPACE-complete via a polynomial-time reduction from Avoid True on positive CNF formulas.
Continuous Narayana Interpolations: Hankel Total Positivity and Log-Convexity Preservation

We study a continuous interpolation between the type $B$ and shifted type $A$ Narayana triangles and its extension through affine moments of the continuous $q$-ultraspherical (Rogers) measure. For every fixed $0<q<1$ and $-1<β<1$, these affine moments form a coefficientwise Hankel-totally positive sequence in the polynomial variable $t$. The proof rests on a general continuant criterion: decreasing nonnegative off-diagonal weights and coefficientwise positivity of the leading continuants imply total positivity of the full tridiagonal matrix. A telescoping identity gives positive certificates for shifted continuants and stability under coordinatewise decreases of the weights. We determine the exact power of $t$, palindromicity, and extreme coefficients of arbitrary Hankel minors. Classical limits recover the continuous Narayana family, including its moment representation and gamma positivity. We further prove that the continuous Narayana transformations preserve strong $t$-log-convexity for every real $θ\ge0$, and that the $d$-Hoggatt transformations have the same preservation property for every integer $d\ge1$. The preservation proofs use the Zhu--Sun criterion and a mixed-minor one-sign-change argument whose local ingredient is a hypergeometric hitting-probability inequality.
Shrinking targets versus recurrence: A survey on the Hausdorff dimension theory
Zhang-nan Hu; Jun-jie Huang; Bing Li

This survey reviews results on the Hausdorff dimension of shrinking target sets and recurrence sets in dynamical systems. In their basic formulations, shrinking target sets concern orbits approaching a prescribed centre, whereas recurrence sets concern orbits returning close to their initial points. A central theme is the comparison of the Hausdorff dimensions of these two classes of limsup sets. The dynamical systems considered include expanding conformal systems, irrational rotations, affine iterated function systems, and matrix transformations. Related results on Hausdorff measure are also included when they provide natural refinements of the dimension theory. Finally, we review results on badly approximating orbits and non-recurrent sets, with particular attention to winning properties and intersections with self-conformal and self-affine sets.
Normalized Orbit Frames and Essential Spectrum, II

Given $0<r_{j}<1$ with $r_{j}\to1$, there exist a normal operator $T$ on $\ell^{2}$ with eigenvalues $λ_{j}$ satisfying $|λ_{j}|=r_{j}$ and $g\in\ell^{2}$ such that \[ \left\{ \frac{T^{n}g}{\left\Vert T^{n}g\right\Vert }\right\} _{n\geq0}\text{is a frame}\:\Longleftrightarrow\:\sum_{j\geq1}\left(1-r^{2}_{j}\right)=\infty. \] Whenever this condition holds, the frame bounds can be chosen with ratio arbitrarily close to one.

Consider the one-dimensional nonlinear stochastic heat equation $$ \frac{\partial u(t,x)}{\partial t} =
\frac{\partial^2 u(t,x)}{\partial x^2} +
σ(u(t,x))\dot W(t,x), \qquad t>0,\ x\in\mathbb R, $$ where $\dot W$ is a Gaussian noise that is white in time and fractional in space with Hurst parameter $H\in(1/4,1/2)$. Hu et al. ({\it Ann. Probab.} {\bf 45} (2017), 4561--4616) established existence and uniqueness of the solution under the assumptions that $σ$ is differentiable, both $σ$ and $σ'$ are Lipschitz continuous, and $σ(0)=0$. Hu and Wang ({\it Ann. Inst. Henri Poincaré Probab. Stat.} {\bf 58} (2022), 379--423) subsequently removed the technical condition $σ(0)=0$ by developing the well-posedness theory in a suitable weighted space associated with the weight $λ(x)= c_H (1 + |x|^2)^{H-1}$.

The main difficulty lies in handling the nonlocal fractional-difference structure induced by the rough spatial noise. We address this difficulty using weighted heat-kernel increment estimates. These approximations yield exact Lévy-type uniform moduli of continuity in both time and space, together with Khinchin and Chung laws of the iterated logarithm.
On a problem on partitions into distinct primes

For a positive integer $n$, we write $L(n)$ in place of the maximum number of distinct primes whose sum is $n$, assuming there is a way of writing $n$ as a sum of distinct primes, with $L(n) = 0$ otherwise. Again if $n$ admits a partition into distinct primes, then we let $K(n)$ denote the number of parts in the unique partition that has a largest product, with $K(n) = 0$ otherwise. In the latest editions of Guy's classic text on unsolved problems in number theory, the problem as to whether or not $L(n) - K(n)$ is unbounded was left open, and it appears that this has remained open. We solve this problem in the affirmative. Our proof relies, to a large extent, on a consequence of Vinogradov's theorem together with a 1948 result due to Sierpiński on the existence of primes whose gaps to the immediately preceding and following primes both exceed any prescribed positive bound.
Markov maps and quasi-conformal deformations associated to geometrically finite Kleinian groups

It is known that the dynamical properties of Kleinian groups with parabolic elements are much more complex than those without parabolic elements. In this paper, we mainly study the quasi-conformal deformation properties of geometrically finite Kleinian groups with parabolic elements. We show that, for a Kleinian group $G$ with parabolic elements, there exists a subset $K$ of the limit set $Λ(G)$ such that the first return map $f_{K}$ is (eventually) expending. Furthermore, the expending property is invariant under quasiconformal deformations. As an application, we show that the geometrically finite Kleinian groups have Ruelle's property. Finally, we use eigenvalue algorithm to calculate the precise Hausdorff dimensions of Hecke groups, which serves as an example to support our results.

We establish nearly sharp $W^{1,\infty}$ stability estimates for the Legendre spectral Ritz projection associated with Laplacian on a square domain. Its norm grows proportionally to the square root of the polynomial degree, up to a cubic logarithmic factor. The upper bound uses an integral representation of the discrete gradient projection in terms of one-dimensional semigroup kernels and a rank-two Duhamel comparison between the mass-matrix semigroup and its infinite-dimensional counterpart. The lower bound follows from the endpoint concentration of the Legendre kernel. As an application, we derive gradient maximum-norm error estimates for the Poisson and heat equations, with spatial factors optimal up to logarithmic terms.
A Stabilized CR-CR Method for Fourth-Order Elliptic Problems

We present a CR-CR method for strain gradient elasticity and prove its robustness with respect to the Lame parameter $λ$ and the length scale $ι$. The method introduces the strain as an independent symmetric tensor and discretizes both the strain and the displacement using CR elements. The commuting properties of the CR interpolation operator with the relevant differential operators leads the robustness with respect to $λ$. A stabilization term weakly imposes the relation between the strain and the symmetric gradient of the displacement. The method also applies directly to the biharmonic equation and singularly perturbed fourth-order problems. For these problems, we prove that the CR-CR method is equivalent to an RT-CR method proposed by Huang and Tang. This result extends the classical equivalence between the RT-P0 mixed method and the CR method for the Poisson equation to fourth-order problems. The equivalence shows that the stabilization term arises naturally from the RT-CR mixed formulation.
High-Probability Regret Bounds for Feel-Good Thompson Sampling

Feel-good Thompson sampling (FGTS) augments the posterior of vanilla Thompson sampling with an exploration term that favors reward functions with high predicted optimal values. This modification achieves minimax-optimal regret up to logarithmic factors in linear contextual bandits, but existing analyses of its two standard variants establish regret guarantees in expectation. In this paper, we derive the first high-probability regret bounds for both cumulative and current-step FGTS in contextual bandits with general realizable function approximation. Our bounds depend on the corresponding decoupling coefficients and the prior mass near the true reward function. In the $d$-dimensional linear setting, both variants satisfy $\mathrm{Regret}(T)=O\big(d\sqrt T\log(2T)+\sqrt T\log(1/δ)\big)$ with probability at least $1-δ$, where $T$ is the time horizon. This bound matches the dimension and horizon dependence of algorithms based on the upper confidence bounds, up to logarithmic factors. Relative to the expected-regret guarantees, the cost of controlling the regret with high probability is confined to additive terms with at most linear dependence on $\log(1/δ)$. The proof ideas are partially developed by GPT-6 Astra under the authors' guidance.
Arithmetic Visibility in Polygons: Curved Sight in the Art Gallery

In the classical art gallery problem, a guard sees a target when the segment joining them lies entirely within the polygon. We explore what changes when sight may bend along regular arcs on absolutely irreducible curves, but only those defined by primitive integer polynomials of total degree at most \(d\) and coefficient height at most \(H\). We call such curves admissible sight carriers.

For instance, in an alternating comb, the number of guards needed for a row of targets spanning the comb grows linearly with the number of sides at each fixed degree, even for carriers with arbitrary real coefficients. Arithmetically, no admissible carrier may pass through the points at all. We show that every finite set of algebraic targets in a rational polygon becomes visible from any rational interior guard, with explicit bounds. We also construct, for every \(d\), arbitrarily large Galois orbits in the unit square, all of projective height \(4^{d+1}\), whose points must each guard themselves at degree \(d\) for every \(H\). We formulate a finite-length conjecture under an explicit auxiliary-degree hypothesis and a separate termwise conjecture for the correction residues of one-sided iterates. We prove reductions to the $k=0$ strip and to last vacuum mode $-1$, recover the length-one relation spaces, and give explicit Virasoro computations at word length two for $n=1$ and $n=2$. The $Y_L$ identities are the input for the companion paper (Part II).
Digital Self-Interference Cancellation for In-Band Full-Duplex Systems Based on Transformer Neural Operators

Digital-domain self-interference cancellation is essential in in-band full-duplex radios after passive suppression and analog cancellation. In this regime, conventional iterative digital cancellers update their coefficients from desired-signal-contaminated received samples and may suffer substantial performance degradation. This paper reformulates digital-domain self-interference cancellation as an operator-learning problem. The proposed framework learns the temporal evolution of the residual self-interference channel from historical observations and uses the learned operator together with the known local transmit signal to reconstruct the current residual self-interference. A Transformer neural operator is used to realize this framework. The resulting method is trained in a desired-signal-free setting and then applied in the presence of a desired signal. A continuity-based analysis characterizes the sensitivity of the learned operator to the resulting input perturbation. A nonequilibrium-capturing unified gas-kinetic scheme I: discrete orthogonal basis construction and expansion on velocity space

A fixed velocity grid often retains redundant kinetic degrees of freedom (DOFs), particularly under near equilibrium conditions. For unsteady flows, the explicit scheme achieves speedups of 12.64 to 58.50 over the standard UGKS. In steady state tests, only about $2\%$ of the original kinetic DOFs are required in continuum regions, accelerating each implicit iteration by a factor of 33.87. We study factorized gradient descent (FGD) for overparameterized asymmetric matrix sensing with the balancing regularizer $\frac18\|L^\top L-R^\top R\|_F^2$. An exact indefinite lifting of the population objective decomposes the dynamics of FGD into positive, negative, and null spectral subspaces. The first two components have linear restoring terms, whereas the null component contracts only quadratically. For independent isotropic sub-Gaussian sensing matrices and independent centered sub-Gaussian noise with scale proxy $σ$, we prove the local bound \[
 \|L_tR_t^\top-X^\star\|_2
 \lesssim\max\left\{\frac{1}{ηt+1/σ_r},
 κσ\sqrt{\frac{d_1+d_2}{n}}\right\}, \] under a sufficiently small initialization error, the number of linear measurements $n\gtrsimκ^2(d_1+d_2)\max\{k^2,σ^2/σ_r^2\}$, and step size $η\lesssimσ_1^{-1}$. Wouter van Doorn; Pietro Monticone; Melvyn B. Nathanson

A set $A$ of integers is an $h$-basis for $n$ if every integer in $[0,n] = \{0,1,2,\ldots,n\}$ belongs to the sumset $hA$, that is, can be represented as the sum of exactly $h$ not necessarily distinct elements of $A$. The classical postage stamp problem asks for the largest integer $n_h(k)$ such that $[0,n_h(k)] \subseteq hA$ for some set $A$ of nonnegative integers of size $k+1$. We consider the effect of allowing negative elements. Let $n^{\flat}_h(k)$ be the largest integer such that $[0,n^{\flat}_h(k)] \subseteq hA$ for some set $A$ of integers of size $k+1$ containing at least one negative integer. For $k=2$, we have $n^{\flat}_h(2) < n_h(2)$ if $h$ is odd or $h=4$ and $n^{\flat}_h(2) = n_h(2)$ if $h$ is even and $h \neq 4$. Proofs of these comparison results were autonomously discovered and formally verified in Lean by https://aristotle.harmonic.fun/}{Aristotle}, a formal reasoning agent developed by https://www.harmonic.fun/}{Harmonic}. In this paper we give new proofs of these results.

Let $M$ be a complete Riemannian manifold and define a magnetic Schrödinger operator $\LL = ({\bf d}+ iA)^*({\bf d}+iA) + V$ where $A$ is a real $1$-differential form in $L^2_{loc}$ and $V \in L^1_{loc}$ is a nonnegative electric potential.

It extends to a bounded operator on $L^p$ for $p \in (1, 2]$ with norm bounded by a constant $c_p$ depending only on $p$. It is then independent of the dimension of the manifold and independent of $A$ and $V$. We also prove weak type $(1,1)$ bounds for symmetric elliptic operators subject to various boundary conditions on rough domains of $\RR^d$. The proofs are based on a new weak type $(1,1)$ criterion for operators.

In this paper, we establish sparse bounds for singular integral operators with rough non-translation-invariant Calderón-Zygmund kernels.

Motivated by the relative-slice problem in $4$-manifold topology, we define for a knot $R$ the notion of a relative knot concordance group $\mathcal{C}_R$ and analyze the structure of its algebraic analogue $\mathcal{AC}_R$ modulo torsion. Using Milnor signatures, we show that $\mathcal{AC}_R$ has infinite rank for every $R$. We also show that any prescribed finite set of natural numbers can be realized as orders of elements in a single relative concordance group.

We prove a folklore conjecture on exponential sums with multiplicative coefficients: if $f$ is multiplicative with $|f(n)|\le1$, $(a,q)=1$, $|α-a/q|\le q^{-2}$ and $q\le N/(\log N)^2$, then \[

Let $\LL = -Δ+ V$ be a Schrödinger operator with a non-negative potential. We prove explicit positive corrections to the Dirichlet and Neumann Pólya inequalities at every positive eigenvalue index of every annular sector. Real-order angular integration preserves the exact area term, while directional rounding estimates and radial trials control all frequencies. We derive the code dimension from the greatest common divisors of the entries and minors, with a simplified formula for odd lifting factors. A residue characterization identifies additional common factors of the minors and leads to a method for controlling the dimension through polynomial selection. The problem of Private Information Retrieval (PIR) across graph-based replicated systems has seen a surge of interest in recent literature. In such systems, servers are modeled as the vertices of a graph, and each file is represented by an edge connecting the pair of servers that store it. While previous research on Graph-PIR (G-PIR) has focused mostly on perfect information-theoretic privacy, relaxing this constraint has the potential for significantly higher retrieval rates. In this work, we consider the setting of Graph-based Weak Private Information Retrieval (G-WPIR), under an $ε$-privacy metric. We adapt an existing G-WPIR scheme for arbitrary graphs to analyze its performance under the $ε$-privacy metric. Additionally, we establish a lower bound on the expected download cost for arbitrary graphs under the $ε$-privacy metric and derive from it an explicit rate upper bound for complete graphs. Finally, we show the achievable rate-privacy trade-offs for two specific graph classes---complete graphs and complete bipartite graphs.
New Qualitative and Quantitative Estimates for Neumann Eigenvalues toward Pólya's Conjecture
Xiang He; Renjin Jiang; Fanghua Lin; Zuoqin Wang

We introduce the Enhanced Neumann Pólya inequality, which is stronger than Pólya's conjecture, and verify it for many classes of domains, including strip-tiling domains, Euclidean balls, thin product domains, and certain higher-dimensional tiling domains. We develop a geometric removal approach for the Enhanced Neumann Pólya inequality.

A key ingredient is a joint energy estimate for the full density and the non-zero-mode vorticity, which preserves the positive nonlinear diffusion and avoids the mixed diffusion terms arising from separate estimates of the density modes. We study two explicit constructions of binary Calderbank--Shor--Steane quantum low-density parity-check (QLDPC) codes with check weight six. Every cubic graph has four total dominating sets covering each vertex at most twice

In 2018, Goddard and Henning conjectured that every cubic graph has four total dominating sets covering each vertex at most twice, and asked the analogous question for transversals of $3$-uniform $3$-regular hypergraphs. We prove the conjecture, which also answers the question in the affirmative.
Fourier-Mukai transforms by a family of stable sheaves and preservation of stability
For a Fourier-Mukai transform whose kernel is a family of Gieseker stable sheaves, we shall give a condition for the preservation of Gieseker stability of sheaves.

Random reshuffling stochastic gradient descent (RR-SGD) is widely used for finite-sum optimization in machine learning. For convex $L$-smooth components, recent work establishes convergence guarantees for an averaged iterate with component stepsizes as large as order $1/L$. However, the final iterate is a natural output in practice, and existing last-iterate guarantees in this setting require stepsizes that scale inversely with the number of components $n$. We establish an expected objective-gap bound for the last iterate of standard RR-SGD on unconstrained problems with a constant component stepsize satisfying $0<η\lesssim 1/(L(1 + \log(nK)))$, where $K$ is the number of epochs. By retaining the sampling bias at random comparison points, we remove the explicit $1/n$ factor from the stepsize restriction. Combined with existing small-step bounds, our result matches the corresponding averaged-iterate convergence rate up to logarithmic factors.
Birational maps of moduli spaces of stable sheaves on a K3 surface induced by Fourier-Mukai transforms
We shall study birational maps of moduli spaces of stable sheaves on a K3 surface with Picard number 1 induced by Fourier-Mukai transforms.
A pure source transfer domain decomposition method for Helmholtz equations in 3D unbounded domain

We develop and analyze a three-dimensional pure source transfer domain decomposition method (PSTDDM) for the Helmholtz equation in free space. Extending the two-dimensional PSTDDM proposed by [Du and Wu, J. Sci. Comput., 83(2020),83:68], the proposed method transfers sources successively along the $x_1$, $x_2$, and $x_3$ directions, yielding layer-wise, bar-wise, and block-wise PSTDDMs. The main challenge in the convergence analysis is deriving wavenumber-explicit truncation-error estimates. To address this challenge, we establish inf--sup conditions for the uniaxial perfectly matched layer (UPML) problem under relaxed restrictions on the PML parameters and reformulate the source-transfer operators. We then introduce a positive-definite reconstruction step that produces a globally conforming approximation. In addition, a new quantitative lower bound is established for the imaginary part of the complex PML distance, more easily yielding exponential decay estimates in three dimensions. These lead to wavenumber-explicit convergence estimates for all three PSTDDMs. Numerical experiments demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed methods both as direct solvers and as preconditioners for GMRES.

Let $p$ be an odd prime, and let $ρ\colon G\to \GSp_{2n}(\Z_p)$ be an irreducible symplectic residually multiplicity free representation. We define the symplectic extension graph $Γ_ρ^\GSp$ associated with $ρ$ to be the directed graph whose vertices are the residual factors of $ρ$ and a directed edge between two vertices corresponds to a nonsplit extension between the vertices realized by $ρ$. Using the Euclidean Bruhat--Tits building associated with $\GSp_{2n}(\Q_p)$, under some assumptions, we prove the existence of certain paths in $Γ_ρ^\GSp$ and show that $Γ_ρ^\GSp$ is a disjoint union of nonempty strongly connected subgraphs. Moreover, we provide examples to show that the result we obtain is optimal.
A potential projection method for the nonlinear Schrödinger equation with low regularity potential

We propose a potential projection (PP) method for the nonlinear Schrödinger equation (NLSE) with low-regularity and singular potentials by replacing the potential with its Fourier projection (truncated Fourier series). This gives rise to an NLSE with projected potential (NLSEwPP). We rigorously establish its well-posedness under low-regularity potentials, and its convergence to the original NLSE. Numerically, TS-PP-FP consistently achieves optimal temporal and spatial convergence rates with respect to the regularity of the exact solution under low-regularity and even singular potentials. Compared with the time-splitting Fourier spectral method, TS-PP-FP attains the same convergence rates at significantly lower computational cost and preserves the mass conservation and time symmetry (that are lost in the Fourier spectral discretization of the time-splitting method); compared with the time-splitting FP method, it is substantially more accurate for low-regularity potentials with the same computational cost.
Dirac Points in High-Contrast Dielectric Honeycomb Structures
Yi Huang; Bowen Li; Ping Liu

Softplus Affine(1, 1) Processes: Enlarged Stationarity Region, Stationary Unit Roots, and Inference

At a stationary unit root, the conditional mean has a power-law tail with an explicit index, and the observations can exhibit long memory. At the unit root, these results require only a finite mean and yield standard Wald inference even when the observations have infinite variance or long memory. The proof first establishes homogeneity of the spectrum from the weak exponential approximation rate. A closure theorem for reflectionless Jacobi matrices then transfers reflectionlessness from the periodic approximants to the limit, and a theorem of Poltoratski and Remling rules out singular spectrum on a homogeneous set.

We prove an endpoint Pucci maximum principle for domains in $\mathbb R^2$, formulated using a generalization of elementary symmetric polynomials to noninteger orders. As a result, we sharpen an earlier result of Astala, Iwaniec and Martin, and deduce a new Sobolev inequality for $q$-Hessians where $1 < q < 2$. In each case, the analysis separates the continuous convolution error from the error introduced by discretization. The contribution of kernel energy to the error exposes the dimensional dependence of tensor-product kernels and motivates our weight-adapted ANOVA constructions. Under suitable summability conditions on the weights, we establish convolution error and kernel energy estimates that yield dimension-uniform error bounds for the resulting quasi-interpolants. Numerical experiments corroborate the theoretical convergence rates and illustrate the effect of coordinate weighting on dimensional dependence.

We study symmetric 2-(v, k, λ) designs admitting a flag-transitive point-primitive subgroup G of automorphisms, where gcd(k, λ) = p and p is a prime. In this paper, we show that G is of affine or almost simple type.

We introduce a $q$-analogue of the bicolored Eulerian quasisymmetric functions by incorporating an additional grading arising from affine length, obtained by interpreting bicolored permutations as affine permutations. We also provide an intrinsic description of this refinement in terms of bicolored permutations by introducing notions of alignments and crossings, together with an explicit bijection identifying these statistics with the alignments and crossings in the existing literature. Finally, we prove that our refinement is symmetric by expressing it in terms of the Theta operators appearing in the Theta coinvariant Conjecture and the modified Macdonald symmetric functions. Assuming the Theta coinvariant conjecture implies the Schur-positivity of our refinement.

Let $F: \mathbb{R}^2 \to \mathbb{R}^2$ be a polynomial map with nowhere zero Jacobian determinant. It is known that the global invertibility of $F$ is equivalent to the pullback of a parallel vector field being parallel. In this paper, we construct the phase portraits on the Poincaré disc of the pullbacks of the canonical annular, radial, and strip vector fields under non-injective maps $F$ that have recently appeared in the literature. Our arguments use local and global properties of vector fields as well as local and global properties of functions, thereby connecting techniques from dynamical systems and singularity theory.

In this paper we study the behavior of transformer networks generating text over long periods of time. We show that even a three-token, single-layer attention-only transformer can fail to converge. We then study a rich class of transformers with arbitrary finite depth, layer normalization, MLPs, RoPE encodings, and an arbitrary mix of local and global layers. We show further that, while each transformer has a temperature threshold, the supremum of this set is infinite, so there is no global minimal temperature that forces all transformers to converge.

In this article, we approach the Arnold corank problem posed by Arnold himself in 1975, which asks whether the corank of a holomorphic function is a topological invariant. Here, the corank of a holomorphic function is the corank of its Hessian matrix at 0, which is one of the most basic and fundamental invariants of a holomorphic function. Here, we prove the topological invariance of the corank mod 2. Consequently, we obtain another proof of the Arnold corank problem in dimension 3, which was recently proved by Fernandes, Jelonek, and the author of this article. We also prove that the corank is constant in a continuous family of holomorphic functions with isolated singularities and constant Milnor number. We also approach a conjecture recently posed by Budur, Fernández de Bobadilla, Lê, and Nguyen (2022), which states that if two germs of holomorphic functions are right topologically equivalent, then the Milnor fibers of their initial forms are homotopy equivalent. We prove that a (much) weaker version of this conjecture, which states that if two holomorphic functions are right topologically equivalent, then the Milnor fibers of their initial forms have the same Euler characteristic, is equivalent to the Zariski multiplicity conjecture for right topological equivalence. Here $κα_c(κ)$ is the critical inverse temperature of the Curie-Weiss-Potts model. A comparison of color profiles transfers this limit to the unconstrained model for $β<β_{\max}(κ)$, an explicit threshold. In the same range, the magnetizations of two replicas and their overlap matrix satisfy a joint quenched central limit theorem with independent Gaussian limits. The fourth cumulant of the disorder enters the limiting mean and variance explicitly.

Although pointwise root-$n$ inference is possible under standard conditions, we show that this need not translate into locally reliable inference. Imposing a uniform bound on a minimum-norm solution restores Hellinger continuity under regularity conditions, but does not by itself ensure stable root-n inference. If, in addition, both inverse problems are ill-posed and the solution whose norm is uniformly bounded is nonunique at a law $P_0$, then under regularity conditions the target fails to be pathwise differentiable; consequently, asymptotically linear estimators exhibit nonvanishing root-$n$ bias under some local alternatives, causing Wald confidence intervals to undercover asymptotically. Uniqueness of Limit Cycles for Abel Equations and Planar Systems

We prove that contact $(+1)$-surgery along a Legendrian $n$-sphere $Λ\subset(\mathbb{S}^{2n+1},ξ_{\mathrm{std}})$ with \[ \mathrm{tb}(Λ)\ne (-1)^{\frac{n(n-1)}{2}+1} \] has vanishing contact homology. Comput., 2024] and shows that, regardless of the distribution of the snapshot points, the convergence is always (asymptotically) exponential in the number of snapshot points if the function $A(p)$ admits an analytical extension. Simulation Based Inference of a Simple Neural Network Structure
