In an earlier article, the author showed that, if $ϕ\in H^2$, then \[ f\in\mathcal{H}(b) \iff \Bigl(f\in H^2 \text{ and }\sum_{m\ge0}\Bigl|\sum_{n\ge0}\overline{\hatϕ(n)}\hat{f}(m+n)\Bigr|^2<\infty\Bigr), \] in which case we have \[ \|f\|_{\mathcal{H}(b)}^2=\sum_{m\ge0}|\hat{f}(m)|^2 +\sum_{m\ge0}\Bigl|\sum_{n\ge0}\overline{\hatϕ(n)}\hat{f}(m+n)\Bigr|^2. \] It was also shown that there exists a space $\mathcal{H}(b)$ for which $ϕ\in\cap_{p<2}H^p$, yet \[ f\in\mathcal{H}(b)\not\Rightarrow \sum_{m\ge0}\Bigl|\sum_{n\ge0}\overline{\hatϕ(n)}\hat{f}(m+n)\Bigr|^2<\infty. \] Here we complete this circle of ideas by showing that there exists a space $\mathcal{H}(b)$ for which $ϕ\in\cap_{p<1}H^p$, yet \[ \Bigl(f\in H^2\text{ and } \sum_{m\ge0}\Bigl|\sum_{n\ge0}\overline{\hatϕ(n)}\hat{f}(m+n)\Bigr|^2<\infty\Bigr) \not\Rightarrow f\in\mathcal{H}(b). \]
Nonstandard combinatorial ultrafilters and a new local witness model

A central object in the theory of proof complexity generators is Krajicek's local witness model. We construct a new such model as a definable ultrapower using a definable version of a selective ultrafilter over a model of arithmetic. We transfer some set theory of combinatorial ultrafilters to the definable nonstandard setting.
Non-uniqueness for McKean--Vlasov SDEs with Hölder diffusion coefficients
Martin Bergerhausen; Paul Nikolaev; David J. Prömel

We show that uniqueness may fail for one-dimensional McKean--Vlasov stochastic differential equations with Hölder continuous diffusion coefficients. More precisely, for every \(α\in(1/2,1)\), we construct an equation with a diffusion coefficient that is \(α\)-Hölder continuous in the state variable, Lipschitz continuous in the measure variable, and of linear growth, for which uniqueness in law and pathwise uniqueness fail. The construction relies on a spreading estimate together with a Schauder fixed-point argument.
An Exact Branch-Price-and-Cut Algorithm for a Truck-as-Hub Vehicle Routing Problem with Drones
Fan Pu; Sivakumar Rathinam; Yunlong Zhang; Xiaopeng Li; Xiubin Wang; Yang Zhou

Rural last-mile logistics remains challenging because of sparse demand, limited road infrastructure, and long travel distances. We study a Truck-as-Hub Vehicle Routing Problem with Drones in Rural Areas, in which multiple trucks each carry a dedicated fleet of drones. Drone launch and retrieval are restricted to predesignated passive synchronization pads, where a visiting truck temporarily acts as a mobile hub, may dispatch multiple drones simultaneously, and must wait until all launched drones return before continuing its route. We formulate a mixed-integer quadratic programming model that jointly accounts for customer delivery delays, truck return times, and operating costs. To solve the problem exactly, we transform the original truck--drone network so that each feasible route can be represented as a single path and develop a branch-price-and-cut algorithm with tailored pricing, cutting, branching, and parallel-computing procedures. Computational experiments show that the proposed algorithm proves optimality for most large-scale test cases and achieves optimality gaps of no more than 4% for the remaining cases, whereas Gurobi reaches the 1,800-second time limit on all large-scale instances when applied directly to the compact formulation. Sensitivity analyses show that drone operating costs and managerial priorities substantially affect drone utilization and customer delays, providing practical guidance for balancing service quality and operating cost in rural delivery systems.
A Half-Space Theorem for the Allen--Cahn Equation in All Dimensions
We prove that, in every dimension, a bounded, non-constant entire solution of the Allen--Cahn equation whose zero set is contained in a half-space is a one-dimensional heteroclinic solution.
Stability in the determination of the coefficients for coupled relativistic Schrödinger system
Nitesh Kumar; Parveen Kumar; Tanmay Sarkar

In this article, we prove a stability result for the identification of the coefficients appearing in a coupled relativistic Schrödinger system posed on a bounded domain of $\mathbb{R}^{1+n}$, where $n \geq 3$. More precisely, by utilizing input-output operator, where Neumann boundary data are available only on a subset of the boundary, and constructing an appropriate geometric optics solution, we derive a stability estimate of $\log$-$\log$ type for the matrix-valued first-order coefficients. This result is subsequently used to obtain a $\log$-$\log$-$\log$ type stability estimate for the zeroth-order matrix-valued potential.
Anomaly Flow II: Estimates and Long-time Existence for the Coupled Flow

In this follow-up to \cite{Sua25}, we extend the results to the coupled anomaly flow which incorporates the evolution of a Hermitian metric on a holomorphic vector bundle over a compact complex $3$-fold with general slope parameter $α'$. This yields a similar sufficient smallness condition on the slope parameter $α'$ in order to extend the flow on $[0, τ)$ to $[0, τ+ ε)$. We also augment the argument of \cite{Sua25} slightly to fix the peculiarity of the units in the condition for $α'$ for the $k = 1$ case.
DisCo Algebra: Why Disintegration and Combination Are Not Inverses

We present DisCo algebra---a compositional framework for joint probability built from a symmetric cooperad (disintegration) and a symmetric operad (combination) on the bare family $\mathcal{P}_n=\mathrm{Prob}([0,1]^n)$. No probability integral transform, no external summary functions, no enrichment of objects with conditional kernels. The disintegration side uses block-wise joint CDFs as intrinsic, measure-determined 1D summaries, yielding a lossy compression. The combination side reads the same summaries and reconstructs via regular conditional measures, yielding a lossless embedding. We prove that combination followed by disintegration is the identity on admissible inputs, but disintegration followed by combination is not---the information loss is exactly the conditional KL divergence between the true conditional distribution and the conditionally independent product. This asymmetry reveals a hard limit on how much cross-block dependence can be captured by scalar block summaries.
Exponential Green energies, quantization, and minimizers on compact Riemann surfaces

We study the exponential Green energies associated with a finite point configuration on a Riemann surface. We focus on studying optimal or close-to-optimal configurations, and show that they must be well-spread out on the surface. We study in particular the round sphere and obtain values for the minimal Green energy of a configuration. The first version of this paper was written with the help of ChatGPT.
Compactness and essential norms for two-weight fractional Riesz transforms on curves
Ji Li; Chun-Yen Shen; Chaojie Wen; Brett D. Wick; Liangchuan Wu

We prove a compact two-weight $T1$ theorem for the $α$-fractional Riesz vector, $0\leqα<n$, when one measure is supported on a compact regular $C^{1,\mathrm{Dini}}$ curve $Γ$. The measures may have common point masses. Under the global boundedness assumptions, we give a two-sided estimate for the essential norm in terms of Muckenhoupt and testing constants computed after restricting both measures to small cubes. Compactness is equivalent to the uniform vanishing of these local bounds as the cube side length tends to zero. The smooth truncations have a unique weak operator limit and converge in operator norm in the compact case. For arclength measure and distance power weights, we determine the compactness ranges for Green gradients on bounded tubes and for Newtonian gradients and Biot--Savart fields on the whole space. The whole-space operators in these ranges are compact but are not Hilbert--Schmidt. When $α=n-1$ and both measures have positive continuous arclength densities $a,b$ on the same closed curve, we obtain the exact essential norm $πc_{n-1,n}\max_Γ\sqrt{ab}$.
Affine realization of tilted Richardson varieties

Richardson varieties provide geometric representatives for products of Schubert classes, with stratifications indexed by the subintervals of Bruhat intervals. We construct analogous geometric models for tilted Bruhat intervals for all split connected reductive groups. Our construction uses Richardson varieties in affine flag varieties and yields abstract tilted Richardson varieties whose isomorphism classes, together with their labeled stratifications, are independent of the choices involved. We obtain an explicit formula for the point-counting polynomials of their open parts in terms of increasing minimal weight paths, extending Dyer's formula for Kazhdan--Lusztig $R$-polynomials. Over the real numbers, their totally nonnegative parts are regular CW complexes homeomorphic to closed balls, which gives a natural geometric realization of the posets of tilted Bruhat subintervals in all Lie types. Over the complex numbers, we prove that their fundamental classes push forward under a continuous loop evaluation map to the Poincaré duals of the minimal-degree coefficients of quantum Schubert products.
Uniform Green packing on compact Riemann surfaces

We extend the packing results of Etayo, Hedenmalm, and Ortega-Cerda for complex tori to arbitrary compact Riemann surfaces. The construction uses two different approaches, one based on complex geometry of line bundles, and the other on Laplace designs. Both approaches give the same basic existence of close-to-optimal point configurations on the given surface. This version was written with the help of ChatGPT.
Julien Roger; Sam Bodmer; Jian Qian; Benjamin Riviere

The average-reward setting for reinforcement learning is challenging because its Bellman operator is known to contract in span only when the underlying Markov chain is mixing. Whereas existing work typically assumes a contraction property, e.g., through environment mixing, we consider the setting where we are given a reward-agnostic $m$-step mixing policy, and we control the contraction and exploration properties of the learned policy by regularizing toward the mixing policy. We provide finite-time analysis of $Q$-learning algorithms that can be instantiated with multiple choices of regularization, with guarantees measured with respect to the regularized fixed point. Our framework exposes novel regularizer-dependent objects that control contraction, exploration, and operator bias. In the one-step setting, our rates match the best known rates for $Q$-iteration and synchronous $Q$-learning, and for $m$-step mixing we derive new rates. We also study $Q$-planning variants, and show that planning acts as time-localized learning, where the planning horizon $H$ trades off the bias from the boundary value against the sample complexity. Finally, we present numerical studies validating the analysis: (i) knowledge of a strong mixing policy improves convergence and exploration, and its advantage increases with bottleneck severity and, (ii) our theory predicts the convergence and bias rankings of regularizers from the $α$-divergence family.
Hilbert functions over the exterior algebra and f-vectors in higher rank II: Generalizing Linusson's count to sumsets of f-vectors

Let $E$ be the exterior algebra of an $n$-dimensional vector space over a field, let $F$ be a graded free $E$-module with $r$ generators of degrees $d_1 \le \dots \le d_r$, and let $M$ range over the monomial submodules of Amata and Crupi. The Hilbert function of $F/M$ is a shifted sum of $f$-vectors of simplicial complexes; the companion paper determines the convex hull of such sums, and here we count them. For $r = 1$ the count is Linusson's (1999); we show that no new recursion is needed for general $r$. Using two statistics of an $f$-vector -- its top nonvanishing degree and the initial degree of the corresponding ideal -- we prove that the number of achievable Hilbert functions is a product of $r-1$ transfer matrices, one per generator-degree gap, with entries differences of Linusson's refined counts $E^p(n,k)$. The rank enters only as the length of a matrix product. The same holds for the proper variant. Consequences: a linear recurrence in $r$ for constant gaps, with exact exponential asymptotics $K λ^r$ when the gap is positive; polynomiality in $r$ when all gaps vanish; a threshold beyond which the count is a plain power; and polynomiality in the number of vertices.
A proof of Kahane's conjecture in the Wiener algebra

We prove Kahane's conjecture: if a continuous unimodular function $F$ on the circle satisfies $\|F^n\|_{A(\mathbb{T})}=o(\log|n|)$ as $|n|\to\infty$, $n\in\mathbb{Z}$, then $F(x)=e^{i(mx+b)}$ for some $m\in\mathbb{Z}$ and $b\in\mathbb{R}$. The main step is a logarithmic lower bound for averages: for every nonconstant real-valued $φ\in A(\mathbb{T})$, $\frac{1}{T}\int_a^{a+T}\|e^{itφ}\|_{A(\mathbb{T})}dt \ge c_φ\log T \quad(a\in\mathbb{R},\ T\ge T_φ)$, where $c_φ>0$ and $T_φ>1$ are independent of $a$. The proof uses exact sampling on finite subgroups of the circle, uniformly bounded localized modulations, and the weighted non-harmonic Littlewood inequality of Jaming--Kellay--Saba. A suitable cutoff and a small linear perturbation of the phase ensure that a fixed positive proportion of the coefficients at the beginning of the frequency ordering have modulus one. Passing to integer powers and removing the degree of the circle map yield Kahane's conjecture without any additional smoothness assumptions. We also give equivalent phase, convolution, and operator formulations, and derive consequences for homomorphisms of weighted Wiener algebras and for higher-dimensional tori.
Sharp bounds and extremal structure of minimally strongly $k$-connected digraphs
Junran Yu; Gregory Gutin; Hong-Jian Lai; Xiaoyan Zhang

Let $D$ be a finite simple minimally strongly $k$-connected digraph, where $k\ge 2$, and let $n=|V(D)|$. Mader proved in 1985 that $|A(D)|\le 2k(n-k)$ for all sufficiently large $n$, with equality if and only if $D\cong \overleftrightarrow{K}_{k,n-k}$ (JCTB 1985). We prove that this bound holds whenever $n\ge 3k-1$ and that the order threshold $3k-1$ is best possible. Moreover, if $n\ge 3k$, then equality holds if and only if $D\cong \overleftrightarrow{K}_{k,n-k}$. The threshold $3k$ is also best possible. These results resolve the conjecture of Mader in (JCTB 1985).
Uniqueness and stability for inverse potential scattering with multiple wavenumbers
Dong Qiu; Xiang Xu; Yue Zhao

This paper is concerned with the inverse scattering problem of determining a real-valued potential for the three-dimensional Schrödinger equation from multi-wavenumber data. Under suitable a priori bounds, we establish local increasing stability from near-field Dirichlet data on a fixed sphere for polynomially decaying potentials, and global increasing stability from full far-field amplitudes for exponentially decaying potentials. The stability estimates consist of a noise term and a remainder term, with the latter decreasing as the upper measured wavenumber increases. We also obtain global uniqueness from exact near-field data under weaker regularity assumptions. The analysis combines analytic continuation, weighted resolvent estimates, and half-ray identities whose differences at chord endpoints cancel the unknown exterior contribution.
A Unified Kalman-Type Classification of Controllability for Linear Stochastic Systems

We provide a unified algebraic classification of approximate controllability, approximate null controllability, exact null controllability, and exact controllability for finite-dimensional linear stochastic control systems with constant coefficients and multidimensional Brownian noise. The controls may enter both the drift and the diffusion terms, and the joint diffusion-control matrix may have arbitrary rank. A finite decreasing sequence of subspaces defines a common geometric obstruction. Its vanishing characterizes the two approximate properties and exact null controllability. Exact controllability to arbitrary random targets additionally requires the joint diffusion-control matrix to be surjective. The codimension of the obstruction is given by a rank difference of explicit polynomial block matrices, yielding finite tests in the original coefficients. When the joint diffusion-control matrix is surjective, we obtain a finite Kalman-type full-rank condition for exact controllability. If the obstruction vanishes, a linear state feedback with a deterministic time-dependent gain drives every initial state to zero at any prescribed positive time with finite energy and polynomial small-time cost. An equivalent orthogonal elimination algorithm computes the rank differences with polynomial storage and cost, avoiding exponentially large block matrices. A two-noise example relates the input classification to terminal errors and control energy in penalized stochastic linear-quadratic control problems.

Let $(A,\mathfrak{m})$ be a Noetherian local ring and let $I\subseteq \mathfrak{m}$ be an ideal in $A$. Let $\ell(I)$ be the analytic spread of $I$. Let $G_I(A) = \bigoplus_{n \geq 0}I^n/I^{n+1}$ be the associated graded ring of $I$ and let its depth be $t$. We prove $\text{depth} \ A/I^n \geq t - \ell(I)$ for all $n\geq 1$.
Stable Manifolds and Uniqueness of Parabolic Rays in the Newtonian $N$-Body Problem

We study uniqueness for parabolic motions in the Newtonian $N$-body problem with a prescribed minimal normalized central configuration at infinity. A McGehee compactification identifies their tails with the strong stable manifold of the corresponding outgoing zero-energy equilibrium. The configuration projection of this manifold is locally a smooth graph, yielding a smooth initial-velocity field and uniqueness among all parabolic motions confined to a sufficiently narrow truncated cone, without any minimizing assumption. For parabolic geodesic rays, a renormalized action excess and a quantitative no-exit argument remove the confinement hypothesis when the initial configuration lies sufficiently far inside a smaller cone. We then prove that the set of collision-free initial configurations admitting more than one such ray has Lebesgue measure zero. The global argument propagates the local stable manifold backward, discards critical values of the configuration projections by Sard's theorem, and separates distinct regular branches through an explicit differential formula for their renormalized excess. No nondegeneracy assumption on the prescribed minimal central configuration is required. The proofs combine invariant-manifold theory with direct action comparisons and do not use weak KAM theory, Busemann functions, or the differentiability theory of Hamilton--Jacobi solutions.
Risk-Constrained MPPI Tuning with Update-Aware MA-ES Racing
Morteza Kimiaei; Roya Khalili-Amirabadi; Mohsen Jalaeian-Farimani

We formulate offline tuning of Model Predictive Path Integral (MPPI) controllers as a chance-constrained black-box optimization problem and develop an update-aware framework based on Matrix Adaptation Evolution Strategy (MA-ES). We use statistical information from noisy controller evaluations to determine when the evolutionary update is sufficiently reliable. When the recombination direction is certified, a derivative-free nonmonotone line search (NMLS) is used to refine the candidate solution, and a separate validation stage assesses the final frozen controller. We establish a worst-case arithmetic-complexity bound for both online MPPI control and offline tuning. Numerical experiments on TurtleBot 4, Jackal-like, and Ackermann models show that the proposed NMLS refinement is competitive with standard MA-ES, transfers across the three vehicle models without model-specific retuning, and improves several cost and validation measures. Both MA-ES variants also compare favorably with the tested randomized derivative-free line search (VRBBO) configuration. The results support the practical applicability and transferability of the proposed framework, while not claiming universal superiority or hardware-level safety.
Non-convex integer programming: a deterministic solution method of the large block sale problem

We study a non-convex, nonlinear integer mathematical program with a linear constraint. This problem originates in finance and consists of selling a large predetermined quantity of a financial asset over a fixed time horizon, while maximizing the total proceeds. The selling price is modeled using a deterministic penalty function capturing the market's adverse reaction to the selling flow. From a complexity perspective, the problem is in NP. We first solve the problem exactly using dynamic programming and propose several heuristics that yield tight numerical lower bounds. We then reformulate the problem into an equivalent factorable form and derive a tight convex relaxation using McCormick inequalities. This relaxation is embedded within an adapted Branch & Bound algorithm to find the global optimum in finite time. Numerical experiments show that our methods outperform several widely used generic solvers (LocalSolver, Scip, Baron, Couenne, and Bonmin) for selected instances, but do not yield tight upper bounds, beyond small instances.
Dimensional transition and spectral instability in lattice Hardy inequalities

Discretization can change a sharp stability threshold even when the continuum threshold is recovered at infinity. We study this phenomenon for the Hardy inequality on the integer lattice in dimensions at least three: its best coefficient agrees with the continuum value through dimension eight and is smaller from dimension nine onwards. We characterize this transition by the total critical defect, the summable error obtained by testing the lattice operator against the critical continuum power. A theta-function representation proves that the defect is negative and strictly decreasing from dimension nine; explicit positive Hardy remainders establish its positivity in dimensions three through eight. An exact energy identity relates this defect to the energy saved by optimizing the profile outside the neighbours of the origin. This exterior remains stable in dimensions eight and nine, locating the first loss of positivity in its coupling to those neighbours. We give self-contained proofs of both dimensional ranges. We then describe how local attraction creates a negative eigenvalue in a general class of lattice operators with critical inverse-square tails. Its magnitude is exponentially small near the threshold, with both the rate and the multiplicative prefactor determined by zero-energy solutions. The result allows connected finite modifications of the lattice and nonradial corrections to the tail. The same analysis controls the spread of the emerging state and gives a two-dimensional return scale for the associated Markov chain in every ambient dimension.
Continuous meets discrete: geometry dependence of the performance of iterative solutions for nonsymmetric PDEs in terms of Laplace eigenvalues
F. Francesconi; J. Karátson; B. Lados; J. Rowlett

It is a classical fact in spectral geometry that the eigenvalues of the Dirichlet Laplacian depend continuously on the geometry of the underlying domain, under suitable geometric restrictions. We show that this theoretical property is reflected in a concrete numerical situation: the convergence rate of iterative solvers for convection-diffusion problems remains stable under deformations of the domain. The connection is a superlinear estimate for preconditioned GMRES/GCR in which the relative residual errors are bounded by an explicit expression of the eigenvalues of the Laplacian, or of a symmetric positive elliptic operator in divergence form. We prove that this bound depends continuously on the domain, uniformly in the iteration index, under either regularity hypotheses on the boundary or a topological constraint in dimension two. We also establish corresponding statements on the discrete level. Two examples delimit the theory: domains bounded by a fractal curve, where continuity still holds, and perforated domains, where it fails. The theoretical results, including both examples with rough domains, are confirmed by numerical experiments.
A quantum algorithm for meshless lattice Boltzmann method with unitary interpolation
Chi Zhang; Hefeng Wang; Hua Xiang

We present a mass-weighted meshless formulation for the shifted incompressible lattice Boltzmann method (LBM) whose streaming step is exactly unitary, combining with the Carleman embedding. In traditional meshless LBM, on a scattered node set the semi-Lagrangian streaming step is an interpolation, which is not unitary; a generic block encoding of this matrix therefore requires a normalization proportional to its sparsity and logarithmically many ancillas. To overcome the non-unitarity, we instead express the interpolation as the exponential exp(a Dx + b Dy) of mimetic derivative operators. Endowing each node with its Voronoi mass and applying a mass-weighted similarity transform renders these derivative operators skew-Hermitian by enforcing moment constraints together with low-wave number trigonometric differentiation conditions, so that the interpolation becomes exactly unitary. Such unitarization of interpolation leave the local collision step unchanged up to a rescaling of its quadratic term, where the same weights define the amplitude encoding of the distribution functions. For quasi-uniform node sets, the mass-weighting diagonal remains within a unit-order normalization that degrades only mildly as the Carleman truncation order grows, thereby mitigating the cost of block encoding. Numerical experiments on the Taylor Green vortex confirm that the method reproduces the full meshless LBM, with the velocity error decreasing as the Carleman order increases.
Local coherence and recollement of abelian categories

We study how local coherenAAce of abelian categories behaves under gluing. For AB5 locally finitely presentable abelian categories, we give conditions on the gluing functors under which local coherence is transferred along a gluing $(\mathcal{A}, \mathcal{B}, \mathcal{C})$: from $\mathcal{A}$ and $\mathcal{C}$ to $\mathcal{B}$, and conversely from $\mathcal{B}$ to $\mathcal{A}$ or $\mathcal{C}$. The coherence theorem for augmented homotopes of Bondal and Zhdanovskiy is recovered as a special case, the coherence theorem for trivial extensions of Fossum, Griffith, and Reiten is a companion result in the same direction. We also introduce quasiprojective pairs of adjoint functors and prove a coherence criterion that generalises the criterion of Gomez Pardo and Martinez Hernandez to arbitrary Grothendieck categories. Finally, we extend Stenstr{ö}m's characterisation of coherence via FP-injective modules to compactly assembled Grothendieck categories: such a category is coherently assembled if and only if the class of CM-injective objects, defined through compact morphisms, is closed under filtered colimits. Along the way we revisit the various equivalent conditions for the coherence of a ring, collecting them in a single place. The proofs make use of the compactly assembled categories of Efimov.
Splines and Operators: Part II - Resolution of Inverse Problems

We present a unified treatment of the data-fitting problems with quadratic (Hilbertian) regularization that arise in approximation theory, machine learning, engineering, and statistics. The generic problem is an optimization in the continuum: given $M$ linear measurements of an unknown function, one minimizes a convex data-fidelity term that is penalized by $\|\mathrm{L} f\|^2_{L_2}$, where $\mathrm{L} $ is a differential-like (spline-admissible) operator. The natural domain of the minimization is the native space $\mathcal{H}_\mathrm{L}$ of $\mathrm{L} $ - the largest Hilbert space over which the regularizer remains meaningful - for which we provide a concise and directly usable characterization. Central to our formulation is a measurement-adapted (conditioned) basis that decouples the null-space and spline components of the solution. This basis serves in three places. First, it tightens the formulation of our representer theorem, which confines the unique solution to an $M$-dimensional space without any orthogonality constraint on the coefficients. Second, it streamlines the implementation, as the exact discretization of the problem becomes an unconstrained convex program with closed-form solutions in the least-squares case, which covers ridge regression, Tikhonov regularization, and smoothing splines. Third, it makes the bridge with the minimum-mean-square-error estimation of generalized Gaussian processes, which is the topic of a companion paper.
Ideal filtrations and stabilization in alternating HRS tilting

We prove that the realization functors obtained by alternating forward and backward HRS tilts of any torsion pair over a finite-dimensional algebra are equivalences from some step onward. The number of steps is bounded by the lengths of the indecomposable projective modules. The even hearts define an increasing filtration of ideals contained in a square-zero ideal. For a torsion pair induced by a two-term silting complex, we identify the successive layers with Buan-Zhou kernel ideals and compute them by reduction modulo the successive ideals. We also describe the largest quotient over which the complex becomes tilting and determine the exact stabilization index from the two parity heights. We construct algebras for which the HRS height is arbitrarily large, and compute their ideal filtrations.
Multiple non-collision periodic solutions for second order singular differential systems with parameters

In this paper, new existence and multiplicity results for positive periodic solutions of singular second-order problems under sublinear and superlinear growth assumptions at infinity are established. Two aspects of our results should be highlighted in comparison with the existing literature. On the one hand, they allow for the consideration of systems exhibiting mixed behavior: sublinear in one component and superlinear in another. On the other hand, in the superlinear case, the existence of up to four positive solutions is established, whereas only two were obtained in previous works. Our approach is based on a recently established vectorial version of the Krasnoselskii-Guo fixed point theorem in product spaces.
Splines and Operators: Part I - Admissibility and Native Spaces

The variational theory of splines requires a native space: a Hilbert space over which the regularization energy $\|\mathrm{L} f\|_{L_2}^2$ is well defined and the minimum-energy interpolation problem admits a spline solution. In this paper, we characterize the operators $\mathrm{L}$ that enable the construction of such spaces. Our framework is based on the completion of a space $\mathcal{S}$ of test functions in a controlled Gelfand-triple configuration $\mathcal{S}\subset\mathcal{H}\subset\mathcal{S}'$, which we call a Hilbert-Gelfand space. This departs from the classical reproducing-kernel techniques. Our construction is substantially more general, as it supports arbitrary linear operators and singular behaviors, and it recovers the reproducing-kernel setting as a particular case. It is also complete and canonical: the admissibility conditions on $\mathrm{L}$ are necessary and sufficient, and $\mathrm{L}$ determines its native space as the unique Hilbert-Gelfand space on which it extends to a bounded surjection onto $L_2$. We first show that Hilbert-Gelfand spaces are in one-to-one correspondence with compatible Riesz pairs $(\mathrm{A},\mathrm{A}^{-1})$ of positive-definite operators $\mathcal{S}\to\mathcal{S}'$. We then extend this correspondence to conditional Riesz pairs, where $\mathrm{A}$ is only conditionally positive-definite, which is the scenario that is relevant to splines. The theory identifies the \emph{attainable null space} of the energy as the unique admissible conditioning, realizes the abstract completions as concrete spaces of distributions, and provides a verifiable admissibility condition in terms of a dual energy functional. The framework is illustrated with the fractional Laplacian, which covers polyharmonic and thin-plate splines, and with ordinary differential operators, which cover exponential splines.
A single LU~factorization approach to model reduction for linear system families with a quadratic matrix pencil
Mikhail A. Botchev; Leonid Knizhnerman; Nikolai L. Zamarashkin; Dmitry A. Zheltkov

To solve a family of large linear systems where the system matrix depends on the family parameter quadratically, we propose a new solution approach. Our method employs the derivatives of solutions with respect to the parameter. It turns out that the accumulated solution derivatives of increasing order, evaluated at a single specially chosen parameter value, provide successively better approximations to solution subspaces for the whole linear system family. We show that the derivatives can be computed by a recurrence, involving, at each step, solving a linear system with the same matrix. Constructing an orthonormal basis for the subspace spanned by the derivatives then leads to an efficient solver where just a single (sparse) LU factorization (or a single preconditioner setup in an iterative scheme) suffices to solve the whole linear system family. We call the new method ODB (orthonormal derivative basis method). As shown in numerical tests, compared to conventional solution methods, the ODB method allows to drastically reduce computational costs.
Overlap distributions under the Gibbs measure of a Haar model of $\log|ζ|$ on and near the critical line

We study the Gibbs measure of $H(h) = \Re\sum_{p^{j} \leq X}U_{p}^{j}/(j p^{j(σ+ i h)})$, a random field modeling large values of the log-modulus of the Riemann zeta function on and near the critical line, where the $U_{p}$ are independent and uniformly distributed on the complex unit circle. Writing $t = \log \log T$, the cutoff $X$ and real part $σ$ may vary with $T$ subject to $T^{1/t^Φ} \leq X \leq T^{1/t^ϕ}$ and $0 \leq σ- 1/2 \leq C_σt^Φ/\log T$, for fixed $Φ\geq ϕ> 1/2$ and $C_σ > 0$. On $I_θ = [ - (\log T)^θ,(\log T)^θ]$, define the Gibbs measure $G_{β,σ,T}^{\mathrm{H}}(\mathrm{d}h) := e^{βH(h)}\mathrm{d}h/\int_{I_θ}e^{βH(h')}\mathrm{d}h'$. For every fixed $θ> - 1$ and inverse temperature $β> 0$, the limiting joint distributions of correlations (overlaps) among points sampled from this measure are determined after averaging over the Haar phases. At and below $β_{c}(θ) = 2\sqrt{1 + (θ\vee 0)}$, the limiting two-overlap distribution is concentrated at $q_{0} = |θ\wedge 0|$. Above this threshold, it assigns masses $β_{c}(θ)/β$ and $1 - β_{c}(θ)/β$ to $q_{0}$ and $1$, respectively, and the limiting joint overlap distribution is described by a Poisson-Dirichlet process of parameter $β_{c}(θ)/β$. Approximate Ghirlanda-Guerra identities are shown to hold uniformly for bounded deterministic functions of the sampled positions. Let $Γ\le \mathrm{SL}(d+1,\mathbb R)$ be a torsion-free hyperbolic group dividing a properly and strictly convex domain $Ω\subset \mathbb R\mathrm P^d$, and let $ρ: Γ\to \mathrm{SL}(d+1,\mathbb R)$ be the inclusion. We study representations of $Γ$ into the coaffine group that are deformations of $ρ\oplus 1 \in \mathrm{Hom}(Γ, \mathrm{GL}(d+2,\mathbb R))$ and that lie on the boundary of the locus of projective Anosov representations. In this setting, we identify a canonical limit set $Λ$ for the action and study its fine geometric features which are, in a suitable sense, stable. We prove the existence of an ending lamination that encodes the failure of the Anosov condition and the non-existence of a Cannon--Thurston map. Under certain conditions, we compute the Hausdorff dimension and show that the corresponding measure is positive.
Description Complexity Bounds for Analytic Approximations of Lipschitz Functions

We study how many bits are needed to write down an elementary analytic expression that uniformly approximates a Lipschitz function. Expressions are finite trees over the basis $\{+,-,\times,÷,\exp\}$ with the variables and rational constants, and their size is $\dc(f)$, the length of the shortest description of $f$ in a fixed binary description language. For functions of one variable we prove that every $L$-Lipschitz $F:[0,1]\to[0,1]$ has an everywhere-defined approximant of accuracy $Δ$ with $\dc(f)\le C\,(L/Δ+\lg(1/Δ+2))$ for all $L,Δ>0$, by a linear spline smoothed with logistic ramps in a description language with one repetition construct. We prove a matching lower bound valid for \emph{every} description language: for $Δ\le 1/36$ and every $L>0$ some $L$-Lipschitz function needs at least $\tfrac1{16}(L/Δ+\lg(1/Δ+2))$ bits. Hence the worst-case description complexity is $Θ(L/Δ+\lg(1/Δ+2))$. For functions on $[0,1]^d$ the same method gives $Θ_d\bigl((L/Δ)^d+\lg(1/Δ+2)\bigr)$, using a tensor-product spline whose coefficients are mixed second differences and cost $O(d)$ bits each. Without the repetition construct the upper bounds carry an additional logarithmic factor, whose necessity for plain expression trees is left open. A reference encoder, decoder and evaluator confirm the constructions numerically, and figures and tables report the checks.
Coefficientwise Extremality and Rigidity for Independent Sets in Bipartite Graph Covers

Let $G$ be a finite bipartite graph and let $\widetilde G$ be an $M$-fold cover. We compare independent sets of $\widetilde G$ with those of the trivial cover, consisting of $M$ disjoint copies of $G$, after prescribing how many vertices are selected above each vertex of $G$. A conjecture from 2011, motivated by the Bethe approximation, asserts that the trivial cover maximizes every such count. We prove this for every feasible occupation profile whose active graph has treewidth at most two or is chordal bipartite. Equality holds exactly when the restricted cover is flat, meaning that fibre relabelings make it trivial. For $M\ge2$ and positive feasible occupations, a nonflat cover of a connected bipartite graph of treewidth at most two has a deficit of at least twice the coefficient of $p_G^{M-2}$ with every occupation reduced by one. A holonomy-dependent bound improves the factor to three for odd-order holonomy; both uniform constants are sharp. Comparison and rigidity survive finite compositions along an edge or a vertex, and quantitative bounds from one piece propagate to the whole graph, giving results beyond the two original classes. On any bipartite base, the first nonzero homogeneous defect is determined by the shortest cycles with nontrivial holonomy. At singleton occupations, our counts are numbers of DP-colorings of full covers. The dual DP color function on these classes and their finite seam compositions equals the chromatic polynomial, with equality attained precisely by canonical labelings. Dong's chromatic-polynomial inequality then yields the Dual-DP Shameful inequality on the same graph class. The main theorems have been formalized in Lean 4.
Directional and Quasi-Omnidirectional Indoor Channel Measurements at Upper 6 GHz
Chengsong Fu; Hongbo Zhao; Jianer Zhou; Xiongbin Yu; Weichao Li; Chen Zhuang; Meng Li; Wenquan Feng; Xiaofeng Tao

This paper presents wideband indoor channel measurements and measurement-based statistical modeling of channel parameters in the upper 6 GHz (U6G) band using directional and quasi-omnidirectional antenna pairs. Measurements span 6.425-7.125 GHz at 32 matched positions per configuration in an open hall and an L-shaped corridor. System calibration and frequency-dependent peak-gain normalization retain antenna radiation-pattern weighting. Close-in and floating-intercept models are fitted to line-of-sight (LOS) and non-LOS (NLOS) path loss, respectively. Shadow-fading residuals, RMS delay spread (DS), and equivalent K factors derived from power delay profiles are characterized. LOS exponents range from 1.98 to 2.14. Despite similar attenuation slopes, directional links exhibit smaller LOS residuals and DS and higher equivalent K factors. Hall DS medians are 1.78 and 36.52 ns for directional and quasi-omnidirectional links. Corridor NLOS slopes are -1.12 and 2.54, respectively, while DS ordering varies by position. These results characterize antenna-dependent parameters for U6G indoor channels.
Shape Holomorphy of the Helmholtz Calderón Projector and the Maxwell EFIE on $C^{1,1}$ Surfaces and Screens

We establish the holomorphic dependence of the Helmholtz Calderón projector on closed $C^{1,1}$ surfaces and of the operator associated with the Maxwell electric field integral equation (EFIE) on closed and open surfaces of the same regularity. More precisely, after transporting the boundary integral operators (BIOs) to fixed reference spaces, we prove that the resulting maps admit bounded holomorphic extensions to complex neighborhoods of compact sets of admissible boundary transformations, a property referred to as shape holomorphy. A key step in our proof consists in extending the results in [Lanza de Cristoforis and Rossi, Analytic Methods of Analysis and Differential Equations: AMADE 2006 (2008), pp. 193--220] and [Dalla Riva, Luzzini, and Musolino, Inverse Problems 38 (2022), 055004] from Schauder to fractional Sobolev spaces. For the EFIE, the single layer representation and the surface Piola transformation give the result in Maxwell trace spaces, whereas the result for open surfaces or screens is obtained by introducing suitable restriction and extension by zero operators. As opposed to existing results, we do not rely on an affine-parametric representation of the boundary deformations, thus allowing for more general parametric shape variations. Finally, we establish shape holomorphy of the shape-to-solution map for the EFIE, subject to interior electric Maxwell nonresonance on closed surfaces but with no such condition on screens. Under suitable summability and stability assumptions, these shape holomorphy results provide an analytic basis for the dimension-robust convergence of interpolation and quadrature methods used in computational uncertainty quantification (UQ) of scattering problems with high-dimensional, shape-parametric uncertain geometry.
A Domain-specific adaptation network for elliptic interface problems
Jiaqi Luo; Hongmei Kang; Xingye Yue; Shixin Xu

Deep learning provides a flexible mesh-free framework for solving elliptic interface problems. However, domain-specific neural approaches often rely on separate networks for individual subdomains, causing the model complexity to grow rapidly as the number of subdomains increases. To address this limitation, we propose a Domain-Specific Adaptation Network (DSAN), which combines a shared backbone with lightweight subdomain-specific adapters to provide local represen- representation flexibility without replicating a complete network for each subdomain. We further establish a stability and error analysis showing that the continuous physics-informed residual controls the solution error, and decompose the resulting error into approximation, optimization, and sampling components. Numerical experiments on two- and three-dimensional problems with multiple regular and irregular interfaces demonstrate that DSAN achieves accuracy comparable to or better than fully decomposed multi-network methods while requiring substantially fewer trainable parameters. More- over, the parameter savings become increasingly pronounced as the number of subdomains grows, demonstrating the scalability of the proposed domain-specific adaptation framework.
Are implicit schemes needed in adaptive time stepping for PDEs?

Implicit time integration is the standard way to overcome the tight CFL time step restriction when solving nonstationary PDEs numerically. However, within an adaptive time accurate integration, the time step size selection is governed not only by stability but also by accuracy requirements. Therefore, an eligible question to ask is: is (unconditionally) stable implicit time stepping really needed if the time step is restricted by accuracy considerations anyway? And how much do we then lose (in terms of the time step size) when switching from the expensive implicit time stepping to stabilized explicit schemes? An answer to this question is also important because such a switch is often done when solving large scale nonstationary PDEs on massively parallel computers. This paper attempts to answer these questions by numerical tests for two particular adaptive time accurate settings: (i)~nonstationary convection-diffusion equations and (ii)~nonlinear heat equations.
MSE Minimization for Movable Antenna Enhanced Wireless Sensing via Array Geometry Optimization
Wenrong Chen; Lipeng Zhu; Wenyan Ma; Zhi Chen; Rui Zhang

This paper develops adaptive movable-antenna (MA) array structures to enhance wireless sensing performance under arbitrary SNR conditions, using the AoA estimation MSE as the sensing metric. Due to the presence of strong sidelobes in the ambiguity function of sparse MA arrays, the classical CRB of AoA estimation MSE fails to characterize the true MSE in the low and medium SNR regimes, rendering CRB-optimized antenna position vector designs suboptimal for MA-enabled sensing. We derive a deterministic MSE approximation that captures the local estimation error within the mainlobe of the ambiguity function and the outlier error induced by sidelobes, providing a tractable and accurate optimization objective. We then propose three adaptive MA structures that are tailored to different hardware and computational requirements. For systems with fully independent motors, a movable free array is optimized by a two-stage greedy algorithm, which approaches the performance of the globally optimal exhaustive search but with lower computational complexity. Halving the required motors, a movable nested array fixes the dense inner subarray and adjusts only the outer-subarray spacing, reducing the optimization to a one-dimensional search. As the most hardware-efficient design, a movable twin array is proposed to adjust the inter-subarray spacing only with a single motor, while still achieving significant MSE reduction over fixed array geometries. Numerical results show that the derived approximation closely matches the true MSE compared with existing performance bounds, and that the proposed structures outperform the CRB-optimized designs by orders of magnitude in MSE across the tested low-to-medium SNR range. Moreover, it reveals that in the low-SNR regime, APV reconfiguration is more effective for improving estimation accuracy than simply increasing the number of fixed antennas.
From Cauchy to Gaussian: Sharp Lower Deviations and Ehrhard-Type Inequality
Yong Huang; Shengyu Tang; Sinan Wang

We establish dimension-free, pointwise optimal lower-deviation bounds for convex functions under spherically symmetric Cauchy-type measures. These bounds use either mean-variance normalization or moments about the median, the latter covering the Cauchy case where the mean and variance are unavailable. By approximation with a parametrized family the Cauchy-type measures, our results recover the Gaussian setting of Paouris and Valettas \cite{PaourisValettas18} and strengthen their variance-sensitive estimate to a sharp bound, with a complete equality characterization. This goes beyond the partial improvements obtained in subsequent work. We also prove an Ehrhard-type inequality for arbitrary convex sets under these Cauchy-type measures in every dimension and characterize all equality cases. This resolves a conjecture posed by Byczkowski, Małecki and Żak \cite{ByczkowskiMaleckiZak22}. The proof follows from a variational argument combined with the joint concavity of fiber rearrangement. The geometric inequality reduces distributions of convex observables to one-dimensional convex transforms, yielding the sharp lower-deviation bounds.
Conley Index of Limit Cycles in Filippov Vector Fields
Letícia Cândido; Dahisy Lima; Ketty de Rezende

Within the framework of multivalued dynamical systems, we compute the Conley index for a class of limit cycles in planar Filippov systems. We classify these cycles according to their interaction with the switching manifold, including crossing, sliding, and mixed regimes. Using the Conley index for multivalued admissible maps developed by Mrozek, we construct the appropriate index pairs and determine the corresponding indices for each class. These computations enlarge the class of Filippov invariant sets for which the Conley index is known and extend previous results on low-codimension singularities to periodic dynamics.

Let $A=\mathbb{Q}[t^{\frac{1}{2^n}}:n\geq 0]$ and consider $A[u,u^{-1};σ]$, a skew Laurent polynomial ring, where $σ(t^q)=t^{2q}$. We study the kernel of derived extension of scalars along $ A[u,u^{-1};σ]\longrightarrow\mathbb{Q}[u,u^{-1}], $ the quotient by $\mathfrak{m}A[u,u^{-1};σ]$, with $\mathfrak{m}=(t^{\frac{1}{2^n}}:n\geq 0)$. A finite free resolution of $\mathfrak{m}A[u,u^{-1};σ]$ over $ A[u,u^{-1};σ]\otimes_{\mathbb{Q}} \bigl(A[u,u^{-1};σ]\bigr)^{\mathrm{op}} $ proves smoothness. A specialization inequality for matrix ranks supplies a nonzero exact colimit-preserving functor that vanishes on every compact object, proving failure of compact generation.
Differential operator approach to the $\imath$Howe duality

The iHowe duality for iquantum groups of type AIII/IV was established in \cite{LX22} via two approaches, based on partial flag varieties and quantum coordinate coalgebras respectively. In this paper, we provide a new construction of this iHowe duality via quantum differential operators. Moreover, by deriving explicit action formulas, we prove that our construction coincides with the two constructions given in \cite{LX22}.
Global $C^{2,α}$ estimate for complex Monge--Ampère equations on compact Kähler manifolds
Haozhao Li; Bing Wang; Kai Zheng
In this paper, we prove a global $C^{2,α}$ estimate for the complex Monge--Ampère equation with a positive $C^α$ right-hand side on a compact Kähler manifold.
An unbounded convex set with the fixed point property for nonexpansive mappings

We construct an equivalent norm on $\mathbb{R}\oplus\ell_2$ and a nonempty closed convex unbounded subset having the fixed point property for nonexpansive self-mappings. The ambient renormed space has the fixed point property on bounded closed convex subsets. The main point is a geometric localization estimate at a distinguished point of the unbounded set; the fixed point conclusion then follows from the Kirk--Ray localization theorem.
Stability and Error Estimates with Optimal $\varepsilon$-Dependence for Strang Splitting of the Allen--Cahn Equation
Rongfu Luo; Chaoyu Quan; Zhijun Tan; Yanyao Wu

In this work, long-time Sobolev stability and error estimates with optimal $\varepsilon$-dependence are established for the Strang splitting method applied to the Allen--Cahn equation with periodic boundary conditions. By combining the modified energy dissipation law, and Hölder-Gagliardo-Nirenberg product estimates, the numerical solution is proven to admit uniform-in-time $H^r$-seminorm bounds $\mathcal{O}(\varepsilon^{-r}+1)$, consistent with the corresponding Sobolev bounds of the exact solution. A second-order error estimate $\mathcal{O}(\varepsilon^2τ^2)$ is further established on any prescribed finite time interval, exhibiting quadratic dependence on $\varepsilon$. Numerical experiments are presented to verify the optimal $\varepsilon$-dependence of both the stability and error estimates.
A Countable Three-Generated Orthomodular Lattice with No $σ$-Complete Embedding

We give an explicit countably infinite orthomodular lattice generated by three specified elements and a direct argument that it admits no injective homomorphism into any $σ$-complete orthomodular lattice. In particular, it does not embed into any set-sized complete orthomodular lattice. The source is a generated subalgebra of a cofinite reduced product of finite-dimensional real subspace lattices. A nonzero finite term $a$ is orthogonal to the orbit of a terminal line under every finite word in three Sasaki projections, while another finite term $X$ satisfies $π_aπ_X(t)=a$. If the image of this countable orbit has a supremum in a target orthomodular lattice, Sasaki adjunction forces that supremum to commute with the generator images. This forces the image of $a$ to vanish. The proof imposes no atomicity, modularity, Hilbert representation, cardinality bound on the target, or preservation of source infinitary operations. All target lemmas are derived from the orthomodular axioms.

Gauging fermion parity in a $(2+1)$-dimensional fermionic topological order requires lifting its symmetries to the resulting bosonic theory. We give a direct tensor-categorical proof that, for a slightly degenerate braided fusion category $\mathcal{C}$ and a fixed minimal nondegenerate extension ${\cal E}$, the restriction homomorphism $r\colon\operatorname{Aut}_{\mathrm{LR}}(\mathcal{E})\to \operatorname{Aut}_{\mathrm{LR}}(\mathcal{C})$ on classes of complex-linear locality-respecting (LR) braided autoequivalences is surjective with central kernel $\mathbb{Z}/2$, generated by fermion attachment. Thus each symmetry class has exactly two LR lift classes, related by attaching the fermion to every vortex. We apply graded Morita theory to reduce the kernel to two module types on the vortex sector, corresponding to tensoring with the vacuum or the fermion. We then prove relative rigidity to show that each type determines a unique LR class, which are distinguished by fermionic self-braiding even when their actions on simple-object labels coincide. We prove surjectivity by extending graph algebras in $\mathcal{C}^{\mathrm{rev}}\boxtimes\mathcal{C}$ to Lagrangian algebras in $\mathcal{E}^{\mathrm{rev}}\boxtimes\mathcal{E}$. We proved recently that there are no unconditional Schauder frames of exponentials in the space $L^p(Ω)$, $1 \le p < 2$, for any set $Ω\subset \mathbb{R}^d$ of finite measure. For $p > 2$, we proved that the same holds provided that $Ω$ has nonempty interior, but the general case remained open. In this note we close this gap, i.e., we establish that exponentials cannot form an unconditional Schauder frame in $L^p(Ω)$, $p \ne 2$, without any additional assumptions on the set $Ω$ of finite measure other than measurability.
Oscillatory Integral Operators Along the Paraboloid and Applications

We prove decay estimates for oscillatory integral operators along $(y_1, y_2, y_1^2+y_2^2)$ in the finite field and the continuous settings. In the continuous setting, our result allows a bi-parameter maximal modulation, which extends the one-parameter version previously established by Pierce and Yung. Our approach is different from theirs. Then we discuss three applications of our estimates: a power saving bound for certain pattern finding problem in finite fields, a short approach to $L^p$ boundedness of an one-parameter Pierce--Yung operator, and $L^p$ boundedness of a bi-parameter Pierce--Yung operator.
Parameter-Free Adaptive Extragradient Methods for Generalized-Smooth Variational Inequalities
Zhaoyang Chu; Hongwei Liu; Yakui Huang

Variational inequalities (VIs) provide a unified framework for optimization, saddle-point, equilibrium, and learning problems, where operators need not be globally Lipschitz. The $α$-symmetric generalized-smoothness condition allows local operator variation to grow with the operator norm, but existing extragradient methods often require unknown problem-specific constants. To address this issue, we propose PF-AEG, an explicit, line-search-free extragradient method whose stepsizes use quantities generated during the iterations, without prior knowledge of these constants. Under $p$-quasi-sharpness, we prove full-sequence convergence and last-iterate squared-distance rates: linear convergence for $0<p\le2$ and $\mathcal{O}(k^{-2/(p-2)})$ for $p>2$. The latter matches existing parameter-dependent rates under comparable assumptions, while the linear guarantee extends the previous $p=2$ result to $0<p\le2$.
