To pass from order $n$ to order $n+1$, we introduce a bordering construction that preserves the signed cofactor vectors of both the matrix and its entrywise cube. Iterating this construction yields the result in every order $n\geq10$.
DeepTelecom: A Differentiable Multimodal Framework for Channel Twinning in Dynamic Heterogeneous Wireless Environments
Bohao Wang; Tianen Yuan; William Yen; Zehua Jiang; Chongwen Huang; Li Wei; Chen Zhu; Jiguang He; Hang Zou; Lina Bariah; Brahim Mefgouda; Anis Bara; Yongliang Shen; Zhaoyang Zhang; Merouane Debbah

Large-scale multimodal data are a key enabler for integrating large generative artificial intelligence models into wireless networks. However, existing wireless datasets offer limited support for heterogeneous environments, particularly in terms of reusable high-fidelity scenes, scalable differentiable ray tracing, and synchronized multimodal data. These limitations are more pronounced in mobile and aerial scenarios with time-varying environments and channels. To address these limitations, we propose DeepTelecom, a material-aware, high-fidelity multimodal channel dataset and reproducible generation framework for networks involving unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs) and reconfigurable intelligent surfaces. DeepTelecom refines coarse indoor/outdoor reconstructions and uses a large language model to map segmented surfaces to frequency-dependent electromagnetic parameters, yielding material-aware Level of Detail 3 digital twins. Then, a differentiable GPU-accelerated Sionna ray tracer simulates propagation across the sub-6 GHz/millimeter-wave/sub-terahertz bands, and specifically captures rotor-induced micro-Doppler signatures of stationary or moving UAVs at different pitch angles and translational velocities. The framework synchronously produces channel tensors, coverage maps, transmission videos, multi-view images, and weather-conditioned renderings, and supports differentiable material calibration from sparse channel anchors. The released dataset contains 10 material-aware indoor/outdoor scenes and 50,000 synchronized UAV samples; the framework supports scalable generation of additional data for user-defined scenes and system configurations. In 3D UAV localization, DeepTelecom reduces the 90th-percentile error from 31.05 m to 2.43 m compared with schemes considering only channel state information, demonstrating its significance for artificial-intelligence-enabled wireless systems.
Multiplicity One and van Dijk's Conjecture for Connected Complex Symmetric Spaces

We give new invariant-theoretic proofs of regularity for the three classical residual families DIII, balanced CII, and BDI/Spin. In DIII and balanced CII, trace contractions and a supertrace identity show that the relevant character spaces in the quadratic moment quotient vanish. These quotient-level vanishings lift to the corresponding equivariant tempered-distribution vanishings. In BDI/Spin, Gram matrices and a volume tensor give the analogous vanishing for the two single-determinant characters. We also give a direct proof of the required equivariant-distribution vanishing for EVII. These results, together with corrected distinguished-nilpotent calculations for the nice factors, establish the required componentwise regularity for the finite-component data attached to all irreducible factors and repair gaps in the previously proposed proofs. Combining these factorwise results across products and finite central quotients yields regularity for every symmetric pair of a connected complex reductive group. Generalized Harish-Chandra descent and a compatible Chevalley involution give multiplicity one for irreducible Casselman-Wallach representations in the connected-group case. A finite-component restriction argument extends this multiplicity-one statement to every possibly disconnected complex reductive $G$ whose symmetric space $G/G^θ$ is connected. Consequently, we establish van Dijk's conjecture on the unitary Gelfand property for connected complex symmetric spaces.
Volker Diekert; Anna E. Frid; Silas Natterer; Alexander Thumm

Twisted equations in free groups are equations in which a finite group of symmetries acts on the free group by automorphisms and anti-automorphisms, such as inversion and reversal; moreover, the variables may be subject to rational constraints. Algorithms from the theory of equations in virtually free groups solve such equations in PSPACE, but they are intricate. Our main result is an elementary algorithm for quadratic twisted equations, which extends the algorithm of Comerford and Edmunds (1981) for quadratic equations in free groups to the twisted setting and to rational constraints. Besides deciding solvability in PSPACE and yielding EDT0L descriptions of solution sets, our algorithm computes, for every quadratic expression, finitely many parametric forms describing its values as freely reduced words. As an application, we study the palindrome length of elements of free groups, that is, the least number of palindromes whose product they are. Guided by the parametric forms that our algorithm computes for products of palindromes, we found, and then proved directly, a characterization of the freely reduced words of palindrome length at most $n$ in terms of patterns describing how palindromes are nested by twisted conjugations, thereby confirming a Catalan structure conjectured by the second author. Consequently, these words form a context-free language, and palindrome length is computable in cubic time as well as in LOGCFL, answering a question of Bardakov, Shpilrain, and Tolstykh (2005).
A degree-linear upper bound for the Pólya exponent of forms with fixed arity

Let $P = \sum_ω a_ωx^ω$ be a degree $d$ homogeneous polynomial in $x_0, \dots, x_n$ with real coefficients. Pólya showed that, if $P$ is strictly positive on the standard $n$-simplex, then $(x_0 + \cdots + x_n)^M P$ has strictly positive coefficients for all $M \gg 0$. The least such $M$ is known as the \emph{Pólya exponent} of $P$. de Klerk-Laurent-Parrilo showed that the Pólya exponent is $O(d^2) P^{(0)}_{\max}/λ(P)$, where $P^{(0)}_{\max} := \max_ωa_ω/\binom{d}ω$ and $λ(P)$ is the infimum of $P$ on the standard simplex. Pólya's Positivstellensatz is a consequence of the classical approximation of the multivariate hypergeometric distribution by the multinomial distribution, as was already implicitly known to de Klerk-Laurent-Sun. By applying known estimates of this approximation from probability theory, we obtain a different $O_n(d) L(P)/λ(P)$ upper bound of the Pólya exponent, where $L(P) := \max |a_ω|/\binom{d}ω$. An example shows that $O_n(d)$ is tight.
Survivor Set of Gauss Map with a Hole at $1$

Let $T$ be the Gauss map. For each $α\in [0,1]$, let $E(α)$ be the survivor set consisting of all $x\in [0,1]$ whose orbit $\{T^k(x):k\ge 0\}$ never enters the interval $(α,1]$. We prove that the set-valued function $α\mapsto E(α)$ is increasing and locally constant almost everywhere. Moreover, we explicitly characterize all intervals where the function $α\mapsto E(α)$ remains constant. We also describe the points at which the map $α\mapsto E(α)$ is not locally constant. Further, we obtain the Hausdorff dimension of $E(α)$ for all $α\in [0,1]$. We prove that the function $α\mapsto \dim_H(E(α))$ forms a devil's staircase on $(0,1]$, but is not continuous at $0$. This discontinuity implies that the result of Raith [Acta Math. Univ. Comenian. 63 (1994), 39-53] fails for piecewise monotone interval maps with infinitely many branches. Finally, we give an application quantifying the set of points sharing identical $α$-continued fraction expansion and regular continued fraction expansion.
Domain dependence of Sobolev-curl constants and structure of critical curl-curl solutions
Yong Liu; Jun Wang; Xuan Wang; Wen Yang

This paper investigates intrinsic critical Sobolev-curl constants on bounded domains and the structure of finite-energy solutions to the critical curl-curl equation in R^3. First, for 1< p < 3, we prove that the intrinsic critical p-curl constant on (0, a)\times D is bounded above by a^{p/3} times a Sobolev quotient on D. The proof uses an aligned test field whose optimal curl-free correction vanishes. Consequently, these constants tend to zero along thin convex boxes. For p = 2, we construct explicit convex and nonconvex domains with intrinsic constant below the sharp scalar Sobolev constant. The nonconvex example gives an affirmative answer to the domain-existence question in Problem 5 of Mederski and Szulkin(Arch. Ration. Mech. Anal. 241 (2021), 1815-1842), while the convex example disproves the lower bound stated there for convex domains. Concerning their Problem 2, we obtain an implicit Newtonian representation of finite-energy solutions and exclude two special forms of solutions. These structural results do not yet provide an explicit ground state or an unconditional ground-state decay rate as asked in Problem 2.
Consumption adjustment with mean-reverting risk premia: A singular stochastic control approach
Gugyum Ha; Junkee Jeon; Jehan Oh

We study a two-sided singular stochastic control problem in which changes in consumption carry utility costs and the risk premium follows the mean-reverting Kim-Omberg model. Optimal consumption is reflected between two moving barriers given by thresholds that depend on the current risk premium. These thresholds are the stopping boundaries of a Dynkin game for a two-dimensional diffusion driven by a single Brownian motion. A sharp occupation estimate shows that they are Lipschitz in logarithmic scale, uniformly in the cost of reducing consumption, and that smooth fit holds along the diffusion direction at every contact point. Outside a bounded interval of risk premia and at most two further points, the thresholds are infinitely differentiable. As the reduction cost grows, optimal consumption converges to the ratcheting policy.
UAV SAR Imaging via Diffusion Posterior Sampling under Non-Ideal Motion in ISAC Systems
Keying Zhu; Le Liang; Jie Yang; Fan Liu; Shi Jin

Unmanned aerial vehicle-enabled synthetic aperture radar (SAR) offers significant potential for providing communication services to ground users while sensing the surrounding environment in low-altitude integrated sensing and communication (ISAC) systems. However, its practical deployment is challenged by known non-ULM trajectories and unknown position errors, which violate conventional SAR assumptions and cause severe image defocusing. We address these non-ideal impacts by formulating the ISAC SAR imaging as an exact linear inverse problem to accurately model arbitrary trajectories with multiple-input multiple-output orthogonal frequency division multiplexing waveforms. Based on this formulation, we develop a diffusion posterior sampling (DPS)-based super-resolution SAR framework, where a pre-trained diffusion model provides a data-driven image prior and the exact physical model enforces measurement consistency during posterior inference. The inference process is further accelerated for practical implementation. For unknown position errors, we develop a joint iterative DPS and motion compensation (MoCo) optimization algorithm with discrete cosine transform reparameterization and coarse-to-fine spectral scheduling. Simulations demonstrate that our framework achieves high-accuracy reconstruction across diverse trajectories and remarkable super-resolution, maintaining greater than 21.3 dB peak signal-to-noise ratio (PSNR) even under half physical resolution truncation. Under unknown motion errors, the joint DPS and MoCo algorithm achieves 23.65 dB PSNR with a residual position-error estimation error of 0.19 cm.
Almost tight asymptotic enumeration of finite $p$-groups: Almost all finite groups are $2$-groups of class $2$

Let $f(n)$ denote the number of isomorphism classes of groups of order $n$. We prove, uniformly over all primes $p$, that \[ \log_p f(p^m)=\frac{2}{27}m^3-\frac49m^2+O(m), \] with an absolute implied constant. This improves the classical upper bounds of Sims (\emph{Proc. Lond. Math. Soc.}, 1965) and Newman--Seeley and matches Higman's lower bound (\emph{Proc. Lond. Math. Soc.}, 1960) through the quadratic term. We also prove that \emph{the proportion of $2$-groups of nilpotency class $2$ among all groups of order at most $n$, counted up to isomorphism, tends to $1$ as $n\to\infty$.} These results answer questions~22.3 and~22.19 of Blackburn--Neumann--Venkataraman (\emph{Enumeration of Finite Groups}, 2007). Our proof refines Sims' enumeration framework using graded Lie brackets, constraints on deeper commutator coordinates, and incidence and Fourier estimates for alternating forms. Normalization by changes of generating bases then determines the quadratic term in the upper bound. We also prove that all but a $p^{-Ω(m^2)}$ fraction of groups of order $p^m$ have a central elementary abelian Frattini subgroup. Combining this concentration with the sharp enumeration bound of Bläser--Li--Qiao--Rogovskyy (\emph{arXiv}, 2025) for $p$-groups of Frattini class $2$ yields the linear error term. The same presentation estimates give fixed-quotient extension bounds which, together with Pyber's prescribed-Sylow theorem and the concentration result, establish domination by $2$-groups of nilpotency class $2$.
Characterization of $\mathbb{A}^1$-Milnor numbers of small rank
C-Y. Jean Chan; Thomas Hagedorn; Joel Louwsma; Michael Wijaya

The $\mathbb{A}^1$-Milnor number of a polynomial map is a quadratic enrichment of the classical Milnor number, defined as the local $\mathbb{A}^1$-Brouwer degree of the gradient. We study which elements of the Grothendieck-Witt ring of nondegenerate symmetric bilinear forms arise as $\mathbb{A}^1$-Milnor numbers. Over fields of characteristic not $2$, $3$, or $5$, we show that every element of the Grothendieck-Witt ring of rank at most $7$ that is a local $\mathbb{A}^1$-Brouwer degree is also an $\mathbb{A}^1$-Milnor number. Unlike for local $\mathbb{A}^1$-Brouwer degrees, however, in general not all $\mathbb{A}^1$-Milnor numbers can be obtained from two-variable polynomials. Over an arbitrary field of characteristic not $2$, $3$, $5$, or $7$, we characterize the elements of the Grothendieck-Witt ring of rank at most $8$ that are $\mathbb{A}^1$-Milnor numbers of two-variable polynomials. Over subfields of $\mathbb{R}$, this implies that there are local $\mathbb{A}^1$-Brouwer degrees of ranks $4$, $6$, and $8$ that are not the $\mathbb{A}^1$-Milnor number of a two-variable polynomial. We also prove that under a mild hypothesis one can reduce the number of variables of a polynomial while preserving the $\mathbb{A}^1$-Milnor number up to multiplication by a unit.
A sharp bound for the least signless Laplacian eigenvalue of triangle-free graphs
Dongxiu Cai; Zhengbo Chen; Xiao-Dong Zhang

We prove that every finite simple triangle-free graph $G$ on $n\geq1$ vertices satisfies $q_{\min}(G)\leq7n/50$, where $q_{\min}(G)$ is the least eigenvalue of its signless Laplacian matrix $Q_G=D_G+A_G$, with $D_G$ the diagonal matrix of vertex degrees and $A_G$ the adjacency matrix. The constant is sharp, since the Higman--Sims graph and its balanced blow-ups attain equality, as shown by de Lima, Nikiforov and Oliveira (2016). This proves the bound conjectured by Balogh, Clemen, Lidický, Norin and Volec (2023). The proof uses five test column vectors associated with an ordered edge to obtain a matrix Rayleigh inequality. Our use of local Rayleigh inequalities together with flag-algebra semidefinite programming is inspired by Zhou (2026). We use semidefinite programming and rational approximation to find the required positive semidefinite matrices, and complete the proof by exact correction and verification.

We define a $d$-cube in a graph $G$ to be monophobic in $G$ if, whenever it supports a $d$-face of a discrete singular $d+1$-cube, it must also support another face. In many cases, the presence of such cubes implies the nontriviality of discrete cubical homology and homotopy groups associated with $G$. We describe several large classes of examples and characterize the property completely when $d=2$.
Copula Active Subspaces II: Error Decomposition, A Posteriori Estimation, and Sharpness of the Bounds
Joshua Chen; Peter Jan van Leeuwen

The Copula Active Subspaces (CAS) method of Part I estimates a non-Gaussian observation-noise density $π_{\boldsymbol{n}}$ from residual samples. Its KL divergence $\mathcal{D}_{\mathrm{KL}}(π_{\boldsymbol{n}}\,\|\,\widehatπ_{\boldsymbol{n}})$ admits an exact decomposition into marginal, projection and reduced-density terms and bounds the posterior KL divergence averaged over the true predictive distribution. We derive a priori bounds for these terms, together with estimates or bounds from residual samples. Weighted nearest-neighbour entropy estimates are used for the marginal and reduced-density terms, with asymptotic standard errors in exact rank coordinates. For the projection error, the score is fitted on one subsample, and its mean squared magnitude outside the retained subspace is estimated on the other. Corrections for score and rank-transform errors then give a theoretical upper bound with probability at least $1-δ$. Tests on three known noise laws in dimension $d=20$ use the estimated rank transform. In $11$ of $12$ combinations of example and sample size, the sum of the two estimated terms and the trace bound exceeds the reference divergence after averaging over the estimated models. In these tests, score-estimation error is the largest contribution to looseness. The overestimate from the Gaussian log-Sobolev inequality alone is at most a factor of $1.98$.
When Do Restricted Sumsets Cover a Finite Abelian Group?

For a subset $A$ of a finite abelian group $G$, let $Σ_k(A)$ denote the set of sums of $k$ distinct elements of $A$, and let $Σ(A)=\bigcup_{k\ge1}Σ_k(A)$. The problem of determining when $Σ(A)=G$ goes back to Erdős and Heilbronn. Nguyen and Vu later formulated the corresponding fixed-length question: for a prescribed $k$, when does $Σ_k(A)=G$? For groups of odd order, we prove the sharp large-order threshold $|A|>|G|/3+1$, which forces $Σ_k(A)=G$ throughout the entire middle range $4\le k\le |A|-4$. This determines the limiting thresholds posed by Girard, Griffiths and Hamidoune. If $p$ is the least prime divisor of $|G|$, then, for fixed odd $p$ and sufficiently large $|G|$, the exact threshold $|A|\ge |G|/p+p-1$ forces covering throughout the middle range beginning at $2p-2$. Thus, throughout this range, prescribing the number of summands does not change the sharp covering threshold. For $3\le k\le2p-3$, the restricted and ordinary $k$-fold covering problems have the same asymptotic threshold. As an application to MDS elliptic codes on an elliptic curve $E/\F_q$, we sharpen the half-scale conjecture of Li, Wan and Zhang, obtaining the sharp $1/3$-scale bound when $|E(\F_q)|$ is odd and, more generally, the exact bound determined by the least prime divisor of $|E(\F_q)|$.
The canonical class and Chern character operators on Hilbert schemes of points

Let $X$ be a smooth projective complex surface. We obtain explicit formulas for the Chern character operators on the Hilbert schemes of points $X^{[n]}$ in terms of Nakajima operators, determining in particular the coefficients of the terms involving the canonical class $K_X$ and its square. Consequently, the cohomology ring structure of the Hilbert scheme is determined. As an application, we give an alternative proof of the action of the affine Yangian $Y_{t_1,t_2}(\widehat{\mathfrak{gl}}_1)$ on the cohomological Fock space $\mathbb{H}_X = \bigoplus_{n\geq 0} H^*(X^{[n]},\mathbb{Q})$.
Local Antimagic Chromatic Number of Middle Graph and Direct Product of Graphs
Huimin Xu; Gee-Choon Lau; Ruixue Zhang

An edge labeling of a connected graph $G=(V, E)$ is called a local antimagic labeling if it is a bijection $f: E\rightarrow \{1, 2, \cdots, \left | E \right | \}$ such that for any pair of adjacent vertices $u$ and $v$, $f^{+}(u)\neq f^{+}(v)$ where $f^{+}(x)=\sum f(e)$, with $e$ ranging over all the edges incident to $x$. The local antimagic chromatic number of $G$, denoted $χ_{la}(G)$, is the minimum number of distinct induced vertex labels across all possible local antimagic labelings of $G$. This paper investigates two families of graphs $G(m^{[n]})$ (a graph class constructed by augmenting a bipartite structure $B(m^{[n]})$ with cyclic edges) and $K_{1,s}\times C_n$ (the direct product of a star $K_{1,s}$ and a cycle $C_n$). Under the conditions odd integer $m\ge 1$ and even integer $n\ge 4$, we establish the exact values of $χ_{la}(G(m^{[n]}))$ and $χ_{la}(K_{1,s}\times C_n)$ for various $s$. Furthermore, we characterize several graph families achieving $χ_{la}(G)=2$ or $3$.
Erkao Bao; Tyler Lawson; Cheuk Yu Mak

For an odd prime $p$, we prove a Smith inequality over $\mathbb{F}_p$ for exact Lagrangian Floer homology under a symplectic $\mathbb{Z}_p$-action, assuming an equivariant stable normal trivialization compatible with the Lagrangians and the required relative Pin data. As an application, we obtain a rank inequality between the symplectic Khovanov homology of a $p$-periodic link and that of its quotient. These results extend the involutive localization of Seidel and Smith. The main construction is a stabilized chain complex. At every invariant intersection point we adjoin the Morse complex of a finite-dimensional normal spectral sphere, whose generators lie in free $\mathbb{Z}_p$-orbits. The differential counts holomorphic strips coupled to sphere half-trajectories by a one-sided weighted asymptotic evaluation. We prove transversality, a uniform spectral cutoff, and the compactification and gluing statements needed for the chain identity. The stabilized complex is quasi-isomorphic to the ordinary Floer complex and contains the complex of the fixed data as a subcomplex with free quotient, so the algebraic Smith inequality applies.
Harmonic Reduction of Spin-Coupled Grover Walks on Hypercubes via Quantum Bernoulli Noises

We consider spin-coupled Grover walks on hypercubes within the framework of quantum Bernoulli noises (QBN). We identify parity-dependent harmonic subspaces generated by the central Hamming layers: in even dimension they give a fixed-point subspace, whereas in odd dimension the walk reduces on the harmonic subspace to an explicit eight-dimensional reduced dynamics. Using symmetric-group representation theory, we characterize the corresponding isotypic structure and determine the reduced spectrum. The harmonic reduction also yields explicit long-time probability behavior and shows that the resulting states may occupy an asymptotically vanishing fraction of the hypercube while still spanning its full Hamming diameter.
Memory-Augmented Phase-Field Modeling: Onsager Formulation, Internal-Variable Lifting, and Structure-Preserving Computation
Peng Ding; Qingxia Liu; Zhiping Mao; Zhen Zhang

In this work, we develop a general memory-augmented phase-field (MAPF) framework based on Onsager's variational principle, in which memory effects are incorporated through a general relaxation kernel while preserving the thermodynamic consistency of the underlying system. Rather than treating fractional models as fundamental formulations, we show that they can be interpreted as reduced descriptions associated with specific power-law memory kernels. The proposed MAPF equations provide a unified modeling framework for non-Markovian phase-field dynamics. To facilitate analysis and computation, we further introduce an equivalent internal-variable representation that transforms the original nonlocal-in-time dynamics into an extended Markovian gradient system. This formulation preserves key structural properties, including energy dissipation and mass conservation, and enables the development of efficient structure-preserving numerical schemes. In particular, we construct an energy-stable scalar auxiliary variable approach combined with a fast rank-one implementation that exploits the relaxation-spectrum-induced coupling structure, resulting in a computationally efficient algorithm with reduced storage requirements. The proposed framework establishes a systematic connection between memory-dependent phase-field modeling, internal-variable thermodynamics, and structure-preserving numerical computation. Numerical experiments demonstrate the accuracy, stability, and efficiency of the proposed methods for phase-field dynamics with long-time memory effects.
Sharp Constants and Extremizers in Homogeneous Tree BMO

We develop a finite-tree formalism for sharp inequalities on real-valued, mean-centered $\operatorname{L}^1$-BMO over homogeneous $q$-ary filtrations. A reduction theorem identifies local and global sharp constants with the supremum of finite-depth constants. Finite anchoring gives compact optimization problems and rational extremizers under rational piecewise-linear hypotheses, while stable centering shows that imposing zero root average preserves the supremum over all depths. The principal application is the absolute-value map: we construct centered examples in which taking absolute values increases the BMO seminorm and obtain bounds strictly below the universal factor $2$. Jensen-defect Carleson functionals and martingale-difference envelopes provide further applications, illustrating distinct anchoring mechanisms and the differences between finite-depth rationality, stabilization, and global attainment.
The strong Ramanujan bound for Drinfeld modular forms

The Ramanujan bound states that the degree of the trace of the $\mathfrak{p}$-Hecke operator on a space of weight $k$ Drinfeld cusp forms is at most $d(k-2)/2$, where $\mathfrak{p}$ is a prime of degree $d$ in $\mathbb{F}_q[T]$. We prove the strong Ramanujan bound, which states that at level 1, this bound can be improved to $d(k-(q+1))/2$. In addition, we classify when the strong Ramanujan bound is sharp; surprisingly, this turns out to depend on $\mathfrak{p}$ only through the parity of its degree. We also prove results related to the smallest slope of the Atkin operator and mod $p$ distributions of Frobenius polynomials of Drinfeld modules over finite fields.
Convergence of Least Squares Methods for PDEs on R^d with Shallow ReLU^k Networks
Tong Mao; Lei Shi; Hanfei Zhou

We establish inverse inequalities in Gaussian Sobolev norms for shallow $\mathrm{ReLU}^k$ trial spaces. The estimates identify the sharp regularity threshold and quantify the dependence on parameter separation and bias magnitude. Based on these estimates, we prove convergence of weighted least squares discretizations of linear PDEs on $\mathbb R^d$ using shallow networks with prescribed inner parameters and finitely many residual samples in an expanding ball. Under suitable stability and regularity assumptions, we obtain an error bound of order $h^{k+(d+1)/2-r}δ_\pm^{-(S-r)}$ in the Gaussian Sobolev norm of order $S$, up to logarithmic factors, where $r$ is the PDE order, $h$ is the parameter fill distance, and $δ_\pm$ is the antipodal separation. The convergence results cover deterministic and random sampling and extend to fixed bounded regions by restriction. We construct parameter sets with $δ_\pm\asymp h$, yielding a convergence rate in terms of the network width that matches a lower bound up to logarithmic factors. Numerical experiments support the theoretical results and provide practical guidance on balancing accuracy and stability.
Global existence and convergence of a density heat flow for strictly subcritical Liouville systems
Zetao Cheng; Haoyu Li; Woongbae Park; Lei Zhang

We study a density heat flow associated with normalized Liouville systems on a closed connected Riemannian surface, and we show that this flow leads to the existence of solutions for the corresponding subcritical Liouville systems. The coupling matrix is symmetric and entrywise nonnegative, with no invertibility, irreducibility or inverse-matrix sign assumption. Under the strict subcriticality conditions $8π\sum_{i\in J}ρ_i>\sum_{i,j\in J}a_{ij}ρ_iρ_j$ for every nonempty set of components $J$, every smooth positive initial density of masses $ρ_i>0$ generates a unique global smooth positive solution converging in every $C^m$ norm to a stationary density. The limiting potentials solve the stationary Liouville system. Our proof uses entropy coercivity and a gradient inequality in the density variables, which also yields algebraic or exponential convergence rates.
Signed Quantities and Quadrilaterals: Geometry without Cases

Ordinary angles and unsigned areas discard orientation, and much of the case analysis in plane geometry is the price of that loss. Signed quantities (directed angles, oriented areas and directed distances) keep the signs and so let one argument serve for every configuration. We illustrate this with results that hold uniformly for convex, concave and crossed quadrilaterals: the diagonal area formula, an identity expressing one diagonal in terms of the sides and the other diagonal, a test for a pair of parallel sides, a theorem on equidiagonal quadrilaterals (such a quadrilateral has a pair of equal opposite sides if and only if it has a pair of parallel opposite sides), and a single ratio of directed distances that decides whether the vertices lie on an ellipse, only on hyperbolas, or on a circle.
On the generalization of Christol's theorem to domains of finite type over finite fields

We generalize Christol's theorem---which characterizes algebraic power series over a finite field in terms of automatic coefficient sequences---to completions of domains of finite type over a finite field~$\mathbb{F}_{q}$. Let $A$ be such a domain of dimension~$d$ and $\mathfrak{a}$ an ideal of depth~$d$. In the $\mathfrak{a}$-adic completion $\hat{A}$, choose an $\hat{A}$-regular sequence $\boldsymbol{x}=\{x_{1},\dots,x_{d}\}\subset\hat{\mathfrak{a}}$ and a set of representatives $E$ of $\hat{A}/(\boldsymbol{x})$ that is an $\mathbb{F}_{q}$-vector subspace consisting of algebraic elements. Every element $y\in\hat{A}$ then admits a unique expansion $y=\sum_{u\in\mathbb{N}^{d}}a_{u}x^{u}$ with coefficients $a_{u}\in E$. We prove that $y$ is algebraic over $A$ if and only if the coefficient sequence $\{a_{u}\}_{u\in\mathbb{N}^{d}}$ is $q$-automatic. The proof relies on a careful study of henselizations, which are shown to coincide with the algebraic closures inside the completions under certain conditions. As an application, we obtain a complete characterization of the automaticity of $β$-expansions for formal Laurent series over $\mathbb{F}_{q}$, answering questions posed by Hbaib--Mkaouar and Scheicher--Sirvent.
Symmetric two-level preconditioning for the method of reflections

We develop and analyze a symmetric two-level preconditioner for the method of reflections for Laplace problems in perforated domains. Using constant boundary modes, we define a coarse correction through a symmetric coercive dual formulation. Combining this coarse correction with parallel reflection corrections gives a symmetric positive definite preconditioner for solving the dual system by the conjugate gradient method. Under a geometric separation condition, we prove a condition number bound independent of the number and sizes of the holes and the diameter of the ambient domain. We also derive geometry-dependent convergence estimates for the one-level methods that explain the need for a coarse correction.
Compact localization and co-sobriety of Smyth power spaces

We establish a compact-localization theorem for finite iterates of the Smyth power space. Successive union maps assign to every finite-level Smyth object a canonical least compact saturated carrier in the original space, and co-sobriety at each positive finite level is equivalent to co-sobriety of the corresponding iterates over all compact saturated carriers. Consequently, if every compact saturated subspace of a $T_0$-space $X$ is stably compact---in particular, if every such subspace is Hausdorff---then $\PS^n(X)$ is co-sober for every finite $n\geq 1$. This applies to every $k_1$-Hausdorff space and hence to every Hausdorff or metrizable space. For the first iterate, we also give a direct full-Vietoris argument, independent of stable compactness, which shows that each $k$-irreducible compact saturated family is generated by its union.
Haagerup conformal field theory at central charge eight

We construct a chiral algebra $U$ of central charge eight inside the lattice vertex operator algebra $V_{E_6\oplus A_2}$. It is generated by two commuting affine $\mathfrak{sl}_2$ current algebras at levels $1$ and $39$, the stress tensor of the lattice theory, and a single weight-two field built from three lattice exponentials. We announce that $U$ is strongly rational and completely unitary, and that $Rep(U)$ is equivalent, as a unitary ribbon category, to the Drinfeld center $Z(\mathcal{H}_3)$ of the Haagerup fusion category $\mathcal{H}_3$. Its characters are the $γ=0$ Evans--Gannon vector. From $U$ we obtain a diagonal full CFT, and also a holomorphic $E_8$ extension on which $\mathcal{H}_3$ acts by topological defects.
DS and AMDS Symbol-Pair Codes from Three Families of Simple Root Cyclic Codes
Jiawei He; Zihan Zhang; Xiaoqiang Wang; Zhao Lin

Symbol-pair distances of simple-root cyclic codes are important for evaluating error correction performance under overlapping pair read channels. In this paper, we construct three families of simple-root cyclic codes over finite fields of odd characteristic via generator polynomials. For length \(2q+2\), the minimum symbol-pair distance is \(10\) for every odd prime power \(q\ge 7\), established by excluding invalid support configurations. For length \(4q-4\), when \(q\equiv 3\pmod 4\) and finite field constraints hold, it is \(9\) or \(10\). For length \(2(q-1)\), reciprocal-polynomial analysis shows it is \(11\) or \(12\). All obtained codes are MDS or AMDS symbol-pair codes.
Products of co-sober spaces need not be co-sober

We answer negatively the question whether the product of two co-sober spaces must be co-sober. For a nonempty closed subset $A$ of a $T_1$-space $(X,τ)$, we consider the topology consisting of the co-finite open sets together with the $τ$-open sets disjoint from $A$. We determine its $k$-irreducible compact subsets and derive a criterion that produces two compact co-sober spaces whose product contains a non-singleton $k$-irreducible compact saturated subset of the diagonal. Applying the criterion to a specific Kovář--van Douwen space gives two countable compact Fréchet--Urysohn $T_1$ anti-Hausdorff co-sober spaces whose product is not co-sober. A further construction yields a countable compact Fréchet--Urysohn $T_1$ anti-Hausdorff co-sober space whose square is not co-sober. The failure of product closure also gives an alternative proof of the known non-reflectivity of co-sober spaces in the category of $T_0$-spaces.
Minimax Wasserstein Testing under Differential Privacy
Bonwoo Lee; Ilmun Kim; Cheolwoo Park

We study Wasserstein-$p$ goodness-of-fit and two-sample testing under differential privacy. For general compact metric spaces, we establish upper and lower bounds on the minimax separation radii in terms of covering numbers, matching up to logarithmic factors. On the hypercube $[0,1]^d$, these bounds match up to constant factors for two-sample testing in all dimensions and for goodness-of-fit testing whenever $d\neq 4p$, thereby closing logarithmic gaps in existing non-private results. At the critical case $(d,p)=(4,1)$, we further show that a logarithmic factor is unavoidable by establishing matching minimax bounds for non-private Wasserstein-$1$ goodness-of-fit testing under a bounded-density assumption. Finally, for unbounded domains, we establish minimax-optimal separation rates up to logarithmic factors under an exponential tail condition.

In this work, we focus on deriving the absolute moments of the general ized hyperbolic (GH) distribution via its mean-variance mixture structure. Conditioning on the GIG mixing variable reduces the problem to Gaussian moment calculations and known GIG power moments, avoiding direct integration with Bessel functions. The variance gamma (VG), normal inverse Gaussian (NIG), hyperbolic, Normal, and Student t distributions emerge as natural special or limiting cases of the generalized hyperbolic family. This approach offers a substantially simpler and more transparent derivation, facilitating both implementation and verification.
A framework for spanning forest identities

Identities of spanning forest polynomials can come from determinantal identities such as the classical Dodgson identity. They can also be useful in quantum field theory calculations, particularly the quadratic ones. To better understand the structure of spanning forest polynomial identities, we look at when identities on a given graph are generic for all graphs, we ask about dimensions of spaces of spanning forest identities indexed by certain parameters, and we set up a framework that we hope will be helpful for further progress in these directions. As part of this framework, we identify a family of maps naturally given by the all-minors matrix-tree theorem, and we show that their ranks are counted by the Narayana numbers via explicit construction of bases.
Flat and Ghost dimensions in tensor triangulated categories with a compact tilting generator

Let $\mathcal{T}$ be a tensor triangulated category with a compact tilting generator $M$ and abelian heart $\mathcal{H}_M = M^{\bot_{\neq0}}$. We define a triangulated flat dimension $\mathrm{flatdim}_{\mathcal{T}}X$ for $X\in\mathcal{T}$, and give criteria in terms of tensor vanishing and resolutions by the class of pure quotients of $\mathrm{Add}(M)$. We further introduce $M$-ghost length and $M$-ghost dimension, and show that the global dimension of $\mathcal{H}_M$ controls the $M$-ghost length of all objects in $\mathcal{T}$, and that the $M$-ghost dimension of $\mathcal{T}$ coincides with the weak global dimension of $\mathcal{H}_M$ and the supremum of $\mathrm{flatdim}_{\mathcal{T}}X+\mathrm{inf}X$ of bounded objects, and the relative triangulated dimension of $\mathcal{T}^c$ with respect to $\mathrm{add}(M)$. This extends the classical Hovey-Lockridge theorem, which is recovered for derived categories of rings.
Yang-Mills Theory in the Multisymplectic Framework

This Master's thesis develops and applies the multisymplectic field-theory framework to (pure) Yang-Mills theory. Building from the geometric foundations of jet bundles and the Poincaré-Cartan forms, the work constructs the Lagrangian multisymplectic formalism for first-order field theories, recovering the usual Euler-Lagrange field equations and extending the Poisson brackets of symplectic mechanics to a full graded Lie algebra. It then establishes the Legendre correspondence with the multisymplectic Hamiltonian formalism (in which Hamilton equations are retrieved) including the case of singular Lagrangians (where a constraint algorithm is reproduced). Breaking Lorentz covariance via a Cauchy surface slicing, the thesis then relates the covariant multisymplectic picture to an instantaneous presymplectic (infinite-dimensional) formulation in which the instantaneous De Donder equations and presymplectic brackets are obtained in a compatible way. A comprehensive treatment of symmetries then leads to multisymplectic and instantaneous momentum maps generalizations and to several versions of Noether's theorems. Specializing the formalism to principal-bundle gauge theory, the thesis identifies the multisymplectic configuration space with the bundle of connections, gauge symmetries with symmetries in the multisymplectic language and builds the Yang-Mills Lagrangian. Lastly, among many computations, the standard tensorial Yang-Mills equations and the Bianchi identity in local trivializations are retrieved, Yang-Mills conserved currents and charges are obtained and the graded algebra is derived for a special class of Hamiltonian forms.
A Nullstellensatz for the field of complex Laurent series
Pablo Cubides Kovacsics; Sebastián Uribe Rincón

Let $T$ be the theory of the valued field of complex Laurent series $\mathbb{C}(\!(t)\!)$ in the language of rings expanded by a constant for $t$ and by predicates for $n$-th powers. We introduce a $t$-adic analogue of Kochen's operator, namely $γ(x)=x/(1+tx^{2})$, and the associated Kochen ring $Λ_{L}$ of a field extension $L$ of a model $K$ of $T$. Our main result characterizes the field extensions of $K$ which embed into a model of $T$ (the formally $T$-adic} fields): $L$ is formally $T$-adic if and only if $1/t\notinΛ_{L}$. As an application we prove a Nullstellensatz for $\mathbb{C}(\!(t)\!)$: a polynomial $f\in K[X_{1},\dots,X_{n}]$ vanishes on the zero set of an ideal $I$ if and only if $f^{m}=\sum_{i}ω_{i}f_{i}$ for some $m\geqslant 1$, generators $f_{i}$ of $I$ and coefficients $ω_{i}$ in the ring $Λ_{K(X)}\cdot K[X]$. We derive the resulting correspondence between $R$-ideals and algebraic sets, and we compare natural incarnations of the associated $T$-spectrum: prime ideals, morphisms into models of $T$, and the space of types of $T$.
Error Bounds and a Smoothing Penalty Method for Binary Orthogonal Optimization

Binary orthogonal optimization arises in semantic hashing, orthogonal binary projection, and Hadamard matrix design. Existing methods often handle binarity and orthogonality separately, so their outputs need not satisfy both constraints simultaneously and generally come without a residual-based guarantee of exact feasibility. Using an exact box-constrained reformulation, we establish local and global Lipschitz error bounds and prove that the Lipschitz exponent is optimal. In particular, when the binary orthogonal feasible set is nonempty, any box-constrained matrix whose orthogonality residual is below $1$ admits a feasible sign rounding, and the rounding distance is bounded by this residual. These bounds also yield a globally exact nonsmooth orthogonality-residual penalty over the box and a uniformly sharp local penalty threshold. We further develop a smoothing penalty method for binary orthogonal optimization (SPBO). We prove that every accumulation point is stationary for the limiting nonsmooth penalty problem. Numerical experiments on orthogonal binary projection, supervised hashing, and Hadamard completion show that SPBO substantially reduces orthogonality violations while retaining competitive objective values or retrieval accuracy.
Prior-Informed Generalizable Low-Rank Representation Learning via Regularized Adversarial Reweighting
Keyao Zhan; Junwei Lu; Tianxi Cai

Modern learning problems increasingly leverage data from heterogeneous sources to improve robustness and generalizability under distribution shift, often with high-dimensional parameters admitting low-rank structure. Existing group distributionally robust optimization (group-DRO) approaches optimize against adverse source mixtures, but extending this principle to low-rank matrix estimation with a broad class of losses leads to a challenging nonconvex-concave problem for which methods and theory remain limited. We propose Prior-Informed generalizable Low-rank representation Learning via Adversarial Reweighting (PILLAR), which smooths the group-DRO objective by regularizing adversarial source weights toward a user-specified reference distribution while learning a shared low-rank representation. By tempering extreme adversarial reweighting, PILLAR improves estimation stability and reduces the potential conservativeness of group-DRO. Using Burer-Monteiro factorization, we optimize the nonconvex-concave objective by bifactored gradient descent with mirror ascent. We establish linear convergence to a statistical neighborhood of the population saddle point and derive an error bound that separates low-rank estimation from adversarial reweighting. We further show that PILLAR improves on vanilla group DRO when the latter's excess conservativeness dominates source heterogeneity and prior misspecification. Simulations and an electronic health record study of suicide-attempt risk demonstrate improved worst-source and transported predictive accuracy.
Persistence of conormal analyticity for the Euler equations in the half-space
Benjamin Ingimarson; Igor Kukavica; Marco Sammartino

We prove the persistence of conormal analyticity through the $H^r$ norm, with $r \geq 4$, for the 3D incompressible Euler equations in the half-space $Ω= \mathbb{R}_+^3$. We also establish a lower bound on the radius of conormal analyticity which depends on $\|u\|_{H^r}$ and initial data. In particular, persistence is established in both of the spaces $X_τ^{\rm co}$ and $A_τ^{\rm co}$, the former being based on the conormal operator $Z_k = ϕ^k \partial_3^k$ and the latter being based on $L^k = (ϕ\partial_3)^k$. Finally, we show that the norms $\|\cdot \|_{X_τ^{\rm co}}$ and $\|\cdot \|_{A_τ^{\rm co}}$ are equivalent up to a small loss in radius, the proof of which uses explicit identities relating the two conormal operators.
Harmonic numbers and Lerch functions behind falling factorial generating functions
Hemen Dutta; Gradimir V. Milovanovic; Yilmaz Simsek

We study a family of special numbers and polynomials introduced by Simsek whose exponential generating function has as denominator a falling factorial in the exponential variable. Using the partial fraction decomposition of this denominator, each member of the family is expressed by a single finite sum involving Bernoulli polynomials, Apostol Bernoulli polynomials and two variable Fubini polynomials evaluated at reciprocals of integers. A second expansion, around the point where the denominator vanishes, expresses the same numbers through Stirling numbers of the second kind and generalized harmonic numbers, and yields closed formulas for the first few members. We construct a function, built from the Hurwitz zeta function and Lerch s transcendent, which interpolates the polynomials at the negative integers and gives a closed form of a multiple series recently introduced by Pokaz, Ribicic Penava and Simsek, we give an Euler type integral representation for it, and show that the numbers are signed combinations of moments of geometric random variables. Recurrence relations, asymptotics and an extension to arbitrary distinct nodes are also given.
Two-Species Boltzmann--Kac Kinetics with Matsumoto--Yor Nonlinear Collisions: Conserved Energy and Conic Equilibria

We extend Mark Kac's kinetic framework from single-species Euclidean spaces to a two-species, non-linear interaction space on the open cone $(0, \infty)^2$ governed by the Matsumoto--Yor rational collision involution. We identify a non-linear conserved energy $E(x,y) = x + y + 1/x$ and an invariant conic metric measure $dμ= \frac{dx \, dy}{x(x+y)}$. By establishing a two-species $H$-theorem, we prove that entropy production vanishes if and only if post-collision velocities are statistically independent ($I(U;V)=0$). In contrast to the transform-domain proof of Letac and Wesołowski~\cite{letac2000}, which relies on joint Laplace transforms of general measures, our approach yields a direct physical derivation in state space via the transformation law for logarithmic gradients and separation of variables. This uncouples the functional-differential system to uniquely characterize the Generalized Inverse Gaussian (GIG) and Gamma distributions as the non-equilibrium thermodynamic equilibria.
Controlling The Skips of Arithmetic Sets

Andrews, Ganchev, Kuyper, Lempp, Miller, A.\ Soskova, and M.\ Soskova conjectured that skip-cototality coincides with weak cototality. We show that the conjecture is false by constructing a $Π^0_2$ set whose skip does not have a cototal degree. We further adapt this construction to obtain additional results. We prove that for each odd $n$, there is a $Π^0_{n+1}$ degree whose $n$-iterated skip does not have a cototal degree. We show that there is a $Π^0_2$ degree which does not contain an introenumerable set.
Optimal strong convergence of a splitting mixed finite element method for a stochastic Keller--Segel system

In this work, we develop and analyze a splitting mixed finite element method, combined with a fully implicit Euler time discretization, for a stochastic Keller--Segel system with general polynomial logistic growth and multiplicative noise. The proposed splitting formulation allows the use of standard finite element spaces without requiring the LBB inf--sup condition associated with traditional mixed finite element methods and, at each time step, avoids the need for solving a coupled nonlinear system. We first establish the well-posedness of the variational solution and derive new high-moment, higher-order regularity, and exponential stability estimates. These estimates provide the key analytical foundation for the strong convergence analysis of the numerical method. A principal contribution of this work is the derivation of error estimates directly in full expectation, without the use of localization arguments. By combining the new stability and regularity estimates with a stochastic Gronwall framework, we overcome the difficulties arising from the interaction between the nonlinear chemotactic coupling and the multiplicative noise. As a result, we establish strong convergence in high-moment norms and obtain optimal convergence rates with respect to both the temporal and spatial discretizations. In particular, the proposed method achieves the optimal rates of order $k^{\frac{1}{2}}$ in time and $h$ in space in the relevant $L^2$- and $H^1$-based error norms. These results provide, to our knowledge, the first optimal strong convergence analysis in full expectation for a splitting mixed finite element approximation of this class of stochastic Keller--Segel systems.
Low-Latency LDPC Decoding Based on Consensus and Return Residual Belief Propagation
Allan E. Feitosa; Rodrigo C. de Lamare

We propose two new decoding algorithms for low-density parity-check (LDPC) codes. The Consensus and Return residual belief propagation (C&R-RBP) algorithm reduces the number of iterations required to achieve a target decoding error rate over an AWGN channel by exploiting the availability of updated information, thereby mitigating the performance degradation caused by the greedy behavior of RBP-based algorithms and reducing error propagation. The Consensus and Delayed Return RBP algorithm (C&DR-RBP) achieves better performance in the early decoding iterations than C&R-RBP, making it particularly suitable for low-latency applications. Both proposed methods maintain the same computational complexity as the original RBP algorithm in terms of residual calculations. We also provide a formal analysis showing that the Consensus mechanism increases the probability of correct bit decisions under initial decoding conditions and in the presence of severe bit transmission errors, providing insight into the performance gains observed in the simulations. Numerical results based on the rapidly growing 5G New Radio (NR) standard, considering different code lengths, code rates, and channel models, demonstrate that both methods outperform competing RBP-based algorithms with similar overall computational complexity in terms of frame error rate (FER) and bit error rate (BER).
Deep learning from a control vantage point
Álvaro Rodríguez Abella; João Pedro Silvestre; Bahman Gharesifard; Paulo Tabuada

This article offers an overview of recent developments in deep learning from a control vantage point. It reviews several classes of models including feedforward and residual neural networks, transformers, large-language models, and selective state space models while explaining how control theory plays an important role in understanding their training, properties, or architecture design. The article explains how residual neural networks can be interpreted as the discretization of a continuous-time control system thereby enabling the use of control theoretic techniques for its analysis. To illustrate the power of this bridge between control and deep learning, two technical results are discussed: 1) the ability of a residual neural network to approximate arbitrary continuous functions is a non-standard controllability problem that can be solved using geometric nonlinear control and 2) transformers, the key architectural component of most large language-models, can be seen the discretization of a consensus algorithm and thus large language-models exhibit consensus. Another point of contact between control theory and deep learning is the connection between backpropagation, the algorithm used to train neural networks, and optimal control. The article addresses how the older connection between these problems, established in the 80's using discrete-time models can be reconciled with the more recent approach using continuous-time models. Several open problems and directions for future research are discussed, including selective state-space models, a recent class of models inspired by the models used in control.
Uniqueness and stability of entropy waves among vanishing dissipation limits from the Navier--Stokes--Fourier System
Cooper Faile; Ingrid Lacroix-Violet; Alexis F. Vasseur

In this paper, we establish the stability of general entropy wave solutions of the compressible Euler equations (that is, profiles with constant velocity and pressure) in the class of vanishing dissipation limits from the Navier--Stokes--Fourier system. If the initial data of our sequence of solutions to the Navier--Stokes--Fourier system converges to the initial data of the entropy wave solution, we further have convergence of the solutions to the entropy wave. This gives uniqueness and stability of the entropy wave in this class. The proof is based on the $a$-contraction theory.
Lattices with Large Kissing Number from Local Density
Huck Bennett; Minki Hhan; Zihan Li; Noah Stephens-Davidowitz

Let $κ_p(n)$ denote the maximum kissing number of a lattice $\mathcal{L} \subset \mathbb{R}^n$. We prove that $κ_p(n) \geq 2^{Ω(\sqrt{n})}$ for all $p\ge 1$ and that $κ_p(n) \geq Ω(α_p^n)$ for all $p > 2$, where $α_p > 1$ is a constant depending only on $p$. In particular, our former result improves on the previously best known lower bound of $κ_2(n) \geq 2^{Θ(\log^2 n)}$ for the $\ell_2$ kissing number, which has stood for over $60$ years. (In concurrent and independent work, Laarhoven and Kominers [arXiv, 2026] showed a similar lower bound on $κ_2(n)$ using similar techniques.) In fact, our lower bounds follow from efficient (randomized) constructions of lattices with large kissing number. Our results use a general construction of lattices with large kissing number. Specifically, we show a simple equivalence between such lattices and a new object that we call an exact locally dense lattice. Closely related objects appear throughout the literature on computational lattice problems. Our constructions of lattices with large kissing number then follow as corollaries by showing that constructions due to Bennett and Peikert [RANDOM, 2023] (using Craig lattices) and Aggarwal and Stephens-Davidowitz [STOC, 2018] (using sparsification of $\mathbb{Z}^n$) in fact give exact locally dense lattices, as well as a new construction of exact locally dense lattices built from rotations of the $m$-dimensional checkerboard lattice $D_m$.
The fifteenth cohomology group of moduli spaces of stable curves
Amy Bradford; Aitor Iribar López; Andreas Kretschmer; Hannah Larson

The new framework of semi-tautological extensions has allowed for explicit understanding of low-degree odd cohomology groups of moduli spaces of stable curves. Let $S^*_ω(\overline{\mathcal M}_{g,n}) \subset H^*(\overline{\mathcal M}_{g,n})$ denote the semi-tautological extension generated by $H^{11}(\overline{\mathcal M}_{1,11})$, that is, the smallest system of subrings of $H^*(\overline{\mathcal M}_{g,n})$ containing $H^{11}(\overline{\mathcal M}_{1,11})$ and the tautological subrings, which is also closed under pullbacks along forgetful maps and pushforwards along gluing maps. Recently, it has been shown that $H^{11}(\overline{\mathcal M}_{g,n}) = S^{11}_ω(\overline{\mathcal M}_{g,n})$ and $H^{13}(\overline{\mathcal M}_{g,n}) = S^{13}_ω(\overline{\mathcal M}_{g,n})$ for all $g$ and $n$. Meanwhile, $H^{15}(\overline{\mathcal M}_{1,n}) \neq S_ω^{15}(\overline{\mathcal M}_{1,n})$ for all $n \geq 15$. Nevertheless, we prove that $H^{15}(\overline{\mathcal M}_{2,n}) = S^{15}_ω(\overline{\mathcal M}_{2,n})$ for all $n$. Moreover, we determine all relations in $S_ω^{15}(\overline{\mathcal M}_{g,n})$ for all $g \geq 2$ and give explicit bases for this vector space in terms of decorated graphs. Conditional upon the conjectured dimension of $H^{15}(\overline{\mathcal M}_{3,14})$, we also prove that $H^{15}(\overline{\mathcal M}_{3,n}) = S^{15}_ω(\overline{\mathcal M}_{3,n})$ for all $n$. As an application, we prove $H^*(\overline{\mathcal M}_{g,n}) = RH^*(\overline{\mathcal M}_{g,n})$ for several new small pairs $(g,n)$.
Volume growth and parabolicity for non-symmetric operators
Leandro F. Pessoa; Stefano Pigola; Alberto G. Setti

The interplay between a weighted volume measure and its naturally associated weighted Laplace operator is fundamental to the geometric analysis of weighted structures governed by gradient vector fields. Beyond the gradient setting, however, the theory has remained considerably less developed, largely because this natural correspondence is lost. In this paper, we identify invariant measures as the appropriate framework for extending the theory to general drifted Laplace operators. This approach yields a systematic treatment of parabolicity in the non-gradient setting, reveals its connection with volume growth, and leads to new volume finiteness results for non-gradient geometric structures.
Greedy Coloring and Simple Exponential Strengthenings of Brooks-Type Theorems
Alex Crane; Carl Feghali; Felicia Lucke; Blair D. Sullivan; Madelyn J. Warr

Brooks' Theorem is a foundational result in graph coloring: if a graph is connected, not a clique, and has maximum degree $Δ\geq 3$, then it admits a proper $Δ$-coloring. In this paper, we give a new proof of a much stronger result: every such graph admits exponentially many proper $Δ$-colorings. Exponential lower bounds have been obtained previously by applying the Combinatorial Nullstellensatz. In contrast, our proof is via a surprisingly simple and constructive analysis of a textbook greedy coloring algorithm. The entire argument is accessible to non-specialists. We extend our techniques to provide quantitative lower bounds on the number of colorings in several more general settings, namely $Δ$-length list coloring, degree-length list coloring (degree-choosability), and degenerate partitioning. In the latter setting, one is asked to partition the vertices such that each partite set induces a subgraph of bounded degeneracy. In contrast to the other coloring variants considered, no clean Brooks-type characterization is possible, since it is known that for some combinations of parameters determining the existence of even one valid partition is NP-hard. We give a new reduction which significantly extends the parameter regime for which determining the existence of a valid partition is NP-hard. Finally, we give a new proof of the classic degree-choosability theorem, generalizing the techniques behind a recent proof of Brooks' Theorem.
Transposition Cayley Spectra and Subgraph Counts

Let $G$ be a finite simple graph on the vertex set $[n]$, and let $Γ(G)$ be the Cayley graph of the symmetric group $S_n$ generated by the transpositions corresponding to the edges of $G$. We study the inverse spectral problem for the assignment $G\mapsto Γ(G)$ through the group-algebra operator $A_G=\sum_{\{i,j\}\in E(G)}(ij)$ and its regular spectral moments $M_k(G)=\operatorname{tr}(A_G^k)$. The moments admit two all-order forms: a universal support expansion in non-induced subgraph counts of $G$, and a representation-theoretic expansion over the irreducible representations of $S_n$. We compute the first nontrivial moments through order six. In particular, the fourth moment already contains the Coxeter triangle relation and determines the signed local invariant $6N_{K_3}(G)-N_{P_3}(G)$, rather than $N_{P_3}(G)$ alone. Consequently, for triangle-free graphs the spectrum determines the second moment of the degree sequence. We also give a simplified sixth-moment formula for triangle-free graphs, showing that in this class the spectrum determines $5N_{K_{1,3}}(G)+2N_{P_4}(G)+12N_{C_4}(G)$. Further structural consequences include bipartiteness and spectral symmetry of $Γ(G)$, a precise connectedness test, and the identification of the standard irreducible component with the shifted graph Laplacian $mI-L_G$.
A Sharp Basis-Mass Inequality for Binary Matroids without a Fano Minor

Let $M$ be a binary matroid of rank $r$ with no $F_7$-minor, and let $B_M^\star$ denote the maximum of its basis-generating polynomial over nonnegative weights of total mass $r$. We prove the sharp inequality $B_M^\star\leq 2^r/(r+1)$, with equality holding if and only if the nonloop simplification of $M$ is $M(K_{r+1})$. Binary matroids with no $F_7$-minor also form the largest minor-closed class of matroids on which this inequality holds.
A splitting proximal method in portfolio optimization with entropic value-at-risk
Nail Baloul; Sorin-Mihai Grad; Oleg Wilfer

Motivated by a recent paper where a convex portfolio optimization problem formulated by means of the entropic value-at-risk is solved via a primal-dual interior-point method, we propose an alternative way of dealing with such problems by means of splitting proximal point methods and making use of Lagrange duality. Numerical experiments where the new method is implemented for solving some portfolio optimization problems are presented as well. As byproducts, we also provide formulae for the projection on the epigraph of the weighted Shannon entropy, and the conjugate function and subdifferential of entropic value-at-risk.
The Dialectical Theorem: The future of universities, mathematics departments, and training of human mathematicians

We consider the future of mathematics as a profession in a world where artificial intelligence may surpass human mathematicians in essentially every technical task. Through an informal dialogue, we explore why human mathematical expertise might nevertheless remain valuable, what kinds of expertise universities should cultivate, and how graduate education might adapt. We also discuss the institutional and economic uncertainties that threaten the continued existence of a thriving mathematical profession, even if the value of human mathematical understanding endures.
Juncheng Wei; Zetian Yan; Zikai Ye

We prove sharp improved Sobolev inequalities on $\mathbb S^n$, $n\ge3$, for antipodally even functions and for axially symmetric functions whose critical density $|u|^{2n/(n-2)}$ has zero barycenter. In both cases, the Dirichlet coefficient improves by the optimal factor $2^{-2/n}$, while the coefficient of the $L^2$ term remains one. Equality holds precisely for constant functions. The even case resolves a conjecture of Dolbeault (2021).
On the Depth Transfer of Neural Optimizers via L-Smoothness
Maximilian Wong; Chenyu Xu; Jiajin Li; Yiping Lu

Scaling deep learning models efficiently requires predictable performance transfer across compute regimes. Establishing reliable hyperparameter transfer allows optimal training dynamics and structural choices to be discovered on low-cost proxy models, avoiding catastrophic failures during massive-scale training. Existing depth-transfer analyses are architecture-specific and heuristic: hyperparameter transfer is only justified through toy blocks, and both rely on infinite-depth dynamics, a specific initialization, and feature-learning criteria. Building on $L$-smoothness framework of Xu et al. (2026), we understand hyperparameter transfer as how do the Lipschitz and $L$-smoothness constants of the loss scale with the depth $K$? We show that inverse-depth residual branch scaling $α=Θ(1/K)$ is sufficient to make both constants depth-independent at fixed width, uniformly over the bounded parameter domain and for arbitrary $p\to q$ geometries. Because the bounds depend on each residual branch only through its Lipschitz and smoothness constants, the argument applies to general residual networks (including branches of block depth $\geq 2$ such as transformer and ResNet blocks) without assumptions on initialization or correlations between layer weights. Since the smoothness constant controls the curvature penalty in the descent inequality, our bounds motivate a learning-rate scale without an additional depth-dependent curvature correction for updates bounded in the prescribed norm. This provides a geometric explanation of inverse-depth residual scaling and its application to the operator-norm geometries associated with AdamW, Muon, and MOGA. Learning-rate sweeps on GPT-2 (depths 2--128) and CIFAR-100 ResNets (8--32 residual blocks) confirm that Muon and MOGA exhibit stable learning-rate transfer under these prescriptions, with a common optimal rate across a 64-fold increase in depth.
The Height of Choe's Higher-Dimensional Enneper Surface

We prove that Choe's higher-dimensional Enneper hypersurfaces in $\mathbb R^{n+1}$, $3\le n\le6$, cannot be confined between two parallel hyperplanes, disproving his slab confinement conjecture. We further strengthen this conclusion by determining their precise height growth exponent. If $H(R)$ denotes the maximal absolute height above the asymptotic hyperplane within the horizontal ball of radius $R$, then $H(R)=R^{α_1+o(1)}$ as $R\to\infty$, where $α_1=\frac{\sqrt{(n-2)^2+4λ_1(Ω)}-(n-2)}{2}$, $Ω=S^{n-1}\setminus[0,\infty)^n$, and $λ_1(Ω)$ is the first Dirichlet eigenvalue of the spherical Laplacian. In particular, $0<α_1<1$, so the height is unbounded but grows sublinearly. The proof combines the blow-down behavior of a fundamental piece of Choe's hypersurface with the rigidity of positive harmonic functions on cones. In dimension two, the formula gives $2/3$, recovering the classical Enneper height-growth exponent.
Hölder regularity for metric Anosov flows

We define a class of flows on compact metric spaces that we call \emph{$C^α$ metric Anosov flows}, $0 < α< 1$ or $α= \mathrm{Lip}$. We give verifiable criteria for a metric Anosov flow to be $C^α$. We show that $C^α$ metric Anosov flows have Hölder continuous local product structure, and in particular Hölder continuous holonomies. We deduce that topological conjugacies between $C^α$ metric Anosov flows are automatically Hölder continuous. We show that any $C^α$ metric Anosov flow admits a strong (i.e. Hölder continuous) Markov coding. This yields strong ergodic properties for equilibrium states for Hölder potentials for $C^α$ metric Anosov flows. The regularity of the local product structure is proved in a non-compact setting which applies for the geodesic flow on the universal cover of a locally CAT(-1) space. This allows us to obtain Hölder regularity results for the holonomy maps for pinched negative curvature manifolds with respect to the Sasaki metric. This contrasts with the result of Ballmann, Brin and Burns that there are examples in this class for which the dynamical distributions are not Hölder.
A Bilevel Market Equilibrium Model for Natural Gas Pipeline Network Operations: Convex Relaxations and Single-level Reformulations
Novel Kumar Dey; Afrooz Jalilzadeh; Erfan Yazdandoost Hamedani; Saif R. Kazi; Anatoly Zlotnik

We propose an integrated market equilibrium model for determining the spot market prices and flow rates in a natural gas pipeline network. The traditional approach solves the market equilibrium model separately from the natural gas network flow allocation problem in a sequential manner. Our proposed framework synthesizes marketing and operations by using a bilevel optimization formulation where the market equilibrium model in the upper level is connected and simultaneously solved with the natural gas network flow model in the lower level. We introduce convex relaxations for the nonconvex Weymouth pipe pressure drop equation and a surrogate for the compressor operating cost. Furthermore, we compare multiple single level reformulations of the bilevel problem based on Karush-Kuhn-Tucker (KKT) optimality conditions, Wolfe duality, and Lagrange duality conditions. Numerical studies on a small 6-node network demonstrates the efficacy and accuracy of our model and the comparison between different duality and optimality based reformulations.
STREGO: A Scalable Implementation of a Trust-Region Framework for Noisy Bayesian Optimization
Youssef Diouane; Issmail El Hallaoui; Meisseme Kadri; Amina Lamghari

TREGO, a trust-region Bayesian optimization (BO) method for expensive blackbox problems, has convergence guarantees, but only for exact function values.
